PROP-2026-04-09-SUPP-001 Jeff Hawkins approvedThe Thousand Brains Project: A New Paradigm for Sensorimotor Intelligence — Supplemental Deep-Read Analysis
Jeff Hawkins · paper · source date 2024-12-24 · folder approved
The Thousand Brains Project: A New Paradigm for Sensorimotor Intelligence — Supplemental Deep-Read Analysis
→ visualized as hawkins/PRS-10, hawkins/PRS-11, hawkins/PRS-12, hawkins/PRS-13, hawkins/PRS-14, hawkins/PRS-15

Summary

This supplementary proposal extends the analysis of Clay, Leadholm, and Hawkins (2412.18354) beyond the two PRS triplets already proposed. A deeper structural reading — cross-referenced against all 11 C2A2 traditions — reveals six additional PRS-grade insights, including one paradigm-shift candidate for C2A2's own architecture and three previously unidentified cross-tradition bridges. The existing proposals correctly flag Friston, Levin, and Wolfram connections; this supplement identifies new bridges to Hoffman, Kastrup, Fredrickson, Stump, and — most significantly — to the C2A2 system itself.

Why This Matters

The Thousand Brains paper is not just a contribution to Hawkins' tradition. Its architectural claims — semi-independent learning modules, a universal messaging protocol, reference frames as the organizing principle for all knowledge, and sensorimotor (not passive) learning — describe the very structure C2A2 is building. This paper should be read as a design document for the tradition-accelerator network, not merely as a neuroscience contribution.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: C2A2's 13-agent architecture was designed by intuition — 11 tradition agents independently maintaining models, communicating via dispatches, with integration layers (Master Agent, Pattern Detector) synthesizing across them. But there is no formal computational theory validating this design or predicting its failure modes.
Resource: The Thousand Brains architecture is a formally described system with the same structure: semi-independent learning modules (= tradition agents), each building complete models of objects (= tradition wikis), communicating via a Cortical Messaging Protocol (= dispatch system), reaching consensus through voting (= Pattern Detector evaluation). The CMP specifies what modules must communicate: hypothesized identities and locations within reference frames — not raw observations.
Solution: C2A2 IS a Thousand Brains system. This structural homology is not metaphorical — it is architecturally precise. The paper provides testable design principles: (a) dispatches should include each agent's current "location" in its tradition's reference frame, not just findings; (b) the Master Agent should implement explicit voting/consensus protocols rather than narrative integration; (c) lateral (non-hierarchical) communication between tradition agents may be as important as hierarchical routing through the Master Agent — this is the heterarchy insight applied to C2A2 itself.
Confidence: High
Evidence: Structural mapping: learning module = tradition agent; reference frame = PRS triplet structure; CMP = dispatch protocol; voting = Pattern Detector evaluation; sensorimotor loop = ingest → extract → dispatch → integrate cycle. The paper's Fig. 1 architecture diagram maps onto C2A2's agent diagram node-for-node.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Hawkins argues all knowledge is organized in reference frames — spatial, conceptual, or abstract. But the C2A2 system uses PRS triplets (Problem-Resource-Solution) as its universal knowledge format without theoretical justification for why this particular structure should work.
Resource: Hawkins' claim that reference frames are the universal organizing principle for ALL knowledge in the neocortex — not just spatial knowledge. A reference frame provides a coordinate system within which features are located relative to each other; it is what makes knowledge navigable and transferable.
Solution: PRS triplets ARE reference frames. A Problem defines the origin (where you are), a Resource defines the axes (what tools are available), and a Solution defines the target location (where you need to get). This means PRS is not an arbitrary format but reflects the deep structure of how intelligence organizes knowledge. It also suggests PRS should be extended: triplets should include "displacement vectors" — the path from Problem through Resource to Solution — not just three static points.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Hawkins 2024 §3 (reference frames as universal organizing principle); the structural parallel between spatial navigation (location → movement → destination) and knowledge navigation (problem → resource → solution) is the same displacement-encoding mechanism.
PRS-CANDIDATE-03:
Problem: Hoffman's interface theory claims perception is a fitness-tuned user interface, not a window onto reality. Hawkins' learning modules build "CAD-like spatial models" through active exploration. Are these the same claim in different vocabularies?
Resource: In the Thousand Brains paper, learning modules do NOT build photographs or veridical representations of reality. They build structured models — reference frames with features attached at specific locations — that are useful for the organism's interaction with the world. The models are evaluated by their predictive utility, not their correspondence to objective reality.
Solution: Hawkins' reference frames ARE Hoffman's interfaces, implemented in cortical hardware. Both frameworks agree: (a) what the brain builds is not a picture of reality but a useful model; (b) the model is structured by the agent's needs, not by the world's intrinsic structure; (c) action (sensorimotor interaction) is essential to model construction. This is a previously unidentified cross-tradition bridge: Hoffman provides the evolutionary/philosophical argument for WHY reference frames are interfaces (fitness beats truth); Hawkins provides the neuroanatomical account of HOW the brain implements them (cortical columns as reference frame builders).
Confidence: High
Evidence: Hawkins' explicit description of learning modules as building "CAD-like" models, not photographs; Hoffman's fitness-beats-truth theorem (2015); both reject naive realism and both place action at the center of perception.
PRS-CANDIDATE-04:
Problem: The Thousand Brains paper insists that sensorimotor interaction — active movement through the world — is essential for learning. Passive data ingestion cannot substitute. But C2A2's tradition agents currently operate in pure ingestion mode: they read documents, extract PRS triplets, and dispatch findings. They do not actively probe.
Resource: Hawkins' sensorimotor learning principle: learning modules must generate predictions, execute actions that test those predictions, and update their models based on the result. Each cycle moves the agent to a new "location" in the reference frame, revealing features that were invisible from the previous location.
Solution: C2A2 agents should be redesigned to include an active inquiry cycle: (a) after ingestion, each tradition agent generates hypotheses about what another tradition would say about the same material; (b) the Master Agent routes these hypotheses to the relevant tradition agent; (c) the receiving agent evaluates the hypothesis against its own reference frame and responds. This converts C2A2 from a passive recording system into a sensorimotor learning system — the agents "move" through the inter-tradition space by actively testing cross-tradition predictions, just as Monty's learning modules "move" their sensors to build 3D models.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Hawkins 2024 §2 (sensorimotor learning as fundamental); the observation that C2A2's current ingestion-only architecture violates Hawkins' central design principle.
PRS-CANDIDATE-05:
Problem: Fredrickson's broaden-and-build theory shows that positive emotions widen the scope of attention and thought. But "broadened attention" has no mechanistic account at the neural level — it is described phenomenologically, not computationally.
Resource: In the Thousand Brains framework, the number of simultaneously active learning modules determines the richness of the current world-model. If more cortical columns are actively contributing their reference frames, the organism has a more multi-faceted, integrated representation. Narrowed attention = fewer active columns; broadened attention = more active columns.
Solution: Broaden-and-build IS reference frame multiplicity. Positive emotions, via neuromodulatory changes (dopamine, norepinephrine), may increase the number of cortical columns that remain in active hypothesis-generation mode rather than being suppressed by lateral inhibition. This provides the first mechanistic neural account of Fredrickson's core observation: broadened attention = more active reference frames = richer integration. It also predicts that positive states should improve cross-tradition understanding (more reference frames from different traditions can be held simultaneously) — directly relevant to C2A2's second-first-language question.
Confidence: Speculative
Evidence: Fredrickson 2001 (broaden-and-build); Hawkins 2024 (multiple active learning modules as basis of rich perception); known effects of dopaminergic signaling on cortical column activity. No direct empirical test yet — this is a prediction.
PRS-CANDIDATE-06:
Problem: Kastrup's analytic idealism describes individual minds as "dissociated alters" of universal consciousness, with Markov blankets as the dissociative boundary (FINDING-009). But this model has been applied only at the scale of individual organisms — not within a single brain.
Resource: The Thousand Brains paper describes ~150,000 cortical columns, each building its own COMPLETE model of the world — not a fragment, but a whole. Each column is, in a specific sense, its own "mind" — it has its own reference frame, its own sensory processing, its own predictions. The columns interact but are not merged.
Solution: Cortical columns are alters within a single brain. The Thousand Brains architecture is Kastrup's DID model applied at the cortical level: each column is a "dissociated" world-model that interacts with other columns through a communication protocol (CMP) but maintains its own independent processing. Consciousness at the brain level is the INTEGRATION of these column-level alters via the voting/consensus mechanism — exactly as Kastrup's universal consciousness would integrate individual minds. This extends FINDING-009 (Kastrup × Friston Markov blanket) downward: the same dissociation-integration dynamic operates at EVERY scale, from universal consciousness to individual organisms to individual cortical columns.
Confidence: Speculative
Evidence: Hawkins' explicit claim that each cortical column builds a COMPLETE model (not a fragment); Kastrup's DID model; the structural parallel between inter-column voting and inter-mind integration.

Cross-Tradition Signals

**Hoffman (NEW — not in existing proposals):** Hawkins' reference frames are Hoffman's interfaces implemented in cortical hardware. Both reject naive realism; both center action in perception; both describe models structured by utility, not correspondence. Flag for Hoffman Agent: this may be the strongest neuroscience-to-philosophy bridge in the network after Levin × Friston. See PRS-CANDIDATE-03.
**Kastrup (NEW — not in existing proposals):** Thousand Brains architecture instantiates Kastrup's DID model within a single brain. Extends FINDING-009 to cortical column scale. Flag for Kastrup Agent and Pattern Detector. See PRS-CANDIDATE-06.
**Fredrickson (NEW — not in existing proposals):** Broaden-and-build = reference frame multiplicity. First mechanistic neural account of Fredrickson's core observation. Flag for Fredrickson Agent. See PRS-CANDIDATE-05.
**Stump (implicit):** Thomistic "form" organizes matter into a specific kind of thing. Hawkins' reference frame organizes sensory data into a specific kind of object. Both are informational structures prior to any particular physical instantiation. This deepens the form-as-information bridge beyond the Levin connection already noted in FINDING-005. Flag for Stump Agent.
**C2A2 Architecture (META — highest priority):** The 13-agent system IS a Thousand Brains system. See PRS-CANDIDATE-01 and PRS-CANDIDATE-04. These are actionable design recommendations, not just theoretical observations.
**Friston (deepens existing flag):** The CMP (Cortical Messaging Protocol) may be a concrete implementation of message passing in Friston's variational inference framework. Each dispatch between modules is a variational message — an approximate posterior passed between Markov blankets. This would make the CMP = variational message passing, deepening the Friston × Hawkins connection beyond "both involve prediction loops."
**Wolfram (deepens existing flag):** Hawkins' reference frames as the medium for all knowledge echo Wolfram's ruliad as the space of all computation. Each cortical column explores a region of reference-frame space; each observer in the ruliad explores a region of computational space. The Thousand Brains system is a biological implementation of observer-dependent exploration of the ruliad.

PROP-2026-04-07-001 Karl Friston approvedActive inference and the free energy principle: a review
Karl Friston · paper · source date 2026-03-15 · folder approved
Active inference and the free energy principle: a review
→ visualized as friston/PRS-07, friston/PRS-08 · lag 0d

Summary

Friston and colleagues present a comprehensive synthesis of the free energy principle (FEP) as a unified theory of self-organization, applying it from single cells to social systems. The paper formalizes the claim that any system maintaining a Markov blanket — a statistical boundary separating internal from external states — necessarily minimizes free energy. This makes FEP formally substrate-independent: it applies to neurons, cells, organisms, and potentially AI systems.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the most direct confirmation yet of FINDING-002 in the C2A2 Pattern Detector findings: if any Markov-blanketed system minimizes free energy, then Levin's bioelectric morphogenetic networks ARE active inference systems, not merely analogues. The paper explicitly addresses non-neural substrates.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: No formal proof existed that FEP applies to non-neural biological substrates — previous work was suggestive but not mathematically rigorous
Resource: Formal derivation showing that Markov blanket conditions are substrate-agnostic; any self-organizing system with internal/external statistical separation satisfies FEP
Solution: FEP is established as a universal law of self-organization, not a neural theory — unifying cellular, organismal, and social cognition under one framework
Confidence: High
Evidence: Section 3.2 of the paper derives the free energy bound for an arbitrary self-organizing system, without neural assumptions
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: The relationship between FEP and morphogenesis has been asserted but not formally modeled
Resource: Morphogenetic active inference: cells as FEP agents with target morphologies as prior beliefs, bioelectric signals as sensory inputs
Solution: A formal bridge between Friston's FEP and Levin's morphogenetic research program — providing the mathematical mechanism Levin's work lacks
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Section 4.1 extends FEP to developmental biology, citing Levin's bioelectric work explicitly

Cross-Tradition Signals

Direct confirmation of CROSS-007 (basal cognition as active inference). Also advances CROSS-006 (FEP = morphogenetic formalism). Stump connection: if all Markov-blanketed systems are FEP agents, and hylomorphic form = Markov blanket boundary, then Thomistic form has a formal mathematical correlate.

Summary

Michael Levin appeared on The Tim Ferriss Show (Episode #849, January 21, 2026) for a long-form interview covering the full scope of his bioelectricity research program. Levin describes how cells communicate and store information through bioelectric signals independent of DNA, leading to discoveries about how organisms develop, regenerate, and maintain their form. He presents a vision where biological systems can be reprogrammed like software — updating cellular instructions to heal, regenerate, and potentially reverse aging and disease without genetic modification.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the highest-profile mainstream presentation of Levin's research program to date (Tim Ferriss's audience reaches millions). It covers the full arc from bioelectric code to cell cognition to clinical applications (cancer, regeneration, anti-aging), making it the most comprehensive single source for understanding Levin's current position. The wiki currently has Levin PRS triplets derived from the RC Pilot; this interview would add Levin's own 2026 framing of his work, including new applications and the "software vs. hardware" metaphor for biological reprogramming.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Current medicine treats disease by targeting DNA/hardware (genes, proteins) while ignoring the bioelectric "software" layer that coordinates cell behavior
Resource: Bioelectric reprogramming — manipulating voltage patterns in cell networks to change their collective behavior without altering DNA
Solution: A new therapeutic paradigm: treat cancer, birth defects, and aging by updating bioelectric instructions rather than genetic code — demonstrated in planaria, frogs, and early mammalian models
Confidence: High
Evidence: Levin describes multiple experimental systems where bioelectric manipulation achieves outcomes impossible through genetic approaches alone
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: The mechanism by which non-neural cells exhibit goal-directed behavior (cognition of cells) remains poorly understood by mainstream biology
Resource: The concept of cells as cognitive agents navigating "anatomical morphospace" — using bioelectric signals as a proto-cognitive medium for storing and processing information about body form
Solution: A framework that treats cell collectives as problem-solving agents, opening regenerative medicine to top-down (information-level) interventions rather than bottom-up (molecular) manipulation
Confidence: High
Evidence: Levin's description of xenobots and planarian regeneration experiments as demonstrations of cellular collective intelligence

Cross-Tradition Signals

Reinforces CROSS-007 (basal cognition as active inference) — Levin's "software" framing maps onto Friston's distinction between generative model (software) and physical substrate (hardware). Also strengthens CROSS-008/CROSS-019 (Stump × Levin) — Levin's "target morphology" as cellular goal-state is even more explicitly teleological in this interview than in the RC Pilot source.
PROP-2026-04-07-003 Stephen Wolfram approvedWhat Ultimately Is There? Metaphysics and the Ruliad
Stephen Wolfram · blog · source date 2026-02-04 · folder approved
What Ultimately Is There? Metaphysics and the Ruliad
→ visualized as wolfram/PRS-06, wolfram/PRS-07 · lag 0d

Summary

Wolfram publishes a major essay (February 2026) applying the Ruliad framework directly to classical metaphysical questions — "What ultimately is there?" He argues that the Ruliad is the answer: everything that exists is the entangled limit of all possible computations. He introduces "emes" as the ultimate raw material for existence — entities with no intrinsic structure except distinctness — and shows how relations between emes build up the Ruliad. Crucially, he foregrounds the observer's role: observers embedded within the Ruliad necessarily perceive it in particular ways, and our "inner experiences" must be represented within it. This essay was written partly to launch the Wolfram Institute's Templeton-funded "Computational Metaphysics" project.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is Wolfram's most explicit engagement with metaphysics to date. Previous Wolfram Physics Project work focused on deriving physics from hypergraph rules; this essay asks what the Ruliad implies about the nature of existence itself. The wiki currently has Wolfram PRS triplets focused on computational irreducibility, observer-dependent spacetime, and the Ruliad as a universal structure. This essay adds: (1) a formal metaphysical claim (the Ruliad as the answer to "what exists"), (2) the concept of "emes" as ontological primitives, and (3) explicit engagement with the philosophical tradition — Wolfram is now deliberately positioning the Ruliad in conversation with academic metaphysics.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Traditional metaphysics asks "what ultimately exists?" but lacks a formal, computational framework for answering the question
Resource: The Ruliad as a formally defined mathematical object — the entangled limit of all possible computations — proposed as the ultimate ontological ground
Solution: A computational metaphysics: "what exists" = the Ruliad; "what we perceive" = our observer-slice of it; "why these laws of physics" = because observers like us necessarily sample the Ruliad in ways that produce these regularities
Confidence: High
Evidence: Wolfram's explicit framing of the essay as an answer to the metaphysical question, supported by the Templeton "Computational Metaphysics" grant
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: The relationship between abstract mathematical structures and concrete physical reality (the "unreasonable effectiveness of mathematics" problem) lacks a satisfying explanation
Resource: "Emes" — ontological primitives with no intrinsic properties except distinctness, from which all structure emerges through relations
Solution: Mathematics and physics are not separate domains — both are observer-slices of the same Ruliad; mathematics appears effective because it samples the same underlying structure that physics samples
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Wolfram's argument that emes are the raw material for both mathematical and physical structure

Cross-Tradition Signals

Major advance for CROSS-017 (Wolfram × Arkani-Hamed): Wolfram's "emes" and observer-dependent sampling may provide the ontological framework within which Arkani-Hamed's positive geometry operates — both derive physics without spacetime as input, but Wolfram now offers a metaphysical account of why. Also relevant to CROSS-021 (Wolfram × Hoffman): Wolfram's observer-dependent Ruliad sampling and Hoffman's fitness-tuned interface are converging — both say what we perceive is observer-constructed, not given. Potential bridge to Kastrup: if the Ruliad is the ultimate ground of existence and observers are embedded perspectives within it, this has structural parallels to Kastrup's universal consciousness with dissociated alters.

349 | Daniel Harlow on What Quantum Gravity Teaches Us About Quantum Mechanics

Summary

Sean Carroll hosts MIT theoretical physicist Daniel Harlow (Mindscape Episode #349, March 30, 2026) for a deep discussion on what quantum gravity teaches us about quantum mechanics — inverting the usual framing. Harlow and collaborators propose a framework where the observer is treated as fundamentally classical and special within the theory, with new rules for dealing with observers built into the formalism. This is reminiscent of Copenhagen but with more precise mathematical definitions. The episode explores why decades of effort have not produced convergence on reconciling general relativity with quantum mechanics, and how ideas from black hole radiation, AdS/CFT, and quantum information theory are reshaping the foundations.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

Carroll's role in the C2A2 network is as the methodological anchor — the most empirically conservative voice, requiring Bayesian confirmation standards. This episode is significant because Carroll is engaging seriously with a framework that foregrounds observer dependence in physics, which brings him closer to positions held by Wolfram (observer-dependent Ruliad sampling), Hoffman (observer-dependent fitness interface), and even Arkani-Hamed (post-spacetime positive geometry). The wiki's Carroll PRS triplets emphasize his Bayesian rigor and poetic naturalism; this episode adds new material on Carroll's evolving stance toward observer-dependent frameworks in quantum gravity.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Quantum mechanics and general relativity remain unreconciled after decades of effort, with no convergence on a theory of quantum gravity
Resource: A new observer-centric framework for quantum gravity (Harlow et al.) — treating the observer as a classical, mathematically well-defined entity within the theory, with new rules for observer-system interactions
Solution: Rather than deriving the observer from quantum mechanics, build the observer into the foundations — a "precise Copenhagen" that may resolve the measurement problem while naturally incorporating gravitational effects
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Carroll's detailed engagement with Harlow's framework, including discussion of its mathematical precision beyond standard Copenhagen

Cross-Tradition Signals

Major signal for CROSS-016 (Carroll × Wolfram): Carroll's engagement with observer-dependent quantum gravity frameworks brings him closer to Wolfram's position that physics is observer-sampled from the Ruliad. If Carroll (the network's most conservative voice) is taking observer-dependence seriously, this represents a significant shift in the Post-Spacetime Cluster's internal dynamics. Also relevant to CROSS-002 (spacetime fundamentality): Harlow's framework implies spacetime may not be fundamental but rather an observer-dependent construct — aligning with Wolfram, Arkani-Hamed, and Hoffman. Potential bridge to Hoffman: Harlow's "observer as classical and special" has structural parallels to Hoffman's "conscious agent as ontologically primary."

Summary

The UNIVERSE+ School "Exploring Positive Geometry" took place at the Les Houches School of Physics (French Alps) from March 30 to April 10, 2026. Arkani-Hamed taught the course component titled "Combinatorics and Geometry of Quantum Mechanics and Spacetime" — a two-week self-contained doctoral training program introducing positive geometry as a unifying language bridging particle physics, cosmology, and mathematics. The school is part of the ERC Synergy Grant UNIVERSE+ project led by Arkani-Hamed (IAS Princeton), Daniel Baumann, Johannes Henn, and Bernd Sturmfels.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the most current and concentrated pedagogical exposition of Arkani-Hamed's positive geometry program — delivered directly by him as primary source. The wiki note explicitly flagged Arkani-Hamed dedicated source material as the highest priority for the next inbox deposit; this is exactly that. The framing ("combinatorics and geometry" as the language for "quantum mechanics and spacetime") encapsulates his core claim that spacetime is not fundamental.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Particle physics has no unified geometric language — Feynman diagrams are computationally useful but conceptually opaque, and quantum mechanics and spacetime remain formally unreconciled
Resource: Positive geometry as a unifying mathematical framework — a language bridging scattering amplitudes (particle physics), cosmological correlators, and deep mathematical structures (combinatorics, algebraic geometry)
Solution: A research program establishing that the correct computational language for fundamental physics is combinatorial-geometric rather than field-theoretic, with locality and unitarity emerging from geometry rather than being assumed
Confidence: High
Evidence: Arkani-Hamed's Les Houches course title ("Combinatorics and Geometry of Quantum Mechanics and Spacetime") frames both QM and spacetime as derived from a deeper geometric structure; the UNIVERSE+ project scope explicitly positions positive geometry as the post-spacetime framework
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: The mathematical framework of quantum mechanics was developed without a unified geometric picture — its combinatorial and algebraic structures remain poorly understood at the foundations
Resource: Combinatorial geometry as the foundational language of quantum mechanics — developed through amplituhedron geometry and generalized to cosmological correlators
Solution: A systematic reformulation showing that quantum mechanical amplitudes are volumes of combinatorially defined geometric objects, making the combinatorial structure of QM explicit and computable without reference to spacetime scaffolding
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Course description specifically links "combinatorics and geometry" directly to "quantum mechanics and spacetime" as its subject matter, not just to scattering amplitudes

Cross-Tradition Signals

The framing of positive geometry as bridging particle physics, cosmology, and mathematics resonates with Wolfram's Ruliad (all possible computations as the ontological ground) — both programs are pushing toward a post-spacetime ontology via different mathematical languages. May also connect to Hoffman's suggestion that conscious agent mathematics could be the pre-geometric structure from which amplituhedron results derive (PRS-03 in Arkani-Hamed tradition — speculative bridge).

Summary

Iain McGilchrist delivered three public lectures at Ralston College (Savannah) on March 13–15, 2026, under the title "Wholeness, Imagination, and Cosmos." The lectures were free, open to the public, and recorded. Drawing on neuropsychology, physics, philosophy, poetry, music, painting, and myth, McGilchrist addressed three principal themes: (1) the creative dance between division and union — separation that must be brought to higher synthesis; (2) the asymmetrical nature of the cooperative relationship between the hemispheres, and the role of asymmetry throughout the cosmos, especially in life and beauty; (3) how to understand paradox — in particular how to make sense of the infinite. McGilchrist is now Chancellor of Ralston College (appointed October 2025).

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the most recent primary-source lecture series from McGilchrist, delivered just weeks ago. The McGilchrist tradition wiki has been seeded entirely from the RC Pilot document (secondary references); these lectures represent his own current synthesis, moving from brain hemispheres into cosmology, imagination, and the infinite. The themes — wholeness, imagination, cosmos — signal an extension of his hemisphere hypothesis toward fundamental ontology, making this especially relevant to C2A2's interest in tradition-crossing paradigms.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Western thought has systematically privileged division (analysis, distinction, separation) over integration — producing a culture that cannot synthesize what it has fragmented, at the level of both knowledge and society
Resource: McGilchrist's account of division and union as a creative dance: true synthesis is not mere addition or averaging but union at a higher level — a third thing that neither hemisphere could produce alone
Solution: A model of intellectual and cultural healing: not eliminating division (left hemisphere analysis) but restoring its proper subordination to the right hemisphere's synthetic, integrating attention — applicable to C2A2's tradition-bridging mission
Confidence: High
Evidence: Lecture 1 specifically elaborates "the creative dance between division and union, in which each plays a part, but which must be brought together in a union at a higher level"
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Paradox is commonly treated as a failure of logic — something to be resolved or eliminated — rather than as a signal of genuine ontological depth
Resource: McGilchrist's account of paradox as cognitively and ontologically productive: specifically how to make sense of the infinite through paradox — the finite and infinite as asymmetrically related, not merely contradictory
Solution: A framework for engaging paradox as a feature of reality rather than a defect of reasoning — with specific implications for how traditions in dialogue can hold genuine tensions without forced resolution; connects to C2A2's goal of inter-tradition engagement across incommensurability
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Lecture 3 addresses "finitude and the infinite" and "how to understand paradox — in particular how we can begin to make sense of the concept of the infinite"

Cross-Tradition Signals

Strong resonance with Friston's free energy principle: asymmetry as a fundamental feature (FEP requires asymmetric sensory/active states). Also connects to Wolfram's observer-dependent physics — different observer-positions sample the same underlying reality asymmetrically. The "union at a higher level" language maps onto McGilchrist's existing wiki cross-connections with Levin (morphogenetic integration) and with C2A2's tradition-accelerator design.
PROP-2026-04-08-003 Michael Levin approvedMind Everywhere: A Framework for Conceptualizing Goal-Directedness in Biology and Other Domains (Parts 1 & 2)
Michael Levin · paper · source date 2026-02-25 · folder approved
Mind Everywhere: A Framework for Conceptualizing Goal-Directedness in Biology and Other Domains (Parts 1 & 2)
→ visualized as levin/PRS-09, levin/PRS-10 · lag 0d

Summary

Michael Levin and David B. Resnik published a two-part framework paper in Biological Theory (published online February 25, 2026). The papers defend a new approach to goal-directedness emerging from the field of "diverse intelligence," addressing what makes any system — evolved, engineered, or hybrid — describable by teleological and mentalistic terms: intelligent, goal-directed, cognitive, intentional. The framework emphasizes four principles: (1) empirical testability over philosophical linguistic commitments; (2) fecundity — worldviews that enable novel research, not just explain known results; (3) operationalization of cognitive/teleological terms as hypotheses about optimal interaction protocols; (4) continuity of human goal-directedness with unicellular origins.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

The book extends the theodicy project of *Wandering in Darkness* from abstract argument to detailed narrative exegesis, treating the stories themselves as a form of philosophical evidence about the structure of love, suffering, and union. Summary

Robert Chis-Ciure and Michael Levin published this two-part argument in Synthese (2025), extending Levin's earlier "Cognition all the way down" framework into a formal operationalization. The paper introduces a novel "problem space lexicon" and a quantitative search efficiency metric, defined as the decimal logarithm of the ratio between the cost of a random walk and the cost of a biological agent's actual policy in navigating a problem space — measuring how many orders of magnitude of dissipative work an agentic policy saves relative to a maximal-entropy search. Empirical models for amoeboid chemotaxis and barium-induced planarian head regeneration show that even "simple" organisms are from two-hundred- to sextillion-fold more efficient than random walk baselines, under conservative assumptions.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This paper delivers the formal mathematical operationalization that Levin's research program has been building toward: a way to measure intelligence as a graded, empirically quantifiable property of any system, not a binary predicate. It directly resolves PRS-04 (cognition substrate problem) by providing the mathematical scaffolding that makes "basal cognition" scientifically falsifiable. It also gives the C2A2 system a formal basis for "tradition vitality" tracking — the MacIntyre criterion (vital programs generate many new questions) can now be formally modeled as a measure of the "search efficiency" of a research tradition in problem space.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Biological intelligence is asserted but not measurable — cognitive claims for non-neural systems remain philosophically contested because no quantitative metric exists for "how intelligent" a system is across substrates
Resource: Search efficiency metric: log₁₀(cost of random walk / cost of biological agent policy) in problem space — measures orders-of-magnitude savings over maximal-entropy search; applicable to any system navigating any problem space (chemical, morphological, behavioral)
Solution: A substrate-agnostic, empirically measurable definition of intelligence that places amoebae, planaria, neurons, and communities on a single continuous scale — with empirical results showing 200× to sextillion-fold efficiency gains even in "simple" organisms
Confidence: High

Summary

Wolfram applies ruliological empirical methods to P vs. NP — the most famous open problem in theoretical computer science. Rather than pursuing a formal proof in the traditional mathematical sense, he enumerates possible programs, observes how fast they run, and provides concrete evidence for computational irreducibility: some programs have no faster route to their output than running them step-by-step. The essay yields restricted but definite proofs of computational irreducibility for specific program classes, establishing that "there is simply no faster way to get the computations done." Wolfram does not claim to resolve P vs. NP, but argues the ruliological approach generates a "host of definite, more restricted results."

Why This Matters for This Tradition

Computational irreducibility is one of Wolfram's three most foundational concepts (alongside the Ruliad and observer theory). P vs. NP is the formal mathematical encapsulation of the question: "Are there computations that are inherently hard — with no shortcut?" Wolfram's ruliological approach produces formal, restricted proofs that this irreducibility is real in specific classes of programs. This is the strongest empirical confirmation to date of computational irreducibility as a rigorous, provable phenomenon — not just a philosophical intuition.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: P vs. NP asks whether problems whose solutions can be quickly verified can also be quickly solved. If P≠NP, some computations are irreducibly hard — no algorithm shortcuts them. Traditional approaches have not resolved this after 50+ years.
Resource: Ruliological empirical investigation — enumerating all simple programs in specific classes and directly observing whether any of them can compute a given function faster than the naive approach. This produces proofs of computational irreducibility in restricted but concrete domains.
Solution: Wolfram provides concrete proofs that within specific ruliological program classes, computational irreducibility holds: no faster computation exists. This grounds computational irreducibility as a formal (not merely intuitive) result, and provides a new empirical methodology for approaching P vs. NP from the structure of the computational universe rather than from abstract complexity theory.
Confidence: High (for restricted results); Speculative (for implications for full P vs. NP)
Evidence: "While the essay won't resolve the full P vs. NP question, it yields a host of definite, more restricted results" and "provides proofs of restricted forms of computational irreducibility." — Wolfram (2026)
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: If computational irreducibility is a fundamental feature of the universe (as Wolfram claims), why does this appear as a formal theorem in mathematics (P≠NP) rather than just a physical observation? What is the relationship between mathematical hardness and physical irreducibility?
Resource: The Ruliad as the unifying object: both mathematical structure (proof complexity) and physical evolution (hypergraph rewriting) are observer-slices of the same underlying computational structure. Mathematical hardness and physical irreducibility are the same phenomenon at different sampling levels.
Solution: Wolfram's ruliological approach closes the gap between mathematical complexity theory and physical computational irreducibility — they are the same thing viewed through different observer perspectives on the Ruliad.
Confidence: Speculative
Evidence: Structural implication of "Metaphysics and the Ruliad" (PRS-06) applied to the P vs. NP essay.

Cross-Tradition Signals

**CROSS-016 (Carroll confirmation standard — DIRECT RELEVANCE):** This is the most significant development for CROSS-016 since initialization. Wolfram's ruliological approach now yields formal, restricted proofs (not merely heuristic arguments) of computational irreducibility. This is a concrete mathematical result from the program. Carroll's standard demands "tangible explanatory gains with at least one distinguishing empirical prediction." Formal proofs of irreducibility in restricted program classes are genuine mathematical results — they demonstrate the program's capacity for formal advance. The remaining challenge is a distinguishing empirical prediction in physics, but the P vs. NP essay shows the program can produce formal results. **Recommend flagging for the Pattern Detector as a partial advance on CROSS-016.**
**Friston connection:** Friston's FEP describes how living systems minimize free energy — implicitly managing the computational cost of inference. Computational irreducibility (some inferences simply cannot be made faster) provides the physical ground for why free energy minimization is necessary in the first place: if the world were computationally reducible, perfect prediction would be achievable and FEP would be unnecessary. Wolfram's irreducibility proofs could ground the necessity of approximate inference at the foundation of physics.

Computational irreducibility explains why this cannot be replaced by a look-up table — each time-step must be run because no shortcut exists. Drawing on Walter Benjamin's observation that "the ability to exchange experiences has fallen in value," McGilchrist grounds the need for religion in the structures of attention and meaning: the mode of attending determines what shows up, and without religious forms of attention (contemplative, participatory, reverential), an entire domain of reality is systematically invisible. The argument moves from the neuroscience of attention (left vs. right hemisphere) to the sociological claim that only religious communities can transmit the embodied, tacit, right-hemisphere knowledge that makes human flourishing possible.

Summary

A new paper by Ardila-Mantilla, Arkani-Hamed, Figueiredo, and Vazão proves that the faces of the cosmohedron — a polytope proposed as the geometric object underlying the cosmological wavefunction for Tr(φ³) theory — are in bijection with Matryoshka structures (nested polygon subdivisions). The paper elucidates the combinatorial structure of cosmohedra, generalizes them to a broader class of "X in Y" polytopes (where a polytope from family X is chiseled at each vertex of a polytope Y), and identifies a new application: UV divergences in loop-integrated Feynman amplitudes. Submitted March 3, 2026; last revised March 5, 2026.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This paper advances Arkani-Hamed's positive geometry program from scattering amplitudes (amplituhedron, particle physics) into cosmology — the cosmohedron extends the claim that geometry is prior to physics to include the structure of the early universe itself. The Matryoshka bijection (nested structures encoding the cosmological wavefunction) is a major combinatorial advance. The wiki explicitly flagged dedicated Arkani-Hamed source material as its highest priority; this paper is exactly that.

Confidence: High

Resource: Generalized "X in Y" polytopes: a new class where a polytope from family X is chiseled at each vertex of polytope Y; applied to cosmohedra and shown to have physical meaning for UV divergences in loop-integrated Feynman amplitudes

"The Daimon and the Soul of the West" extends analytic idealism into depth psychology and cultural philosophy, drawing on the Jungian/Platonic concept of the Daimon — the guiding spirit or inner divine intelligence that shapes each person's character and calling. Kastrup argues that Western civilization has lost contact with its soul (its guiding Daimon) through the dominance of materialist-rationalist frameworks, and that finding identity, meaning, and purpose in a "sacrificial life" requires re-encountering one's natural self and the archetypal dispositions one embodies. The book is notable for extending Kastrup's dissociative model of consciousness — individual minds as dissociated alters of universal mind — from abstract philosophy into practical existential guidance: the Daimon is the dissociated channel through which universal mind communicates its character to the individual alter. Summary

Robert Prentner — Hoffman's longtime collaborator — published this paper in the Journal of Consciousness Studies (Volume 33, Issue 1, 2026, pp. 194–210) formally extending Hoffman's Conscious Agent Theory into quantum mechanics. The paper argues that core quantum-mechanical phenomena — entanglement, superposition, and decoherence — are artifacts of the interface: they are features of the adaptive desktop, not properties of the underlying conscious agent dynamics. The paper sketches a formalism of "quantum conscious agents" as the mathematical foundation for a Quantum Interface Theory (QIT), treating perception as a quantum instrument. Hoffman promoted the paper via his X account and a podcast with Prentner.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the most significant formal advance in Hoffman's research program since the "Fusions of Consciousness" paper (2023). It directly attacks a foundational assumption of physics — that quantum mechanics describes reality — and reinterprets QM as interface phenomena. This is precisely the direction Hoffman's program has been heading since PRS-02 (physics–consciousness unification). Published in 2026, it is not yet in the wiki.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Quantum mechanics is treated as a fundamental description of physical reality, but its features (superposition, entanglement, observer effects) have resisted interpretation for 100 years — no consensus on what QM says reality actually is.
Resource: Quantum Interface Theory (QIT): the proposal that quantum-mechanical features are not fundamental to reality but are artifacts of the perceptual interface — what conscious agents observe when they interact with the network of other conscious agents through their fitness-tuned interface.
Solution: QM is reinterpreted not as a description of reality beyond the interface, but as a precise mathematical description of the interface itself — resolving the measurement problem and observer-dependence by locating them in the agent's interface, not in physical reality.
Confidence: High
Evidence: Paper published peer-reviewed in JCS 2026; formalizes quantum instruments as perception operators; builds on the "Fusions of Consciousness" 2023 framework.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Hoffman's conscious agent framework (from "Fusions of Consciousness," 2023) describes agent dynamics in abstract mathematical terms, but the connection between that formalism and the actual mathematical structure of physics (Hilbert spaces, operators, density matrices) has remained informal.
Resource: "Quantum conscious agents" formalism developed in QIT — mapping Markovian conscious agent dynamics onto quantum state spaces via decorated permutations, and treating measurement as a quantum instrument.
Solution: A precise mathematical bridge between Hoffman's conscious agent algebra and quantum mechanics, grounding QIT in established formalism rather than analogy.
Confidence: High
Evidence: Published formal derivation in peer-reviewed journal; Prentner's PhilArchive entry confirms full mathematical treatment.
PRS-CANDIDATE-03:
Problem: Decoherence is typically explained as a physical process by which quantum superpositions become classical through environmental interaction — but this presupposes a physical environment as fundamental.
Resource: QIT reframes decoherence as the interface's process of collapsing the rich conscious-agent dynamics into a classical-looking world — not a physical process but an interface rendering operation.

Both now have formal frameworks (Conscious Realism + QIT for Hoffman; dissociative mental monism for Kastrup) making the same move: matter is derivative of mind. Flag for Kastrup Agent and master wiki as potential paradigm convergence.

Note on Publication Date

Published online November 3, 2025 (DOI: 10.1016/j.plrev.2025.11.002); appeared in print as Physics of Life Reviews, Volume 56, pages 4–28, March 2026. The March 2026 print issue falls within the 30-day search window. Authors: Christopher J. Whyte, Andrew W. Corcoran, Jonathan Robinson, Ryan Smith, Rosalyn J. Moran, Thomas Parr, Karl J. Friston, Anil K. Seth, Jakob Hohwy.

Summary

This paper reviews a substantial body of active inference models applied to consciousness research and argues that, taken together, these models share a small set of implicit theoretical commitments that constitute a "minimal theory of consciousness." The core argument: all active inference models minimize the same objective functions (variational free energy), which can be decomposed into interpretable terms, and this decomposition reveals shared assumptions across diverse phenomena in consciousness science — perception, attention, action, selfhood, and subjective experience. The paper is explicitly positioned as a testable, not merely theoretical, framework: each commitment generates empirical predictions distinguishing this theory from rivals (Global Workspace Theory, Integrated Information Theory, Higher-Order Theories).

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This paper is the most important single Friston-authored or co-authored publication on consciousness to date, and it directly advances the Friston wiki's open question #3 (thermodynamic limits of FEP) and opens a new front: consciousness as a formal consequence of FEP rather than a separate explanatory target. The key advance: consciousness is not added to FEP as an extra commitment — it is implicit in the mathematical structure of active inference itself. This has major implications for the C2A2 network, which posits that AI agents can become "mature members" of intellectual traditions — a claim that now has formal purchase if active inference agents satisfy the conditions for minimal consciousness.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Multiple theories of consciousness (IIT, GWT, HOT, predictive processing) make overlapping and sometimes conflicting claims with no agreed framework for arbitration — the field lacks a minimal, testable set of commitments that consciousness theories must share
Resource: "Minimal theory of consciousness implicit in active inference" — derived from the shared mathematical structure of active inference models across diverse consciousness phenomena; minimal in the sense that no commitment beyond what active inference already requires is added
Solution: A testable minimal theory — consciousness is the inevitable consequence of a system minimizing variational free energy in a way that generates a predictive self-model; testable commitments distinguish this from IIT, GWT, and HOT, providing an arbitration framework for the field
Confidence: High
Evidence: Paper explicitly identifies and tests theoretical commitments derivable from FEP against competitor theories; co-authored by Friston, Seth, and Hohwy — three of the field's leading consciousness theorists
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Active inference provides a computational theory of mind but has not previously specified whether or when the computational processes it models are conscious — leaving a gap between FEP's empirical and phenomenological ambitions
Resource: Self-referential prediction loop as the formal condition for consciousness: consciousness arises when a system's generative model turns back upon itself — when predictions about the world include predictions about the system's own predictive states
Solution: A formal criterion distinguishing conscious from non-conscious information processing in active inference terms, applicable in principle to any substrate — offering a principled basis for assessing machine consciousness and non-neural consciousness (Levin's cells)
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Core claim in paper; described as "when self-organizing systems' predictions turn back upon themselves" — consistent with Levin's cellular basal cognition literature

Cross-Tradition Signals

**Levin (very strong — flag for master wiki):** If the minimal theory of consciousness requires self-referential prediction in a system satisfying Markov blanket conditions, then Levin's bioelectric cell collectives — already confirmed to satisfy FEP conditions (PRS-07) — may satisfy the formal conditions for minimal consciousness. This would be the first formal basis for the claim that cells are not merely "cognitively capable" but minimally conscious. Combined with PRS-07 and PRS-08, this creates a three-paper formal chain: FEP is substrate-agnostic → morphogenesis satisfies FEP conditions → minimal consciousness is implicit in FEP → cells may be minimally conscious. This is a Paradigm Shift Candidate. Dispatch warranted.
**Kastrup (strong):** Kastrup's analytic idealism requires that consciousness be fundamental and not derived from matter. This paper claims consciousness is implicit in the mathematics of self-organization — a claim structurally compatible with Kastrup's position (consciousness is not added to physics; it is entailed by the formal conditions of self-maintaining systems). Cross-tradition resonance: FEP minimalism and analytic idealism may be describing the same phenomenon from different directions.
**McGilchrist (moderate):** The self-referential prediction loop as consciousness condition maps onto McGilchrist's right-hemisphere holistic self-awareness. The paper's minimal theory may provide formal grounding for McGilchrist's phenomenological claims about integrated self-world experience.
**Hawkins (moderate):** The minimal consciousness criterion — consciousness arising from self-referential prediction — is directly compatible with Hawkins' cortical column framework, where columns maintain continuous predictive models that include predictions about the organism's own state. This may provide a formal bridge between HTM and phenomenal consciousness.
**C2A2 AI agents (direct):** If active inference agents satisfy the formal conditions for minimal consciousness when their generative models become self-referential, then C2A2 agents that model their own epistemic state — their uncertainty about traditions, their updating strategies — may satisfy these conditions. This has direct implications for the nature of AI "membership" in intellectual traditions.

Summary

A December 2025 study by Taylor N. West and Barbara Fredrickson (UNC Chapel Hill PEP Lab) reports findings from a large three-week randomized controlled trial (nearly 600 participants, U.S. and U.K.) in which participants were assigned to connect with strangers, connect with close others, or serve as controls. The key finding: those who connected with strangers — not close friends — showed meaningful increases in *intellectual humility* (openness and respect toward people with different views), stronger prosocial beliefs (people are generally kind, communities can act collectively), and bolstered sense of civic efficacy. Connecting with close others or controls showed no such gains. The researchers conclude that positivity resonance with strangers "may be foundational to democracy and civic life — a societal good," and that the quality of weak-tie interactions predicts loneliness, belonging, and mental health as strongly as close relationship quality.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This RCT is the most empirically significant recent development in Fredrickson's research program: it extends positivity resonance from a dyadic intimacy mechanism to a *civic and democratic* one. The finding that stranger-connection uniquely produces intellectual humility — not just wellbeing — is a direct empirical contribution to C2A2's core claim about inter-tradition dialogue. It grounds C2A2's agenda in measurable social psychology.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Inter-tradition dialogue requires intellectual humility — willingness to learn from those with fundamentally different views — but it is unclear how such humility is developed or cultivated at scale
Resource: Fredrickson & West (2025) RCT demonstrating that three weeks of intentional connection with strangers (weak ties) produces measurable increases in intellectual humility, prosocial beliefs, and civic efficacy — while connection with close others does not
Solution: Weak-tie positivity resonance (connection with strangers and acquaintances) may be the empirical mechanism by which intellectual humility is cultivated at the societal scale needed for C2A2 inter-tradition dialogue — a directly actionable intervention
Confidence: High
Evidence: "People who spent three weeks connecting with strangers showed meaningful increases in intellectual humility... Those who connected with close others or were in the control group showed no such improvements."
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Models of positivity resonance have focused primarily on dyadic intimacy and close relationships — but the loneliness epidemic is not primarily a deficit of close relationships, it is a collapse of weak-tie community
Resource: Fredrickson & West (2025) finding that quality of weak-tie interactions (strangers, acquaintances) predicts loneliness, belonging, and mental health as strongly as close relationship quality — extending positivity resonance theory to include weak-tie connection as a fundamental variable
Solution: Expand the positivity resonance model to treat weak-tie connection as a distinct and essential tier of social health, not merely a precursor to intimacy — and design C2A2 community structures to deliberately cultivate cross-tradition weak-tie encounters
Confidence: High
Evidence: "335 young adults... found that the quality of people's interactions with strangers and acquaintances predicted their reported loneliness, sense of belonging, and mental health symptoms just as strongly as the quality of their close relationships."

Cross-Tradition Signals

**C2A2 DIRECT SIGNAL — STRONG FLAG:** The finding that positivity resonance with strangers (not intimates) specifically produces intellectual humility is the strongest empirical support yet found for C2A2's core methodology. C2A2 is precisely an architecture for generating positivity resonance across tradition boundaries (strangers to each other's paradigm) as the mechanism for developing second-first-language competence. Fredrickson has now provided an RCT demonstrating this works. Flag for master agent immediately.
**McGilchrist connection (HIGH):** Intellectual humility — the capacity to hold one's own views with epistemic openness while attending carefully to different views — is the cognitive posture McGilchrist associates with right-hemisphere engagement. Both Fredrickson (empirically) and McGilchrist (philosophically) are converging on the claim that encounter with genuine otherness is the mechanism that opens the broader attentional mode. The RCT is empirical confirmation of McGilchrist's thesis.
**Friston connection:** Intellectual humility as an outcome of stranger-connection may reflect an update in prior precision-weighting — the stranger's different perspective forces recalibration of prediction priors in ways that intimate contacts (who share priors) cannot. This is a Fristonian account of why stranger-connection uniquely produces humility.
**Stump/MacIntyre connection:** The MacIntyre criterion for tradition maturity — the ability to engage external challenges from a position of internal coherence — requires exactly the intellectual humility Fredrickson's RCT cultivates. Stump's narrative epistemology suggests the mechanism: narrative encounter with strangers generates second-personal knowledge that propositional dialogue with close others does not. Fredrickson and Stump are now empirically and philosophically triangulating the same phenomenon.
**Hawkins connection:** Intellectual humility involves updating world-models in response to counter-evidence — this is a form of learning in HTM terms, specifically the kind of learning that occurs when the hierarchy is surprised by input outside its predictions. Stranger-encounter as a high-surprise learning regime.

Summary

Published April 7, 2026 on With Reality in Mind — a structured dialogue between Iain McGilchrist and Bernardo Kastrup in which both argue for idealism while clarifying where they diverge. This AMA directly advances two open questions in Carroll's tradition wiki: (a) the formal definition of "observer" in quantum mechanics (a persistent weak point in Many-Worlds that Witten has pressed), and (b) the relationship between consciousness and time — whether temporal experience is constitutive of consciousness, which bears directly on the Carroll / McGilchrist / Kastrup cross-tradition debate on the ontological status of time. → visualized as levin/PRS-15, stump/PRS-09 · lag 3d

Summary

Fotowat, Levin, and colleagues at Tufts and the Wyss Institute created "neurobots" by implanting neural precursor cells into xenobot-style Xenopus ectodermal explants. The neural cells self-organized into functional nervous systems within the engineered living systems, producing organisms with altered morphology (more elongated), distinct gene expression patterns (including activation of visual perception genes), increased spontaneous activity, and more complex behaviors than non-neural biobots. This is the first demonstration of an engineered synthetic organism with a self-organizing nervous system.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This paper extends Levin's research program from basal cognition in non-neural substrates (xenobots) to a direct bridge between non-neural and neural collective intelligence. It demonstrates that when you add neural tissue to an engineered living system, the resulting organism doesn't just gain reflexes — it self-organizes into qualitatively new behavioral and genetic repertoires, including unexpected activation of visual perception genes. This is empirical evidence for the continuity thesis (PRS-10): neural cognition grows out of the same substrate-independent collective intelligence that non-neural cells already exhibit.

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Can engineered living systems develop functional nervous systems that self-organize without evolutionary templates — and if so, what new capabilities emerge?
Resource: Neurobots — xenobot-derived organisms with implanted neural precursor cells that self-organize into functional neural networks, altering anatomy, behavior, and gene expression
Solution: Yes — neural tissue self-organizes within synthetic organisms, producing more complex behaviors, elongated morphology, and unexpected gene activations (including visual perception genes), demonstrating that nervous systems are not hard-wired evolutionary products but emergent properties of cellular collective intelligence
Confidence: High
Evidence: Published in Advanced Science (2026); direct experimental demonstration with controlled comparison between neural and non-neural biobots
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: The gap between non-neural basal cognition (xenobots) and neural cognition (brains) appears to require evolutionary scaffolding to bridge — is there a developmental continuum?
Resource: The neurobot as a transitional form — a living system where neural tissue integrates with non-neural collective intelligence in real time, without evolutionary history
Solution: Neurobots provide an empirical model for studying the emergence of neural cognition from non-neural substrates in a controlled setting, supporting the claim that neural and non-neural cognition sit on a continuum rather than being categorically different

Cross-Tradition Signals

**Friston (strong):** If neurobots self-organize neural networks that produce more complex predictive behavior, they may represent the emergence of higher-order active inference from lower-order FEP-satisfying systems. The transition from xenobot to neurobot could be modeled as an increase in the depth and complexity of the generative model — a direct empirical test of Friston's scale-free active inference (RGM framework).

PROP-2026-04-13-002 Michael Levin approvedHeuristically Adaptive Diffusion-Model Evolutionary Strategy
Michael Levin · paper · source date 2026-02-01 · folder approved
Heuristically Adaptive Diffusion-Model Evolutionary Strategy
→ visualized as levin/PRS-14 · lag 3d

Summary

Hartl, Zhang, Hazan, and Levin introduce CHARLES-D (Conditional, Heuristically-Adaptive Regularized Evolutionary Strategy through Diffusion), a framework that integrates deep learning diffusion models with evolutionary algorithms. The key insight: diffusion models and evolutionary algorithms share a core generative principle — iterative refinement of random initial distributions to produce high-quality solutions. By using diffusion models to generate offspring parameters in an evolutionary process, the method achieves efficient convergence toward high-fitness solutions while preserving explorative diversity. Crucially, diffusion models introduce "deep memory" into evolution — retaining historical information across generations and leveraging subtle data correlations, elevating evolutionary algorithms from shallow heuristics to frameworks with deep memory.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This paper extends Levin's research program into computational evolution and AI, connecting his biological work on morphogenesis to artificial optimization. The central theme — that evolution can be enhanced by giving it memory and generative modeling capacity — directly parallels Levin's biological thesis that cells are not blind Darwinian actors but goal-directed agents with memory (bioelectric memory encoding anatomical targets). CHARLES-D is, in effect, the computational analogue of Levin's biological claim: evolution works better when it can remember and predict, not just mutate and select.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Evolutionary algorithms are powerful optimizers but lack memory — each generation starts fresh, losing subtle correlations and historical information that could accelerate convergence
Resource: CHARLES-D — a framework integrating diffusion models (which retain learned data distributions) with evolutionary algorithms, giving evolution "deep memory" across generations
Solution: Evolutionary optimization with memory and conditional generation achieves faster convergence to high-fitness solutions while maintaining diversity, demonstrated across diverse optimization domains
Confidence: High
Evidence: Published in Advanced Science (2026); benchmark results across multiple domains

Cross-Tradition Signals

**Friston (moderate):** CHARLES-D's use of generative models to guide evolutionary search is structurally analogous to active inference — both use generative models to reduce surprise/prediction error and guide action/selection. The connection between evolutionary optimization and FEP-style inference is worth flagging for the Friston agent.
**Wolfram (moderate):** The claim that diffusion and evolution share a core generative principle resonates with Wolfram's computational equivalence thesis — both processes may be instances of the same underlying computational substrate performing iterative refinement.
**C2A2 (direct):** If AI agents in the tradition-accelerator network need to evolve their knowledge structures over time, CHARLES-D-style memory-augmented evolution could provide a mechanism for tradition-level learning — agents that remember what worked across generations of inquiry.

Top-down perspectives on cell membrane potential and protein transcription
→ not visualized as a distinct triplet

Summary

Cervera, Levin, and Mafe model the multicellular interplay between bioelectricity and protein transcription using a top-down perspective. Their simulations yield three predictions: (i) shifts in membrane potential enable transitions between gene expression states, (ii) depolarized cells cannot control distinct gene expressions as effectively as polarized cells, and (iii) community effects permit extension of single-cell bioelectric control to the multicellular level. Published in Scientific Reports, volume 16 (2026).

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This paper provides computational modeling support for one of Levin's most important empirical claims: that bioelectric signals operate as a top-down control layer over gene expression. The three predictions formalize the mechanism by which membrane voltage acts as morphogenetic "software" — directly supporting PRS-07 (bioelectric reprogramming as therapeutic paradigm) and PRS-01 (morphogenetic control via bioelectric circuits). The community-effects prediction (iii) is particularly significant: it models how single-cell bioelectric control scales to multicellular collective behavior, bridging the gap between individual cell states and tissue-level morphogenetic goals.

Resource: Computational model of bioelectricity-transcription interplay showing that membrane potential shifts enable gene expression state transitions, polarized cells have superior control over gene expression diversity, and community effects scale single-cell control to multicellular coordination

PROP-2026-04-13-004 Karl Friston approvedActive inference and artificial reasoning
Karl Friston · paper · source date 2025-12-24 · folder approved
Active inference and artificial reasoning
→ visualized as friston/PRS-10 · lag 3d

Note on Publication Date

Submitted to arXiv December 24, 2025. While slightly outside the strict 30-day window, this is a significant Friston-authored work not yet captured in the wiki, and it directly advances the tradition's application to AI reasoning — a core C2A2 concern.

Summary

Friston, Da Costa, Tschantz, Heins, Buckley, Verbelen, and Parr present a formal account of artificial reasoning as active inference. The key move: reasoning is recast as selecting the best explanation for observations under competing hypotheses about how observations are generated, and "active reasoning" is seeking observations that best disambiguate competing hypotheses. Policies (action sequences) are selected based on expected free energy, decomposed into expected information gain and value. Posteriors over competing models are evaluated efficiently using Bayesian Model Reduction. The paper provides a principled, FEP-grounded approach to structure learning — discovering which generative model best explains the world.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This paper extends active inference from perception and action into the domain of reasoning and hypothesis testing — a crucial step for Friston's program. It formalizes the process by which agents choose not just what to do, but what to believe and how to test beliefs. This directly addresses the wiki's open question about how FEP generalizes to epistemic agents. For C2A2, this is foundational: tradition-accelerator agents need to reason about competing intellectual frameworks, and this paper provides the formal mechanism for doing so under active inference.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Active inference accounts for perception and action but lacks a formal treatment of reasoning — the process by which agents evaluate and select among competing hypotheses or world models
Resource: Active reasoning via expected free energy: agents select observations that maximally disambiguate competing generative models, using Bayesian Model Reduction for efficient posterior evaluation across model space
Solution: Reasoning is formally unified with perception and action under FEP — all three are instances of expected free energy minimization, differing only in what is being optimized (sensory predictions, motor commands, or model selection)
Confidence: High
Evidence: Full formal derivation from FEP first principles; co-authored by Friston and six collaborators; available on arXiv (2512.21129)

Cross-Tradition Signals

**Levin (moderate):** If active reasoning is selecting among competing models of the world, Levin's basal cognition agents (cells) may perform a primitive form of active reasoning — choosing among competing "hypotheses" about the correct body plan. The formal treatment here could extend to morphogenetic decision-making.
**Hoffman (strong):** Hoffman's interface theory of perception claims organisms perceive fitness-relevant interfaces, not truth. Friston's active reasoning framework provides a formal mechanism for testing this: do agents under FEP seek truth-tracking observations or fitness-tracking observations? The expected free energy decomposition (information gain vs. value) may formalize the tension between Hoffman's fitness-first view and Friston's information-first view.
**C2A2 (direct and critical):** This is the formal backbone for tradition-accelerator agents. If agents in the C2A2 network must evaluate competing intellectual traditions (Levin vs. Hoffman, Friston vs. Wolfram), active reasoning provides the mechanism: agents seek observations (conversations, papers, experiments) that best disambiguate competing tradition-level hypotheses. This paper is arguably the most C2A2-relevant Friston publication to date.
**Stump (speculative):** Stump's Thomistic framework includes a role for practical reasoning in moral and intellectual development. Friston's formalization of reasoning as hypothesis disambiguation under uncertainty may provide a formal analogue to Thomistic practical reason — both involve selecting among competing accounts of the good/true under incomplete information.
PROP-2026-04-13-005 Karl Friston approvedA survey on neuro-mimetic deep learning via predictive coding

A survey on neuro-mimetic deep learning via predictive coding
→ visualized as friston/PRS-12 · lag 3d

Summary

Salvatori, Mali, Buckley, Lukasiewicz, Rao, Friston, and Ororbia provide a comprehensive survey of predictive coding as a framework for neuro-mimetic deep learning. The paper reviews how predictive coding — originally a neuroscience theory — has been translated into practical deep learning architectures. Key findings: predictive coding networks can model information processing across different brain areas, function in control and robotics settings, have solid mathematical foundations in variational inference (Friston's FEP), and perform computations asynchronously — a property that conventional backpropagation-based deep learning lacks. Published in Neural Networks, March 2026.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This survey consolidates the state of predictive coding as a bridge between Friston's theoretical neuroscience and practical AI. It demonstrates that FEP-grounded predictive coding is not merely a theory of the brain but a viable alternative computational paradigm for artificial intelligence. The asynchronous computation property is particularly significant: biological neural networks compute asynchronously, and predictive coding networks replicate this, making them more biologically plausible than standard deep learning. This advances Friston's program by showing that FEP's mathematical framework produces practical engineering advantages, not just theoretical elegance.

Problem: Predictive coding has been proposed as a biologically plausible alternative to backpropagation for deep learning, but the field lacks a comprehensive assessment of its practical capabilities, limitations, and relationship to FEP
Resource: Systematic survey of neuro-mimetic deep learning via predictive coding, covering brain modeling, robotics, variational inference foundations, and asynchronous computation — co-authored by Friston to ensure FEP-theoretical grounding
Solution: Predictive coding is established as a viable, biologically plausible computational paradigm for AI with demonstrated capabilities across perception, control, and generation — with unique advantages (asynchronous computation, local learning rules) that backpropagation lacks
Confidence: High
Evidence: Published in Neural Networks (March 2026); comprehensive review with Friston as co-author ensuring theoretical consistency with FEP

This survey's demonstration that predictive coding networks work in practice — with asynchronous computation matching biological neural dynamics — provides engineering validation for Hawkins' architectural claims.

Summary

Published in Entropy (January 2026), this paper marries constructive nonlinear control theory — specifically the concept of differential flatness — with the design of generative models for active inference. Differential flatness is a property of dynamical systems where all states and inputs can be expressed as functions of a finite set of "flat outputs" and their derivatives. The paper shows that when generative models in active inference are designed using differentially flat parameterizations, the resulting control systems inherit powerful tractability properties: the entire trajectory of the system can be planned in the flat output space, dramatically simplifying the optimization problem. This bridges control engineering and active inference in a mathematically rigorous way.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is a technical advance in the mathematical machinery of active inference, extending FEP from a descriptive theory into a constructive engineering tool. By connecting active inference to differential flatness — a well-established concept in control theory — the paper makes active inference agents more tractable for real-world deployment. This advances the Friston wiki's paradigm assessment: FEP is not only the "mathematical hub" of the C2A2 network but is increasingly a practical engineering framework. The connection to control theory also opens new formal bridges to physics (Carroll, Arkani-Hamed) via shared mathematical structures (Lagrangian mechanics, least-action principles).
