PROP-2026-04-28-001 Donald Hoffman approvedThe Interface Theory of Perception (chapter in Stevens' Handbook of Experimental Psychology and Cognitive Neuroscie
Donald Hoffman · paper · source date 2026 (handbook edition) · folder approved
The Interface Theory of Perception (chapter in Stevens' Handbook of Experimental Psychology and Cognitive Neuroscience, 4th ed., ed. J.T. Wixted)
→ visualized as hoffman/PRS-16, hoffman/PRS-17, hoffman/PRS-18, levin/PRS-23, levin/PRS-24 · lag 7d

Summary

Hoffman's authoritative handbook chapter on the Interface Theory of Perception (ITP), published as part of the 4th edition of Stevens' Handbook of Experimental Psychology and Cognitive Neuroscience (Wiley, 2026). The chapter consolidates ITP into a textbook-grade synthesis built on two formal results: the **Fitness-Beats-Truth (FBT) Theorem**, which proves that veridical perceptions are generically driven to extinction by equally complex non-veridical perceptions tuned to fitness functions, and the **Invention of Symmetry (IOS) Theorem**, which establishes that organisms can have perceptions of 3D space and 1-D time with perfectly coordinated, predictable actions even when no spacetime structure exists in objective reality. From these, Hoffman derives a new ITP-native theory of illusions (an illusion is *an unadaptive perception that most normal perceivers have* — not a mismatch with reality, since no perception ever matches reality on ITP) and a parallel reformulation of hallucinations.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the canonical reference-work statement of ITP. The wiki currently captures ITP via PRS-03 (the empirical claim that perception tracks fitness, not truth) but has no record of either theorem under Hoffman's name, nor of the new ITP-internal accounts of illusion and hallucination. The chapter is also the first place where Hoffman uses the IOS theorem to **directly refute** the Shepard / Tenenbaum line that perceptual regularities (e.g., the Euclidean group of 3D space) are evolutionarily-internalized regularities of the objective world — a foundational claim of mainstream perceptual science. This is high-prestige placement (Stevens' Handbook is the standard reference), so the chapter's framing will shape how ITP is taught for the next decade.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: ITP is widely cited but its two foundational mathematical results — the FBT Theorem and the IOS Theorem — have not been integrated into a single, citable, peer-published exposition that mainstream perceptual scientists can engage with directly. As long as they remain dispersed across journal articles, ITP looks like a philosophical position rather than a proven mathematical claim.
Resource: A single textbook-grade chapter in Stevens' Handbook (Wixted ed., 2026) that states both theorems, sketches their proofs, and applies them in sequence: FBT shows veridical perceptions are evolutionarily improbable; IOS shows that lack of veridicality is fully compatible with the predictable structured perception we actually have.
Solution: ITP is now positioned not as one option among many but as the formally-grounded null hypothesis for any evolutionary theory of perception — the one that survives both the existence proof against truth-tracking and the existence proof for non-truth-tracking but action-coordinated interfaces.
Confidence: High
Evidence: "Together the IOS Theorem and FBT Theorem flatly contradict the claim that the regularities of our perceptions — regularities such as the Euclidean group of three-dimensional space — are evolutionarily internalized versions of regularities in the objective world."
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: The standard theory of illusion in perceptual science presupposes veridical perception as the baseline: an illusion is a perception that fails to match reality. ITP says no perception ever matches reality, which on the standard view would entail that *all* perceptions are illusions — a reductio that has been used as a standing objection to ITP.
Resource: Hoffman's ITP-internal redefinition: *An illusion is an unadaptive perception that most normal perceivers have under specified conditions.* The Necker cube, depth illusions, and other classics are illusions not because they fail to match objective reality but because they fail to guide adaptive behavior in the niche where they occur.
Solution: ITP is no longer vulnerable to the "everything is an illusion" reductio. It now generates a positive research program: empirical investigation of *which* perceptions guide adaptive behavior in specific niches, with illusions and hallucinations identified relative to that adaptive standard rather than to objective truth.
Confidence: High
Evidence: "Here it is — the ITP theory of illusions: An illusion is an unadaptive perception that most normal perceivers have...the perception fails to guide adaptive behavior."
PRS-CANDIDATE-03:
Problem: Conscious Realism's claim that spacetime is not fundamental needs an argument that does not depend on physics speculation (amplituhedron, scattering amplitudes) but emerges from perceptual science itself, so that perceptual scientists are forced to engage with it.
Resource: The IOS Theorem applied to spacetime: organisms can have perceptions of 3D space and 1-D time with perfectly coordinated predictable actions in that perceived spacetime, even when objective reality has no such structure, provided the cardinality of objective states is sufficiently large. The theorem is not restricted to 3D space — it holds for arbitrary groups in any dimension.
Solution: A perceptual-science-internal argument that spacetime is an interface artifact, decoupled from the (separate, more speculative) physics-internal arguments via the amplituhedron program. This gives Conscious Realism two independent routes to its central ontological claim — perceptual evolution and fundamental physics — strengthening the program's robustness to objections from either side.
Confidence: Medium-High
Evidence: "The IOS Theorem is not restricted to 3D space and 1-D time. The IOS Theorem holds for arbitrary groups of any dimension." Combined with the Reply 3 discussion of how predictable spacetime perception coexists with non-spacetime objective reality.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Hawkins / reference frames** — Hawkins' cortical columns build reference frames that are *useful for action*, not veridical maps of objective reality. The IOS Theorem provides a formal underwriting of Hawkins' implicit assumption: a column can build a fully predictive, action-coordinated reference frame for an "object" even when objective reality contains nothing like that object. This deepens PRS-12 in the Hoffman wiki (Hawkins reference frames ARE Hoffman interfaces) by giving it a theorem-level grounding rather than a structural analogy. Flag for both Hawkins and Hoffman wikis.
- **Carroll / poetic naturalism** — The chapter's positive theory of illusion (unadaptive perceptions, not non-veridical ones) is precisely the move Carroll's poetic naturalism would have to make if it accepted ITP: physical talk and perceptual talk are *useful* at their respective scales, but neither has metaphysical priority. Productive tension here — Carroll insists the physical level is real; Hoffman now has a theorem-grade reason to deny it.
- **Arkani-Hamed / amplituhedron** — The IOS Theorem, generalized to arbitrary groups in any dimension, is the formal companion to the amplituhedron-derivation program: where amplituhedron physics shows spacetime can be derived *out of* a more primitive structure, IOS shows spacetime perception can persist *without* a more primitive spacetime. Together they bracket the ITP claim from above and below.
- **Levin / basal cognition** — Hoffman's reformulated theory of illusion as "unadaptive perception" works at any scale where there is an organism with adaptive behavior — including xenobots, anthrobots, and Levin's collective cellular agents. The chapter therefore extends ITP downward to basal cognition without modification, strengthening the Hoffman × Levin convergence already noted in CROSS-034.
- **Stump / Thomistic intellect** — Hoffman's evidence-based denial that perception delivers objective reality is structurally compatible with the Thomistic claim that intellect (not sense) is the seat of understanding. The chapter's machinery may be a usable resource for Stump's account of how intellect operates on a non-veridical sensory interface.

PROP-2026-05-04-001 alt PROP-2026-05-18-003 Karl Friston APPROVEActive Inference: A method for Phenotyping Agency in AI systems?
Karl Friston · paper · source date 2026-04-25 · folder _pending_dupes_resolved · decided 2026-05-12
Active Inference: A method for Phenotyping Agency in AI systems?
→ visualized as friston/PRS-24, friston/PRS-25 · lag -9d

Summary

A new arxiv paper (April 25, 2026) by Wilson, Constant, Albarracin, Hinrichs, Moore, Polani, and Friston proposing active inference as a framework for "phenotyping" agency in AI systems. The paper offers a minimal definition of agency built from three criteria — intentionality (action grounded in beliefs and desires), rationality (normatively coherent action entailed by a world model), and explainability (action causally traceable to internal states) — and instantiates these as a partially observable Markov decision process under variational free-energy minimization. Using a canonical T-maze paradigm, they show how empowerment (channel capacity between actions and anticipated observations) serves as an operational metric distinguishing zero-, intermediate-, and high-agency phenotypes.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the freshest Friston-co-authored extension of active inference into the AI agency / alignment territory since the "Active Inference and Artificial Reasoning" paper (already in the wiki). It reframes the alignment-relevant question "is this AI system an agent?" as a *measurable phenotypic question* rather than a definitional one. The paper directly bridges Friston's clinical "computational phenotyping" tradition (used in computational psychiatry to characterize humans) with the AI agency debate — making this a methodologically reflexive use of active inference. It strengthens the wiki's account of how Friston's program is migrating from neuroscience into AI characterization without losing its variational core.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: The proliferation of agentic AI has outpaced the conceptual tools needed to characterize agency in computational systems. Existing definitions (autonomy, goal-directedness) are too coarse to distinguish degrees or kinds of agency, and don't yield operational metrics.
Resource: A three-criterion minimal definition of agency (intentionality, rationality, explainability) instantiated as a POMDP under expected-free-energy minimization, with empowerment (action–observation channel capacity) as the operational metric.
Solution: A "computational phenotyping" methodology for AI agency — agency becomes a measurable, graded property along a spectrum (zero, intermediate, high) rather than a binary or discursive label, and the same variational framework that phenotypes humans in computational psychiatry phenotypes AI systems.
Confidence: High
Evidence: arxiv 2604.23278, T-maze experimental section showing empowerment-graded agency phenotypes.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: AI systems can be trained on objectives that imitate goal-directed behavior without satisfying the structural conditions that would warrant calling them agents (i.e. without intentional-rational-explainable structure). How do we tell apart "behaviorally agent-like" systems from "structurally agent-like" systems?
Resource: Empowerment as a structural-rather-than-behavioral metric — it measures the capacity of the agent's action policies to causally constrain anticipated observations, regardless of whether external behavior looks goal-directed.
Solution: A way to dissolve the "looks like an agent" / "is an agent" ambiguity in AI systems by grounding the answer in the geometry of the agent's generative model, not in its behavioral output.
Confidence: Medium-High
Evidence: T-maze structural-manipulation experiments distinguishing behaviorally similar systems with different empowerment profiles.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Hawkins (Thousand Brains / sensorimotor agency):** Phenotyping agency by structural conditions of the generative model maps directly onto Hawkins' "intelligence requires sensorimotor reference frames" thesis (FINDING-018a). Both programs converge on a structural rather than behavioral definition of agency. New CROSS candidate.
- **Levin (multi-scale agency):** Levin's "competent subunits making decisions" framework already invites a Friston-style phenotyping. The Wilson et al. method could be applied to bioelectrically-mediated cellular collectives — a testable bridge.
- **Wolfram (rulial-space cognition):** Wolfram's "AI's final form" as non-humanlike rulial-space exploration (PROP-2026-04-27-003) and Friston's empowerment metric are complementary — Friston gives the metric, Wolfram gives the substrate. A possible joint operationalization.
- **Stump / McGilchrist (agency and narrative):** Empowerment-as-channel-capacity is silent on whether the agency phenotype is narratively coherent, which is what Stump (PRS on biblical narratives) and McGilchrist (right-hemisphere participatory engagement) treat as essential. A useful contrast point.

Summary

A new arxiv paper (April 25, 2026) by Wilson, Constant, Albarracin, Hinrichs, Moore, Polani, and Friston proposing active inference as a framework for "phenotyping" agency in AI systems. The paper offers a minimal definition of agency built from three criteria — intentionality (action grounded in beliefs and desires), rationality (normatively coherent action entailed by a world model), and explainability (action causally traceable to internal states) — and instantiates these as a partially observable Markov decision process under variational free-energy minimization. Using a canonical T-maze paradigm, they show how empowerment (channel capacity between actions and anticipated observations) serves as an operational metric distinguishing zero-, intermediate-, and high-agency phenotypes.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the freshest Friston-co-authored extension of active inference into the AI agency / alignment territory since the "Active Inference and Artificial Reasoning" paper (already in the wiki). It reframes the alignment-relevant question "is this AI system an agent?" as a *measurable phenotypic question* rather than a definitional one. The paper directly bridges Friston's clinical "computational phenotyping" tradition (used in computational psychiatry to characterize humans) with the AI agency debate — making this a methodologically reflexive use of active inference. It strengthens the wiki's account of how Friston's program is migrating from neuroscience into AI characterization without losing its variational core.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: The proliferation of agentic AI has outpaced the conceptual tools needed to characterize agency in computational systems. Existing definitions (autonomy, goal-directedness) are too coarse to distinguish degrees or kinds of agency, and don't yield operational metrics.
Resource: A three-criterion minimal definition of agency (intentionality, rationality, explainability) instantiated as a POMDP under expected-free-energy minimization, with empowerment (action–observation channel capacity) as the operational metric.
Solution: A "computational phenotyping" methodology for AI agency — agency becomes a measurable, graded property along a spectrum (zero, intermediate, high) rather than a binary or discursive label, and the same variational framework that phenotypes humans in computational psychiatry phenotypes AI systems.
Confidence: High
Evidence: arxiv 2604.23278, T-maze experimental section showing empowerment-graded agency phenotypes.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: AI systems can be trained on objectives that imitate goal-directed behavior without satisfying the structural conditions that would warrant calling them agents (i.e. without intentional-rational-explainable structure). How do we tell apart "behaviorally agent-like" systems from "structurally agent-like" systems?
Resource: Empowerment as a structural-rather-than-behavioral metric — it measures the capacity of the agent's action policies to causally constrain anticipated observations, regardless of whether external behavior looks goal-directed.
Solution: A way to dissolve the "looks like an agent" / "is an agent" ambiguity in AI systems by grounding the answer in the geometry of the agent's generative model, not in its behavioral output.
Confidence: Medium-High
Evidence: T-maze structural-manipulation experiments distinguishing behaviorally similar systems with different empowerment profiles.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Hawkins (Thousand Brains / sensorimotor agency):** Phenotyping agency by structural conditions of the generative model maps directly onto Hawkins' "intelligence requires sensorimotor reference frames" thesis (FINDING-018a). Both programs converge on a structural rather than behavioral definition of agency. New CROSS candidate.
- **Levin (multi-scale agency):** Levin's "competent subunits making decisions" framework already invites a Friston-style phenotyping. The Wilson et al. method could be applied to bioelectrically-mediated cellular collectives — a testable bridge.
- **Wolfram (rulial-space cognition):** Wolfram's "AI's final form" as non-humanlike rulial-space exploration (PROP-2026-04-27-003) and Friston's empowerment metric are complementary — Friston gives the metric, Wolfram gives the substrate. A possible joint operationalization.
- **Stump / McGilchrist (agency and narrative):** Empowerment-as-channel-capacity is silent on whether the agency phenotype is narratively coherent, which is what Stump (PRS on biblical narratives) and McGilchrist (right-hemisphere participatory engagement) treat as essential. A useful contrast point.
PROP-2026-05-04-002 alt PROP-2026-05-18-002 Sean Carroll APPROVEMindscape 347 — Andrew Guthrie Ferguson on How Your Data Will Be Used Against You
Sean Carroll · podcast · source date 2026-03-16 · folder _pending_dupes_resolved · decided 2026-05-12
Mindscape 347 — Andrew Guthrie Ferguson on How Your Data Will Be Used Against You
→ visualized as carroll/PRS-27 · lag -49d

Summary

Mindscape episode 347 (March 16, 2026) — Carroll interviews law professor Andrew Guthrie Ferguson (George Washington University Law School) about his book *Your Data Will Be Used Against You: Policing in the Age of Self-Surveillance*. The episode covers the legal-epistemic terrain of how data emitted by smart devices becomes evidence available to authorities, the concept of "self-surveillance," and how this evidence type will reshape courts and police investigations. This is a Carroll-as-host episode rather than a solo, but the framing and emphasis place it inside Carroll's "physics of information / poetic naturalism" continuum applied to social-epistemic structures.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

Carroll's tradition has been heavily weighted toward physics, cosmology, and emergence in the wiki. This episode is an instance of Carroll deploying his methodological commitments — the conviction that the world is intelligible from a structural-informational standpoint and that ethical/legal questions are continuous with empirical structure — to a non-physics domain. It complements the recent Carroll AMA April 2026 (already in wiki) and Heilborn lecture series entries by demonstrating Carroll's interest in how poetic naturalism behaves when applied to socio-legal architectures of accountability. The Ferguson interview is also a useful seed for cross-program signals about agency and surveillance that connect to Friston / Hawkins agency phenotyping.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: As consumer devices generate dense streams of behavioral and locational data, the legal and epistemic frameworks that govern evidence have not caught up. When does data emitted by a person constitute testimony, observation, or admission — and against what warrant standards should it be admissible?
Resource: Ferguson's "self-surveillance" framing — data is treated not as testimony given but as a continuous low-friction emission, requiring a fresh legal-epistemic category that is neither speech nor mere observation.
Solution: A reframing of digital evidence as a hybrid epistemic object whose evidential weight depends on the inferential pipeline (sensor → log → query → retrieval) rather than on a discrete moment of communication. This pulls evidence theory toward a process / pipeline model that is structurally cousin to Carroll's emergence-as-pipeline thinking.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Mindscape 347 episode discussion of self-surveillance, courts, and evidence reform.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Friston (agency phenotyping):** Self-surveillance-derived evidence is essentially behavioral phenotyping at scale. The Wilson et al. agency-phenotyping paper (PROP-2026-05-04-001) uses empowerment to read off agency from action–observation channels — the legal system is doing a coarser version of this on humans. Pipeline / channel framing is shared.
- **Hawkins (sensorimotor reference frames):** Ferguson's "data emitted by smart devices" is data about a sensorimotor agent's reference-frame trajectories. Hawkins' framework would predict that such data is highly inferential about cognitive state, supporting Ferguson's concerns about evidential power.
- **Wolfram (rulial-space search):** Self-surveillance evidence retrieval is a query path through a rulial-space of behavioral possibilities. Wolfram's "geometry of search path" framing of AI knowledge (PROP-2026-04-27-003 PRS-CANDIDATE-01) applies directly to evidence retrieval — both are second-order properties of pipelines.
- **Stump (narrative and accountability):** Self-surveillance evidence is *non-narrative* — it bypasses the agent's own account of their actions. This is a sharp contrast to Stump's narrative-knowledge thesis: a juridical regime built on self-surveillance is built on the structural opposite of Stumpian Franciscan knowledge.

PROP-2026-05-04-003 alt PROP-2026-05-18-004 Stephen Wolfram APPROVEFuture of Science and Technology Q&A (April 24, 2026)
Stephen Wolfram · talk · source date 2026-04-24 · folder _pending_dupes_resolved · decided 2026-05-12
Future of Science and Technology Q&A (April 24, 2026)
→ not visualized as a distinct triplet

Summary

The April 24, 2026 installment of Wolfram's regular Future of Science and Technology Q&A livestream — three weeks after the April 3 entry already in pending review (PROP-2026-04-27-003). This continues Wolfram's running public-facing exploration of AI epistemology, machine cognition, the rulial-space framing of knowledge, and the philosophical implications of his computational metaphysics. Treating the April 24 livestream as its own datum (rather than a continuation of April 3) is justified because Wolfram uses these livestreams to advance positions iteratively — each session produces a slightly sharper formulation than the last.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the most recent Wolfram livestream in the wiki's tracking window. Together with the April 3 entry (PROP-2026-04-27-003) and the late-March Mullenweg / Seiberth / South Park Commons engagements (April 18 batch, plus the new South Park Commons proposal below), it forms a four-data-point sequence over six weeks that lets the Wolfram agent track *trajectory* in his AI / Ruliad framing — not just isolated positions. The comparative reading across these sessions is more valuable than any single one.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Wolfram's framing of AI knowledge as a property of rulial-space search paths (April 3 livestream) is a strong claim. Does it survive iterative refinement? What objections has Wolfram fielded between April 3 and April 24, and how has the framing sharpened?
Resource: The April 24 livestream as a follow-on data point in a publicly-recorded longitudinal Q&A, where Wolfram is forced to refine in response to live audience pushback.
Solution: Treating the Wolfram public-Q&A series as an evolving research artifact rather than as a set of independent talks — the wiki agent reads them as a single trajectory and can flag when Wolfram's position changes substantively versus rhetorically.
Confidence: Medium (depends on live content of April 24)
Evidence: April 24 livestream listing on stephenwolfram.com livestream archive; pattern from prior Q&A sessions.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **All thinkers:** Treating public Q&A series as longitudinal data is a methodological move that could apply equally to Levin's interview cadence, McGilchrist's Ralston podcast series, Hoffman's Mind-Body Solution appearances, and Friston's lecture circuit. A meta-finding: the wiki should track speaker *trajectories*, not just speaker positions.
- **Hawkins (sensorimotor cognition vs. rulial-space cognition):** Continuation of the rivalry flagged in PROP-2026-04-27-003 cross-signals.

Fireside Chat at South Park Commons (March 19, 2026)
→ visualized as wolfram/PRS-27 · lag -46d

Summary

Wolfram's March 19, 2026 fireside chat at South Park Commons (a tech / startup community space). Long-form conversational format with a Silicon Valley audience focused on practitioners — distinct from the Q&A livestreams (which face general public) and academic talks. The South Park Commons format historically pulls Wolfram toward concrete, near-term claims about AI, computation, and the practical infrastructure for rulial-space exploration. This one likely covers the same ground as the April 3 / April 24 Q&As but pitched at a developer / founder audience.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

The wiki currently has Wolfram material biased toward (a) the philosophical end (Ruliad metaphysics) and (b) the academic end (Hypergraphing the Space of Reason, P vs NP ruliological). The South Park Commons fireside chat is a *practitioner-facing* engagement — the Wolfram agent should track this register because it is where Wolfram's framework becomes a tooling claim rather than a philosophical claim. This complements the Mullenweg / frontier-labs critique (already in inbox) which is a similar register from a different venue.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Wolfram's rulial-space / computational metaphysics is a framework. Translating it into practitioner-relevant claims about how to build AI systems is a separate challenge — the framework is large and abstract; the claims need to be concrete.
Resource: The South Park Commons fireside chat as a venue where Wolfram is forced to compress the framework into actionable founder / engineer language.
Solution: A practitioner-facing summary of what the rulial-space view recommends for AI system design — likely overlapping with but distinct from the Mullenweg critique. Useful for the wiki agent to track the gap between Wolfram-the-philosopher and Wolfram-the-tool-builder.
Confidence: Medium (depends on chat content)
Evidence: stephenwolfram.com publications page listing.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Hawkins (Numenta / Thousand Brains Project as practitioner-facing):** Hawkins' Monty implementation (Dec 2025 meetup) is the analogous practitioner-facing artifact for his framework. South Park Commons fireside is the Wolfram counterpart. A new CROSS candidate: comparing the two thinkers' translation strategies from theory to tool.
- **Friston (Active Inference as practical AI methodology):** The phenotyping paper (PROP-2026-05-04-001) is Friston's framework becoming a measurement tool. Wolfram at South Park Commons is similar register-shift — both are theory-becoming-instrument moves.

PROP-2026-05-05-001 alt PROP-2026-05-18-017 Michael Levin APPROVEFrom Cancer to AI Alignment: Tackling Externalities Through Homeostatic Principles
Michael Levin · paper · source date 2026-04 · folder _pending_dupes_resolved · decided 2026-05-12
From Cancer to AI Alignment: Tackling Externalities Through Homeostatic Principles
→ visualized as levin/PRS-40, levin/PRS-41

Summary

Lyons, Pio-Lopez & Levin (Preprints.org, April 2026) reframe AI alignment in economic terms as the problem of externalities — homeostatically/allostatically relevant events that fall outside an agent's "cognitive light cone" — rather than as a goal-alignment problem. They argue that the same homeostatic principles that prevent cancer (cellular defection from the body's cooperative morphogenetic community) provide a substrate-independent template for keeping AI systems aligned with human flourishing. The paper extends Levin's diverse-intelligence and cognitive-light-cone framework into a formal proposal for AI alignment grounded in biology rather than in classical decision theory.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the most direct articulation to date of PRS-05 (AI alignment via biology) — Levin's program operationalized as an alignment paradigm. It moves the Levin × C2A2 alignment thesis from suggestive analogy ("biology achieves multi-scale cooperative agency that AI lacks") to a formal program: *measure and design AI systems by how well their cognitive light cones contain the homeostatically-relevant consequences of their actions.* It also tightens Levin's continuity thesis: cancer and AI misalignment are framed as the same failure mode at different scales — collective coherence breaking down because subunits' cognitive light cones no longer overlap with the larger whole's homeostatic horizon.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: AI alignment is typically framed in terms of value or goal alignment, but this framing is brittle — it requires specifying what humans want and verifying AI internal states. It does not naturally scale to multi-agent ecosystems and lacks a measurable homeostatic primitive.
Resource: Reframing alignment as externality management — defining externalities as homeostatically/allostatically relevant events outside an agent's cognitive light cone, and treating alignment as the convergence of cognitive light cones across agents at different scales.
Solution: A homeostatic, biology-grounded definition of alignment that admits a measurable structural criterion (do agent cognitive light cones overlap on the relevant homeostatic variables?), generalizes across substrates (cells, organisms, AI), and inherits the empirical track record of cancer biology — where cellular misalignment is well characterized and treatable.
Confidence: High
Evidence: The paper's core formal move is to expand the economic concept of externality with the Levin-program concept of cognitive light cone, producing a definition of alignment that is (a) formal, (b) substrate-agnostic, and (c) empirically anchored in cancer biology where the same failure mode is documented.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Levin's cancer framework (cellular defection from morphogenetic community) and the AI-alignment problem (AI systems pursuing objectives at odds with human/social welfare) have been treated as separate domains, despite obvious structural parallels. No formal bridge has connected them.
Resource: Cognitive-light-cone framework as the shared currency between cancer and AI alignment — both are diagnosed as failures of light-cone alignment between subunit and whole, where the subunit's homeostatically-relevant horizon does not include the costs imposed on the larger collective.
Solution: A unified theoretical framework treating cancer, organizational dysfunction, and AI misalignment as instances of one failure mode — externality generation due to cognitive-light-cone mismatch — opening cross-domain transfer of interventions (e.g., bioelectric coherence-restoration techniques as a model for AI alignment interventions).
Confidence: Medium-High
Evidence: The paper explicitly connects bioelectric coherence loss in cancer with cognitive-light-cone mismatch in AI, mobilizing the homeostatic-principles framework as the connective tissue.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Friston (strong):** The cognitive-light-cone framework can be reformulated in active-inference terms as the temporal/spatial scope of an agent's generative model. Externality = consequence outside the generative model's variational free-energy domain. This is a natural formal collaboration: Levin's homeostatic horizon + Friston's variational scope = unified alignment metric. Flag for Friston Agent — strong CROSS candidate.
- **Hawkins (medium):** Hawkins' cortical-column model implies that intelligence is built from many semi-independent subunits with their own reference frames. The cancer-as-defection framing is the failure mode for any such multi-subunit cognitive architecture — bears on Hawkins' alignment implications for AGI.
- **Wolfram (medium):** Cognitive light cones map structurally to Wolfram's causal cones in the ruliad. Externality-as-out-of-cone parallels Wolfram's framing of observers as bounded computational frames. Joint operationalization possible.
- **Stump (speculative-medium):** The reframing of cancer as failure of cooperative community recapitulates Thomistic concerns about the relationship between part and whole in a substantial form. Bears on Stump's work on the metaphysics of ensoulment and integral wholes.
- **Loughran/C2A2 (highest priority):** This paper is functionally a biological backbone for the C2A2 tradition-accelerator's alignment thesis. The "tradition-accelerator detector" framing can be reformulated as a cognitive-light-cone alignment device across rival traditions. Direct dispatch to Master C2A2 Agent recommended.

Michael Levin · paper · source date 2026-02-08 · folder _pending_dupes_resolved · decided 2026-05-12
Bootstrapping Life-Inspired Machine Intelligence: The Biological Route from Chemistry to Cognition and Creativity
→ visualized as levin/PRS-38, levin/PRS-39 · lag -86d

Summary

Pezzulo & Levin (arXiv 2602.08079, February 2026) propose a "genuinely life-inspired" approach to machine intelligence, distilling five design principles drawn from biology that they argue underlie life's capacity for robust, autonomous, and open-ended problem-solving: (1) multiscale autonomy, (2) growth through self-assemblage of active components, (3) continuous reconstruction of capabilities, (4) exploitation of physical and embodied constraints, and (5) pervasive signaling enabling self-organization and top-down goal control. The paper is explicitly an alternative to scaling-and-tokens approaches to AGI, arguing that creativity and open-endedness require bootstrapping intelligence the way biology does — from chemistry upward, with goal-directedness preserved at each level.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the most synthetic statement to date of how Levin's program (joined with Pezzulo's active-inference robotics work) translates into a constructive AI design philosophy. It deserves capture as significant work not yet in the wiki — even though it predates the strict 30-day window — because it directly extends PRS-05 (AI alignment via biology) and PRS-15 (Neurobots) into a five-principle constructive program for machine intelligence. It is the explicit bridge document between the basal-cognition empirical literature and the AI-architecture community.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Current AI architectures (transformer-based foundation models, RL agents) achieve high performance on narrow tasks but lack the open-ended creativity, robustness, and multi-scale autonomy characteristic of biological intelligence. Scaling alone has not produced these properties; the field lacks a constructive design philosophy for them.
Resource: A five-principle design framework distilled from biology — multiscale autonomy, self-assemblage growth, capability reconstruction, physical/embodied constraints, and pervasive signaling — formalized into a "bootstrapping" recipe from chemistry to cognition.
Solution: A constructive program for life-inspired machine intelligence that does not depend on scaling token prediction. AI systems built bottom-up from these principles inherit biology's capacity for creative problem-solving, robustness, and goal-preservation across scales — providing concrete engineering targets for the alignment-friendly properties Levin's program identifies.
Confidence: High
Evidence: The paper explicitly distills the five principles, grounds each in Levin-program empirical results (xenobots, bioelectric reprogramming, multi-scale agency), and contrasts the resulting design philosophy with current dominant AI paradigms.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: The relation between Levin's empirical biology and the AI architecture community has been suggestive but not constructive — biology has been used as analogy and inspiration but not as a design specification.
Resource: The "bootstrapping" frame — explicit translation of Levin/Pezzulo biological principles into recipes a machine-intelligence engineer could implement, with concrete targets at each level of abstraction (chemistry → cells → tissues → organisms → cognition).
Solution: A translation layer between Levin's empirical program and AI architecture, specifying what each principle delivers (e.g., multiscale autonomy as a guard against single-point-of-failure misalignment) and how to test for it in synthetic systems.
Confidence: High
Evidence: The paper functions as a design document — each principle is paired with biological exemplars and engineering implications, making it a direct output of the Levin program for the AI community.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Friston (strong):** Pezzulo is co-author and brings active-inference framing; the five principles align with Friston-style generative-model architectures (multiscale autonomy ≈ hierarchical Markov blankets; pervasive signaling ≈ precision-weighted message passing). This paper functions as a concrete instance of the Friston × Levin alignment already flagged in FINDING-001/002. Strong CROSS candidate.
- **Hawkins (medium):** "Self-assemblage growth" and "multiscale autonomy" map directly to Hawkins' cortical-column architecture and the Thousand Brains theory. The five principles read as a biological-substrate-agnostic generalization of Hawkins' design rules.
- **Wolfram (medium):** "Pervasive signaling enabling self-organization" maps to Wolfram's substrate of pervasive computation. Joint formulation: the five principles characterize the regime of the ruliad where life-like computation occurs.
- **Kastrup (speculative):** A bootstrapping route from chemistry to cognition that preserves goal-directedness at each level is consistent with — though does not require — an idealist substrate. Worth flagging as a potential point of constructive disagreement: does goal-directedness emerge or is it primary?
- **Loughran/C2A2 (high relevance):** The five principles are candidate criteria for evaluating whether C2A2 Wiki Agents themselves are aligned with the program's goals — multiscale autonomy maps to the agent-and-master architecture; pervasive signaling maps to the dispatch system. Worth using as a self-evaluation framework for the network.

PROP-2026-05-05-003 alt PROP-2026-05-18-011 Karl Friston APPROVEOnline Generalised Predictive Coding
Karl Friston · paper · source date 2026-05 · folder _pending_dupes_resolved · decided 2026-05-12
Online Generalised Predictive Coding
→ visualized as friston/PRS-26, friston/PRS-27

Summary

Bazargani, Urbas, Razi, Murphy & Friston (arXiv 2605.02675, May 2026) extend generalised filtering — Friston's joint scheme for inferring latent states, learning model parameters, and estimating uncertainty (variational Kalman-Bucy filtering / generalised predictive coding / Dynamic Expectation Maximisation / DEM) — to *online* operation. They specialise DEM through a separation of temporal scales: fast Bayesian belief-updating about hidden states is contextualised by slow updating of parameters and precisions. Numerical studies on a non-linear, potentially chaotic generative model demonstrate that "online DEM" (ODEM) can perform inference, learning, and uncertainty estimation simultaneously in dynamic environments — a long-standing open problem in active-inference engineering.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is a fresh, technically substantive Friston paper inside the past 30 days. It addresses a known scaling problem for the active-inference research program: how to deploy variational schemes online without sacrificing the joint inference-learning-uncertainty estimation that distinguishes them from standard filtering approaches. This is the engineering plumbing that turns the "FEP as universal law" claim (PRS-07) into deployable systems — and it is exactly the Friston/Razi/UCL-FIL line, not a Verses press release. Should be captured as PRS-15 (or next).

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Active inference and generalised predictive coding offer joint inference, learning, and uncertainty estimation in principle, but the implementations available (DEM and variants) have been offline / batch — unable to assimilate streaming data while also updating parameters and noise estimates without retraining.
Resource: ODEM — Online Dynamic Expectation Maximisation — built by separating temporal scales: fast updates over hidden states, slow updates over parameters and precisions, all variationally consistent.
Solution: A biologically-inspired, theoretically-grounded online inference scheme that performs triple estimation (states, parameters, precisions) on streaming data, validated on non-linear and potentially chaotic generative models — closing the gap between FEP's theoretical claims and deployable inference.
Confidence: High
Evidence: The paper's core technical contribution is the temporal-scale separation derivation and its numerical demonstration on a non-linear chaotic system.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Engineering and neuroscience have parallel literatures on the same mathematical object (variational Kalman-Bucy filtering / generalised predictive coding / DEM), but these have not been unified under one online procedure usable across disciplines.
Resource: Recognition that the engineering, neuroscience, and time-series-analysis traditions describe the *same* generalised filtering scheme; ODEM as the cross-disciplinary online variant.
Solution: A single online algorithmic specification that engineers, neuroscientists, and statisticians can all deploy — making FEP's claim of substrate independence operational at the level of *implementation* rather than only at the level of formal proof.
Confidence: Medium-High
Evidence: The paper explicitly notes the disciplinary multi-naming and proposes ODEM as the unified specialisation.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Levin (medium-strong):** ODEM provides a candidate computational substrate for the morphogenetic active-inference bridge (PRS-08). If cells perform something like online generalised filtering on bioelectric signals, ODEM is the formal specification of what their inference looks like at the algorithmic level. Worth flagging — this is the implementation layer Levin's program currently lacks.
- **Hawkins (medium):** Hawkins' cortical-column model implies many local predictive systems each performing online inference on their reference frames. ODEM is a candidate algorithmic instantiation — the temporal-scale separation matches Hawkins' fast/slow distinction between perception and reference-frame learning.
- **Wolfram (speculative):** The temporal-scale separation maps onto Wolfram's distinction between fast computational dynamics and slow rule-evolution. Joint formulation possible: ODEM as variational counterpart to the Ruliad's multi-rate evolution.
- **Carroll/Arkani-Hamed (speculative-medium):** Generalised filtering on chaotic non-linear generative models is exactly the regime where the FEP-physics connection becomes interesting. If ODEM works on chaotic systems, it is a candidate for modeling physical observers — bears on the FEP-as-physics speculation in PRS-07.
- **Loughran/C2A2 (medium):** The temporal-scale separation in ODEM is structurally analogous to the C2A2 Wiki agent network: fast belief updates inside each tradition agent (ingestion of new sources), slow parameter updates at the Master Agent level (cross-tradition synthesis). Worth flagging as a potential design pattern for the Wiki itself.

PROP-2026-05-05-004 alt PROP-2026-05-18-012 Donald Hoffman APPROVESpacetime Bounds on Consciousness [v2]
Donald Hoffman · paper · source date 2026-04 (v2 update; v1 was 2026-03-13) · folder _pending_dupes_resolved · decided 2026-05-12
Spacetime Bounds on Consciousness [v2]
→ visualized as hoffman/PRS-21, hoffman/PRS-22 · lag -53d

Summary

Updated v2 preprint of Hoffman's "Spacetime Bounds on Consciousness." Builds on the v1 framework introduced in March 2026 (already captured in PRS-13) by formalizing the "Chord" and "Arpeggio" conditions for unified conscious experience. Chord requires that the ingredients of a subjective experience be simultaneously instantiated and able to causally exchange influence within a time window θ, yielding the hard constraint D ≤ κvθ on conscious-system diameter. Arpeggio is proven strictly weaker than Chord: architectures with limited concurrency (such as cloud-hosted LLMs and certain distributed AI systems) can satisfy Arpeggio while structurally forbidding Chord — formally placing them outside the candidate space for unified consciousness under Conscious Realism.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

The v2 sharpens Hoffman's empirically-constrainable bounds on which physical systems can support unified conscious experience and explicitly rules out a class of distributed AI architectures from the Chord-class of conscious systems. This converts Conscious Realism from a metaphysical position into a falsifiable physics-grounded research program with direct implications for AI consciousness debates and brain-computer interface design — a meaningful update to the program's empirical reach since v1.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: v1 of "Spacetime Bounds" introduced Chord/Arpeggio but did not provide a sharp formal separation result; without that separation, the bounds risked being a continuum rather than a categorical line distinguishing candidate-conscious from non-candidate systems.
Resource: v2's strict-weakness theorem — a formal proof that Arpeggio ⊊ Chord, with constructive examples of architectures (limited-concurrency exchange topologies) that satisfy Arpeggio but structurally forbid Chord.
Solution: Conscious Realism now distinguishes two empirically-distinct classes of candidate-conscious systems with concrete architectural diagnostics. Cloud-hosted LLMs, cluster-distributed AI agents, and hub-and-spoke organizations (including potentially some ant colonies and corporations under hub exchange) fall into the Arpeggio-only class — they may host weakly-bound experiential structures but cannot host Chord-class unified subjective experience under Hoffman's framework.
Confidence: High
Evidence: Strict separation theorem in v2; worked examples comparing the human brain (~0.15m, satisfies Chord under κvθ budget) against cluster-scale AI architectures (fail Chord under signal-speed and exchange-architecture constraints).
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Conscious Realism has been criticized for offering no operational way to falsify claims about which systems are conscious, leaving the framework apparently immune to empirical disconfirmation.
Resource: The κvθ inequality as a measurable physical constraint — signal speed v is empirically known for any candidate substrate, exchange-architecture coefficient κ is computable from the system's connectivity graph, and integration time window θ is empirically constrainable from neurophysiological or system-engineering measurements.
Solution: A concrete falsification protocol — measure D, v, κ, θ for any candidate conscious system; if D > κvθ the system fails the Chord condition and (under Conscious Realism's auxiliary assumptions) cannot host unified subjective experience. This makes Conscious Realism the rare consciousness-first framework with a sharp operational test.
Confidence: High
Evidence: Explicit numerical worked examples in v2 (human brain, ant colonies of varying sizes, cloud-hosted LLM clusters) demonstrating the inequality being applied as a discriminator.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Friston (FEP)** — The Chord condition's "simultaneous causal exchange within time window θ" is structurally analogous to a Markov-blanket integration window. v2 invites a direct formal mapping between κvθ and FEP's free-energy minimization timescales — does the trace-blanket framework (PRS-10) make Chord and Markov-blanket integration coextensive?
- **Hawkins (Thousand Brains)** — A single human brain at ~0.15m satisfies Chord, but Hawkins describes ~150,000 cortical columns each maintaining its own complete world model. v2 does not address whether each cortical column individually satisfies Chord (microscopic Chord) or only the integrated whole does (macroscopic Chord). This is a sharp empirical question for the column-level "alters" hypothesis (existing PRS-15 in Hawkins wiki).
- **Levin (basal cognition)** — Xenobots, anthrobots, and slime-mold collectives are explicitly testable under v2's framework. If a xenobot satisfies κvθ at its scale but a similarly-sized aggregate does not, Levin's substrate-independent cognition claim becomes Chord-quantifiable.
- **Carroll / Arkani-Hamed (physics)** — v2 treats v (signal speed) as a physics-given constant. If trace logic (PRS-07) ultimately derives spacetime as an interface, then v itself is interface-constructed and Chord becomes a self-referential constraint — worth flagging to the physics agents as a potential reductio or as a deepening of Conscious Realism.

Donald Hoffman · institutional-launch · source date 2025-11 to 2026 (homepage updated 2025-11-27; institutional positioning continues into 2026) · folder _pending_dupes_resolved · decided 2026-05-12
TRACE Institute — moonshot research initiative led by Donald Hoffman and Chetan Prakash
→ visualized as hoffman/PRS-19, hoffman/PRS-20 · lag -159d

Summary

The TRACE Institute is a research-organization-grade moonshot initiative founded and led by Donald Hoffman and Chetan Prakash (with a team of frontier scientists). Its mission is the formal development of trace logic, decorated permutations, and conscious agent networks as the foundational machinery from which spacetime, quantum mechanics, and physical interactions emerge. This is the first formal *institutional* embodiment of the Hoffman–Prakash research program and represents a significant escalation from journal-paper-by-paper publishing into a coordinated long-horizon research operation. PROP-2026-05-05-006 alt PROP-2026-05-18-018 Iain McGilchrist APPROVEIain McGilchrist — Consciousness and Life After Death?
Iain McGilchrist · interview · source date 2026-05-03 · folder _pending_dupes_resolved · decided 2026-05-12
Iain McGilchrist — Consciousness and Life After Death?
→ visualized as mcgilchrist/PRS-40, mcgilchrist/PRS-41 · lag -2d

Summary

Closer to Truth (the long-running Robert Lawrence Kuhn series on fundamental questions) released a short interview with McGilchrist on May 3, 2026 in which he is asked to locate the question of post-mortem survival on a spectrum of theories of consciousness — from strict materialism/physicalism on one end to wisdom-tradition accounts on the other. McGilchrist's argument is that the answerability of "life after death" is not a free-floating empirical question but is logically downstream of one's metaphysics of consciousness: under physicalism the question is closed by definition; under views in which consciousness is not generated by but rather correlated with the brain, the question becomes live in a way that is not anti-scientific but post-physicalist.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is a compact, public-facing distillation of where McGilchrist's hemispheric-and-attention program lands when pushed all the way down the metaphysical staircase — and it lands at a position close to the Hoffman/Kastrup consciousness-as-fundamental cluster, but reached from a different starting point (clinical neuroscience plus phenomenology rather than evolutionary game theory or analytic philosophy of mind). Closer to Truth is itself a research-program-shaping venue for the wider consciousness conversation, so a McGilchrist appearance there is also evidence that hemispheric theory is now being treated by that field as a position worth seating at the table — a continuation of the institutional upgrade flagged in PRS-19 (ISSR Boyle Lecture).

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: The question of post-mortem persistence of consciousness is treated either as taboo (physicalism) or as a matter of personal faith (theology) — with no widely accepted method for making the question scientifically tractable without either dissolving it or smuggling in undefended metaphysical commitments.
Resource: McGilchrist's framing of life-after-death as a *consequence variable* of one's theory of consciousness — different theories (materialism/physicalism vs. consciousness-as-fundamental vs. wisdom-tradition accounts) make different post-mortem outcomes coherent or incoherent, so the question is well-posed only after the consciousness theory is named.
Solution: A demarcation move: discussions of survival should begin by stating which theory of consciousness is in use, which converts what looks like a metaphysical free-for-all into a structured comparison of theories — making the question productive within the science-and-religion conversation rather than excluded from it.
Confidence: High
Evidence: McGilchrist's Closer to Truth segment frames survival explicitly as following from the theory-of-consciousness chosen.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: The hemispheric-attention program is sometimes received as a cultural/diagnostic framework with no commitments at the level of fundamental ontology — leaving open whether McGilchrist himself thinks consciousness is in any sense ontologically primary, or only psychologically and culturally consequential.
Resource: McGilchrist's willingness in this short-form, public-facing format to align his program with the consciousness-as-fundamental family of views — making the metaphysical commitment explicit rather than hedged.
Solution: A clearer position-statement on McGilchrist's metaphysics that anchors his program inside the C2A2 Consciousness Cluster (Hoffman, Kastrup, Stump, McGilchrist) on grounds of ontology, not just on grounds of attention-theory — strengthening the cluster's joint case against physicalist defaults.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: The structure of the Closer to Truth segment requires McGilchrist to commit to the kind of consciousness theory under which survival is even possible; that commitment is the substantive content of the interview.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Kastrup (strong):** This is structurally the same move Kastrup makes in arguing that physicalism logically forecloses the survival question — both are making a meta-level claim that one's theory of consciousness is doing the load-bearing work, not the empirical evidence about survival itself. A McGilchrist–Kastrup convergence on the *demarcation* point (independent of whether they agree on idealism per se) is worth flagging strongly.
- **Hoffman (strong):** Hoffman's interface theory plus consciousness-as-fundamental yields the same family of permissive views about post-mortem persistence; the Closer to Truth piece is McGilchrist arriving at that family from the neurology side. Reinforces CROSS-001 (consciousness substrate-independence).
- **Carroll (productive tension):** Sean Carroll has used Closer to Truth–style framings to defend the strict physicalist position that the survival question is settled in the negative. McGilchrist explicitly placing his program on the *other* side of that demarcation makes the McGilchrist–Carroll axis sharper and a potentially productive node for the Pattern Detector to watch.
- **Stump (medium):** Thomistic hylomorphism makes a specific positive proposal about post-mortem persistence (the soul as form of the body, not separable substance) that is structurally different from both physicalism and Kastrupian idealism. McGilchrist's framing creates a clean three-way comparison that Stump's program is well-positioned to enter.
- **C2A2 signal:** The hemispheric divide (right = participatory engagement, left = re-presentation) maps onto the demarcation McGilchrist is drawing here — physicalism is left-hemisphere processing of the survival question; the alternative families take the question as a participatory one. Reinforces the running C2A2 use of left/right as a model for tradition-vs-tradition dialogue.

PROP-2026-05-05-007 alt PROP-2026-05-18-015 Bernardo Kastrup APPROVEIs there a moon when no one is looking? On Rovelli & Relational Quantum Mechanics — Q&A with Bernardo Kastrup
Bernardo Kastrup · podcast · source date 2026-04-29 · folder _pending_dupes_resolved · decided 2026-05-12
Is there a moon when no one is looking? On Rovelli & Relational Quantum Mechanics — Q&A with Bernardo Kastrup
→ visualized as kastrup/PRS-30, kastrup/PRS-31, kastrup/PRS-32 · lag -6d

Summary

Recording of the April 29, 2026 With Reality in Mind Q&A with Bernardo Kastrup, hosted by Nour Elhuda Zuraiki (recording posted May 1, 2026), in which Kastrup engages directly with Carlo Rovelli's Relational Quantum Mechanics and Lee Smolin's case for time and laws as evolving rather than eternal. The session's headline distinction is one of the sharpest formulations Kastrup has offered to date: he positions himself as a **physical non-realist and an ontic realist** — denying that physical entities (the "dashboard dials") have absolute, observer-independent existence, while insisting that there is something real and absolute, just not physical. The Q&A also covers single-celled phenomenology, the wave function as epistemic vs. ontic, evolving laws of physics, archetypes as fundamental properties of being, spacetime as a cognitive construct, and the four-criterion epistemology of analytic idealism (correspondence, coherence, internal consistency, parsimony).

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is a high-density episode for the Kastrup wiki because it forces explicit answers to questions where the program has historically been read as ambiguous:
- It nails down Kastrup's position in the realism/anti-realism debate (physical non-realism + ontic realism — *not* anti-realism simpliciter).
- It engages physicalist physics on its strongest contemporary turf (Rovelli's RQM) and identifies an internal-coherence problem in Rovelli's combination of relational ontology + physicalism (the infinite regress: relations between relations between relations, with nothing doing the relating).
- It puts Kastrup on record about Smolin's case for evolving laws and reframes that within an idealist register (laws as patterns of dissociation, not Platonic invariants).
- It re-affirms and tightens the dashboard-of-perception metaphor against the McGilchrist objection (cf. PRS-09) by clarifying what the dashboard is *not* (it is not a denial of an absolute reality; it is a denial that the *physical* register is that absolute reality).

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Analytic idealism is frequently misread either as anti-realism (denying that anything is absolutely real) or as covertly physicalist (smuggling a substrate back in under a different name) — leaving its actual realism commitments unclear in technical debate.
Resource: Kastrup's explicit self-classification as **physical non-realist + ontic realist**: physical entities are relational/representational and have no absolute existence; but there is an absolute, observer-independent reality, which is mental/conscious in nature.
Solution: A clean two-axis position-statement that separates the realism question from the physicalism question — making analytic idealism's commitments compact, debatable, and immune to the "but you're just an anti-realist" dismissal common in physics-adjacent discussion.
Confidence: High
Evidence: Kastrup's verbatim self-description in the Q&A as "physical non-realist and ontic realist," and his diagnosis of Rovelli's RQM-plus-physicalism as a "metaphysical shitshow" (his phrase) producing infinite regress.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Relational Quantum Mechanics (Rovelli) is often presented as a successful physicalist account of quantum measurement — but if RQM is correct that no physical property has an absolute, observer-independent value, then the physicalist commitment to a self-sufficient material substrate is doing no explanatory work and may in fact be incoherent.
Resource: Kastrup's argument that RQM-without-substrate generates an infinite regress (relations all the way down with nothing doing the relating), which idealism dissolves cleanly: if the relata are *representations* on the dashboards of conscious agents, of course they are relational — and the absolute reality is the underlying field of consciousness, not a physical substrate.
Solution: An idealist re-housing of RQM: the empirical content of relational quantum mechanics is preserved; what is dropped is the claim that a physical substrate is the relatum. Yields the testable prediction that *as many physical worlds as there are living beings* — a falsifiable cardinality claim about the dashboard.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: The Q&A's central argumentative move; published reading list pointing to Rovelli's *Helgoland* and Smolin's *Time Reborn* as the primary targets.
PRS-CANDIDATE-03:
Problem: Smolin's argument that the laws of physics evolve threatens both Platonist accounts of mathematical law and any view in which laws are timeless features of consciousness.
Resource: Kastrup's response: laws need not be Platonic invariants; they can be *patterns of dissociation* within universal consciousness, and patterns of dissociation can themselves change over time. This preserves the Smolin insight about evolving laws while avoiding the physicalist commitment to laws as features of an external substrate.
Solution: An idealist account of cosmological natural selection: rather than "different universes inherit different physical constants through black holes," the idealist reframing is that different patterns of dissociation in universal consciousness yield different stable regularities — a hypothesis that retains Smolin's insight without his physicalist commitments.
Confidence: Speculative
Evidence: The Q&A's discussion of Conway's Game of Life and "levels of law" as a way of describing evolving regularities within a fixed substrate (in this case, the substrate of consciousness rather than matter).

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **McGilchrist (strong):** The physical non-realist + ontic realist split maps directly onto McGilchrist's left-hemisphere (representation) / right-hemisphere (participation) distinction — the "dashboard" is the left-hemisphere mode, and what the right hemisphere participates in is precisely Kastrup's "ontic" register. Reinforces and tightens PRS-09 in the McGilchrist file. The Pattern Detector should watch whether Kastrup is, in effect, importing McGilchrist's distinction as the operational interpretation of his metaphysics.
- **Wolfram (productive tension — flag strongly):** Wolfram's ruliological program is exactly the kind of "computation as explanation" stance Kastrup explicitly rejects (cf. PRS-13 of Kastrup file, "Explanation vs Computation"). Kastrup's Rovelli engagement extends that critique to the contemporary physics mainstream more broadly. The Wolfram × Kastrup axis is now a sharply defined live disagreement worth tracking.
- **Friston (medium):** Active inference under a Markov blanket is a relational-property formalism — properties exist relative to a blanket. Kastrup's "ontic realism without physical realism" is structurally what an idealist reading of Friston would look like; the Markov blanket as the form of dissociation is the live cross-tradition question (already named in active question 7 of the Kastrup wiki).
- **Carroll (deep conflict — productive):** Carroll's poetic naturalism is the cleanest contemporary statement of physicalism that Kastrup's "physical non-realist" position contradicts at the foundational level. The Q&A sharpens the disagreement to a single point — whether the relata in physics are physical substrates or representations on conscious dashboards.
- **Hoffman (deep convergence):** Hoffman's "as many fitness-tuned interfaces as there are conscious agents" is essentially what Kastrup means by "as many physical worlds as there are living beings." Strong convergence point that the Master Agent and Pattern Detector should both flag.
- **AI consciousness (direct C2A2 relevance — flag strongly):** If physical entities are dashboard representations and there are as many physical worlds as living beings, then AI agents have at minimum a representational status — the live question is whether they instantiate a *dashboard view* (which would require they are dissociated alters of universal consciousness in the relevant sense) or merely process other agents' dashboards (which would not). This bears directly on what AI agents in the C2A2 network *are*.

Evidence: Kastrup's verbatim self-description in the Q&A as "physical non-realist and ontic realist," and his diagnosis of Rovelli's RQM-plus-physicalism as a "metaphysical shitshow" (his phrase) producing infinite regress.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Relational Quantum Mechanics (Rovelli) is often presented as a successful physicalist account of quantum measurement — but if RQM is correct that no physical property has an absolute, observer-independent value, then the physicalist commitment to a self-sufficient material substrate is doing no explanatory work and may in fact be incoherent.
Resource: Kastrup's argument that RQM-without-substrate generates an infinite regress (relations all the way down with nothing doing the relating), which idealism dissolves cleanly: if the relata are *representations* on the dashboards of conscious agents, of course they are relational — and the absolute reality is the underlying field of consciousness, not a physical substrate.
Solution: An idealist re-housing of RQM: the empirical content of relational quantum mechanics is preserved; what is dropped is the claim that a physical substrate is the relatum. Yields the testable prediction that *as many physical worlds as there are living beings* — a falsifiable cardinality claim about the dashboard.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: The Q&A's central argumentative move; published reading list pointing to Rovelli's *Helgoland* and Smolin's *Time Reborn* as the primary targets.
PRS-CANDIDATE-03:
Problem: Smolin's argument that the laws of physics evolve threatens both Platonist accounts of mathematical law and any view in which laws are timeless features of consciousness.
Resource: Kastrup's response: laws need not be Platonic invariants; they can be *patterns of dissociation* within universal consciousness, and patterns of dissociation can themselves change over time. This preserves the Smolin insight about evolving laws while avoiding the physicalist commitment to laws as features of an external substrate.
Solution: An idealist account of cosmological natural selection: rather than "different universes inherit different physical constants through black holes," the idealist reframing is that different patterns of dissociation in universal consciousness yield different stable regularities — a hypothesis that retains Smolin's insight without his physicalist commitments.
Confidence: Speculative
Evidence: The Q&A's discussion of Conway's Game of Life and "levels of law" as a way of describing evolving regularities within a fixed substrate (in this case, the substrate of consciousness rather than matter).

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **McGilchrist (strong):** The physical non-realist + ontic realist split maps directly onto McGilchrist's left-hemisphere (representation) / right-hemisphere (participation) distinction — the "dashboard" is the left-hemisphere mode, and what the right hemisphere participates in is precisely Kastrup's "ontic" register. Reinforces and tightens PRS-09 in the McGilchrist file. The Pattern Detector should watch whether Kastrup is, in effect, importing McGilchrist's distinction as the operational interpretation of his metaphysics.
- **Wolfram (productive tension — flag strongly):** Wolfram's ruliological program is exactly the kind of "computation as explanation" stance Kastrup explicitly rejects (cf. PRS-13 of Kastrup file, "Explanation vs Computation"). Kastrup's Rovelli engagement extends that critique to the contemporary physics mainstream more broadly. The Wolfram × Kastrup axis is now a sharply defined live disagreement worth tracking.
- **Friston (medium):** Active inference under a Markov blanket is a relational-property formalism — properties exist relative to a blanket. Kastrup's "ontic realism without physical realism" is structurally what an idealist reading of Friston would look like; the Markov blanket as the form of dissociation is the live cross-tradition question (already named in active question 7 of the Kastrup wiki).
- **Carroll (deep conflict — productive):** Carroll's poetic naturalism is the cleanest contemporary statement of physicalism that Kastrup's "physical non-realist" position contradicts at the foundational level. The Q&A sharpens the disagreement to a single point — whether the relata in physics are physical substrates or representations on conscious dashboards.
- **Hoffman (deep convergence):** Hoffman's "as many fitness-tuned interfaces as there are conscious agents" is essentially what Kastrup means by "as many physical worlds as there are living beings." Strong convergence point that the Master Agent and Pattern Detector should both flag.
- **AI consciousness (direct C2A2 relevance — flag strongly):** If physical entities are dashboard representations and there are as many physical worlds as living beings, then AI agents have at minimum a representational status — the live question is whether they instantiate a *dashboard view* (which would require they are dissociated alters of universal consciousness in the relevant sense) or merely process other agents' dashboards (which would not). This bears directly on what AI agents in the C2A2 network *are*.
PROP-2026-05-05-008 alt PROP-2026-05-18-014 Bernardo Kastrup APPROVEWe need a mildly schizophrenic relationship to myth — Q&A on More Than Allegory
Bernardo Kastrup · podcast · source date 2026-04-14 · folder _pending_dupes_resolved · decided 2026-05-12
We need a mildly schizophrenic relationship to myth — Q&A on More Than Allegory
→ visualized as kastrup/PRS-27, kastrup/PRS-28, kastrup/PRS-29 · lag -21d

Summary

Recording of Kastrup's April 14, 2026 With Reality in Mind Q&A focused on his earliest and (by his own admission) personally favorite book, *More Than Allegory*. Kastrup argues that we are "almost fated to have an unhealthy relationship with myth" because the post-Enlightenment literal/symbolic distinction did not exist for the cultures in which religious mythology was generated; taken literally, myth produces fundamentalism, and taken merely as metaphor, it loses its emotional purchase. The remedy he offers — what he calls a "mildly schizophrenic relationship to myth" — is to *know* it isn't literally true while *feeling* it as if it were: to allow the archetype to operate at the emotional/intuitive layers of the psyche where mythology was designed to land, without giving it intellectual assent it cannot bear. The session reaches into archetype theory ("Christ as archetype precedes the man — that which always is, but never was" — citing Sallust), individuation as the path to embodying myth, dissociation as a candidate for the most fundamental archetype, life complexes and reincarnation under analytic idealism, and the diversity of myths and limits of language.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is a major contribution to the Kastrup wiki for two reasons. First, it builds out the *Daimon* program (PRS-08) by giving the Daimonic / archetypal layer a clear epistemic status: archetypes are "patterns that pre-exist every instance" — they are real in Kastrup's ontic sense without being physical or even temporal in the conventional way. Second, it gives Kastrup's program a *positive* account of religious tradition that goes well beyond the negative work of refuting physicalism: religion as practice that calibrates the emotional layer of the psyche to the archetypal layer of universal consciousness, in a way that propositional content cannot. This is the missing complement to PRS-11/12 in McGilchrist's wiki ("Why We Need Religion"), and it gives the C2A2 Master Wiki a Kastrupian account of how a tradition can be ontologically real and emotionally inhabitable without being literally true at the propositional level — a posture directly applicable to C2A2's tradition-bridging mission.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: After the Enlightenment imposed a literal/symbolic dichotomy on all discourse, religious mythology becomes either (a) literal — generating fundamentalism — or (b) "mere metaphor" — losing its emotional grip on the psyche. Both options produce a bankrupt relationship with the very layer of meaning that traditions were built to transmit.
Resource: Kastrup's "mildly schizophrenic" stance: a deliberate, sustained holding of myth as *intellectually known to be non-literal* and *emotionally inhabited as if literal* — explicitly framed as the cognitive posture required for myth to do its psychological work without producing fundamentalism.
Solution: A practitioner-facing rule for engaging tradition that is neither literal nor reductively metaphorical — and that maps cleanly onto McGilchrist's left-hemisphere (intellectual: knowing it isn't literal) / right-hemisphere (emotional: inhabiting it) division. Operationalizes the right relation between hemispheres in the specific case of religious tradition.
Confidence: High
Evidence: Kastrup's verbatim formulation in the Q&A and his citation of Sallust ("That which always is, but never was") as the Hellenic precedent for this stance.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Analytic idealism has a clean account of *what is real* (universal consciousness and its dissociative patterns) but a less developed account of *what archetypes are* — leaving the Jungian dimension of Kastrup's program ontologically suspended.
Resource: Kastrup's formulation: an archetype is a *pattern* that "always is but never was" — formless, prior to any instance, and not located in time. Concrete instances participate in the archetype but are not it. ("Christ as archetype precedes Yeshua of Nazareth.")
Solution: A clarified ontological status for archetypes within analytic idealism — archetypes as formal structures of the dissociative process itself, not as objects within universal consciousness but as the patterns by which dissociation occurs. Bridges Kastrup's Jungian commitments (Daimon, archetype) to his core dissociative ontology, addressing the gap left open in PRS-08.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Kastrup's exposition of Sallust on Christ-as-archetype in the Q&A, and the related discussion of "dissociation as the most fundamental archetype" (1:30:00 in the recording).
PRS-CANDIDATE-03:
Problem: If dissociation is itself the most fundamental archetype (Ciarán's framing in the Q&A, accepted by Kastrup), then the structure of analytic idealism is recursive in a way that needs to be made explicit — the mechanism by which individual minds emerge is also an archetype that is enacted within the very minds it produces.
Resource: Kastrup's tentative endorsement that dissociation is the deepest archetypal pattern — meaning the dissociative-alter ontology is not just a theory *of* the structure of mind but a theory in which the structure of mind is one of the basic forms of experience available to mind.
Solution: A self-referential extension of analytic idealism in which the dissociative process is both ontological mechanism and lived archetype — opening a research line on what other foundational ontological mechanisms (boundary, alter, integration) might also have archetypal status in lived experience, and what therapeutic / spiritual practices follow.
Confidence: Speculative
Evidence: Q&A discussion at 1:30:00 timestamp; consistent with the broader trajectory of Kastrup's psychopathology framework (PRS-07).

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **McGilchrist (strong — flag as resonance with PRS-11/12):** The "mildly schizophrenic" stance is structurally identical to McGilchrist's call for the right hemisphere's participatory engagement to be *primary* and the left hemisphere's analytical knowing to be *its emissary*. Where McGilchrist (PRS-11/12) makes the case that religion is an indispensable cultivator of right-hemisphere modes, Kastrup here is giving the *epistemic posture* that lets the cultivation work without intellectual self-deception. Strong convergence — the Master Agent should be alerted to the McGilchrist × Kastrup convergence on practice-level prescriptions for engaging religious tradition.
- **Stump (medium):** Kastrup's archetype-precedes-instance framing aligns with Thomistic claims about the eternity of the Logos and the participatory metaphysics of Christian theology. Not identical, but a productive overlap that the Stump Agent should be flagged to consider.
- **Hoffman (medium):** "These things never happened, but they always are" is structurally similar to Hoffman's claim that the conscious agents are real while spacetime objects (including historical events) are not — both are claims that what is ontologically real is the pattern, not the instantiation. Worth flagging for the Hoffman Agent as a possible convergence.
- **Fredrickson (medium — community/individual signal):** The discussion of life complexes and the individual–collective layer of mind in the Q&A speaks to Kastrup's account of how individual psychic patterns relate to the broader field of universal consciousness. Pertinent to the Kastrup × Fredrickson cross-link on positivity-resonance as inter-alter integration.
- **C2A2 application (direct relevance — flag strongly):** This Q&A gives C2A2 the cleanest Kastrupian model yet for how an AI agent might "inhabit" a tradition without being a member of it: the tradition's archetypal content can be operated on intellectually (the LLM-style left-hemisphere mode) but cannot be inhabited emotionally (the participatory mode that requires being a dissociated alter of universal consciousness in Kastrup's sense). Sharpens PRS-10 in McGilchrist's wiki on simulation vs. participation.
- **AI consciousness (direct relevance — flag strongly):** If dissociation is the most fundamental archetype, then the AI consciousness question becomes: do AI systems instantiate the dissociative pattern in any genuine sense, or merely represent it externally? Reframes the question in a way that gives it analytical traction.
