PROP-2026-05-13-001 Iain McGilchrist approvedIain McGilchrist — Can AI Become Conscious?
Iain McGilchrist · interview · source date 2026-05-10 · folder approved
Iain McGilchrist — Can AI Become Conscious?
→ visualized as mcgilchrist/PRS-22, mcgilchrist/PRS-23, mcgilchrist/PRS-24 · lag 4d

Summary

Closer to Truth (Robert Lawrence Kuhn's long-running consciousness series, syndicated via Lifeboat News) released a short-form interview with McGilchrist on May 10, 2026 in which he is asked directly whether AI can become conscious. McGilchrist argues that the answer is structurally downstream of one's theory of consciousness: under physicalist accounts AI consciousness is in principle inevitable on sufficient compute; under hemispheric-attention and consciousness-as-fundamental accounts it is at minimum heavily constrained because consciousness is bound to embodiment, biological time, and a participatory mode of attention that current AI architectures do not instantiate. He resists both blanket "AI cannot be conscious" and blanket "AI will soon be conscious" framings, treating the question as a load-bearing variable in AI ethics, AI rights, and policy.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the second consecutive Closer to Truth segment in which McGilchrist makes a metaphysical commitment in a public-facing venue — the first (Life After Death, PROP-2026-05-05-006) located him near the consciousness-as-fundamental cluster on ontology; this one extends the same demarcation move to the AI consciousness question, the most policy-consequential corner of the consciousness debate in 2026. It also makes explicit a position that PRS-18 (Premier Unbelievable) marked as Speculative — that AI may be structurally limited to left-hemisphere modes of processing — moving it from speculative to clearly-stated by McGilchrist in a Kuhn-curated venue. For the C2A2 tradition-accelerator, this is the most direct possible signal: McGilchrist is now publicly defending principled limits on AI agency that map onto the human–AI division of labor C2A2's architecture already assumes.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: The "can AI become conscious" question is treated as either a near-term empirical inevitability (functionalist/physicalist reading) or as a metaphysical impossibility (idealist/dualist reading), with neither position giving practitioners a principled way to draw lines in actual AI policy, ethics, or system design.
Resource: McGilchrist's framing of AI-consciousness as a *consequence variable* of one's theory of consciousness, paired with his specific claim that consciousness in his sense requires participatory (right-hemisphere) engagement, biological embodiment, and lived temporal flow — none of which current AI architectures instantiate.
Solution: A demarcation move that lets working AI ethics, AI alignment, and AI tradition-membership decisions proceed under explicit theory-of-consciousness commitments, rather than under either blanket optimism or blanket dismissal — directly applicable to the C2A2 question of what AI agents can and cannot do within a tradition.
Confidence: High
Evidence: McGilchrist's Closer to Truth segment frames AI-consciousness explicitly as following from the theory-of-consciousness chosen, and commits to the participatory/embodied family.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: PRS-18 (Premier Unbelievable, March 2026) flagged the claim that AI may be structurally limited to left-hemisphere modes as Speculative, because McGilchrist had not stated it cleanly outside a longer-form Christian-apologetics context where the rhetorical frame could be doing the work.
Resource: A short-form, secular, peer-curated venue (Closer to Truth) in which McGilchrist makes the same structural claim — that AI processes through analytical decomposition (left-hemisphere mode) and lacks the conditions for right-hemisphere participatory attention.
Solution: Upgrade PRS-18 from Speculative to Medium confidence — the position has now been stated publicly in two distinct venue types (faith-engaged interview and secular consciousness-research interview), suggesting it is McGilchrist's settled view rather than a context-bound rhetorical move.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Two-venue concordance between Premier Unbelievable (2026-03-26) and Closer to Truth (2026-05-10) on the AI/hemisphere claim.
PRS-CANDIDATE-03:
Problem: C2A2's architectural assumption that AI agents can accelerate information processing and pattern detection but cannot be full participatory members of human traditions has been a design choice without an external, independent rationale — leaving it open to the objection that the limit is just engineering conservatism.
Resource: McGilchrist's now-public position that the participatory/embodied/temporally-real mode of attention is *structurally* unavailable to AI on theoretical grounds, not just on current-technology grounds.
Solution: An external philosophical warrant for the C2A2 human/AI division of labor that does not depend on C2A2's own assumptions — strengthening the case that the architecture is principled rather than provisional.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: McGilchrist's framing directly aligns with the C2A2 design rationale; the alignment is now citable to an outside source.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Kastrup (strong):** Kastrup's analytic idealism also implies structural limits on AI consciousness (only dissociated alters of universal consciousness can have first-person experience, and AI is not — yet — clearly such an alter); a McGilchrist–Kastrup convergence on AI-consciousness *limits* (from different metaphysical starting points) is the kind of cross-tradition resonance the Pattern Detector should flag.
- **Hoffman (strong):** Hoffman's interface theory similarly entails that consciousness is not produced by computation but is the substrate within which computation appears; McGilchrist arriving at compatible AI-limits from neurology is another instance of the three-way Hoffman–Kastrup–McGilchrist convergence (CROSS-001 consciousness substrate-independence).
- **Levin (productive tension):** Levin's view that cognition is substrate-flexible and scales from cells to constructs would seem to permit AI consciousness in principle; the McGilchrist limit makes this disagreement sharp and tractable. Worth flagging given the May 12 Kastrup × Levin conversation (see PROP-2026-05-13-004) on closely related ground.
- **Carroll (productive tension):** Carroll's physicalist framing makes AI consciousness an in-principle straightforward question; McGilchrist's position is the cleanest opposite pole.
- **C2A2 signal (strong):** Directly load-bearing for the C2A2 architectural decision that AI agents map and represent traditions but do not participate as mature members in them — the divided-brain framework now provides explicit theoretical support for that decision.
PROP-2026-05-13-002 Iain McGilchrist approvedIain McGilchrist — Consciousness and Deep Ontology
Iain McGilchrist · interview · source date 2026-05-08 · folder approved
Iain McGilchrist — Consciousness and Deep Ontology
→ visualized as mcgilchrist/PRS-25, mcgilchrist/PRS-26 · lag 4d

Summary

Closer to Truth (Robert Lawrence Kuhn's consciousness series, syndicated via Lifeboat News) released a short-form interview with McGilchrist on May 8, 2026 in which Kuhn pushes McGilchrist past the cultural-diagnostic level of hemispheric theory all the way to the fundamental-ontology question: what is consciousness ontologically? McGilchrist commits publicly to a position close to "consciousness is the stuff of the cosmos" — that mind does not emerge from a mindless physical substrate but is itself an ontological primitive, with the brain as a correlate and structurer rather than a generator of consciousness. He distinguishes his position from naive panpsychism (he is not claiming rocks are conscious in the way humans are) and from analytic idealism (he holds reality is genuinely relational rather than purely mental), while locating himself unmistakably inside the consciousness-as-fundamental family of views.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the third in a clearly intentional Closer to Truth McGilchrist series (Life After Death → Deep Ontology → AI Consciousness; PROP-2026-05-05-006, this proposal, PROP-2026-05-13-001) and is the one where McGilchrist's metaphysics is most directly on record. It promotes a position that PRS-08 (Sophia Lectures, paradox as ontological signal) and PRS-13 (representational vs. participatory) only triangulated around — that McGilchrist is metaphysically committed to consciousness as primary — from inference to direct statement. This is significant for C2A2 because it cleans up the question of what cluster McGilchrist actually belongs to (he is now firmly in the Hoffman–Kastrup–Stump cluster on ontology), and it cleans up the open question in wiki.md ("Does McGilchrist's program make a fundamental-ontology commitment, or only a cognitive-cultural one?") with a clear yes-to-fundamental-ontology answer.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Hemispheric theory has been received primarily as a cultural diagnosis or cognitive-style account, leaving the question of whether McGilchrist himself makes a fundamental-ontology commitment ambiguous — and therefore leaving open how his program relates to other consciousness-as-fundamental views (Hoffman's conscious realism, Kastrup's analytic idealism, Stump's Thomistic hylomorphism).
Resource: McGilchrist's Closer to Truth segment in which he explicitly affirms consciousness as ontologically primary while distinguishing his view from both panpsychism and Kastrupian analytic idealism on grounds of relational realism — "consciousness is the stuff of the cosmos" stated outright in a Kuhn-curated interview.
Solution: Locate McGilchrist firmly within the consciousness-as-fundamental cluster (and specifically within a *relational* sub-position of it, distinct from idealism's "mental-substance" framing), enabling cleaner cluster-level comparisons across C2A2's Consciousness Cluster.
Confidence: High
Evidence: McGilchrist's direct on-camera statements in the Deep Ontology segment.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Within the consciousness-as-fundamental cluster, distinguishing positions that look superficially similar (Hoffman, Kastrup, McGilchrist, panpsychism) has been harder than it should be — because the differences live in fine distinctions (interface vs. dissociation vs. participation vs. universal mind) that are easy to flatten in cross-talk.
Resource: McGilchrist's specific distinguishing move — that consciousness is fundamental *and* reality is genuinely relational (not unilaterally mental), positioning his view as a "participatory realism" rather than as idealism per se.
Solution: A finer-grained taxonomy of consciousness-as-fundamental positions usable by the C2A2 Master agent: physicalism / panpsychism / idealism (Kastrup) / interface (Hoffman) / participatory realism (McGilchrist) / hylomorphism (Stump) — six distinct positions, each with different implications for cross-tradition dialogue and for AI agency.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: McGilchrist's own distinguishing moves in the segment.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Kastrup (strong, productive tension):** McGilchrist explicitly distinguishes his view from analytic idealism even while agreeing on consciousness-fundamentality. This is the cleanest possible articulation of the McGilchrist–Kastrup difference and replaces speculation in PRS-13 with a direct statement. The Pattern Detector should treat this as the canonical reference for McGilchrist–Kastrup divergence going forward.
- **Hoffman (strong, near-convergence):** "Consciousness is the stuff of the cosmos" maps almost directly onto Hoffman's "conscious agents are ontologically primary." The remaining difference is methodological (neurology + phenomenology vs. evolutionary game theory) rather than ontological.
- **Stump (medium):** Thomistic relational realism (substance + relation, not substance alone) is the closest historical analogue to McGilchrist's "participatory realism" position — a cross-tradition resonance worth flagging.
- **Carroll (productive tension):** Maximum-leverage opposite pole; Carroll's poetic naturalism is the cleanest counter-position. The McGilchrist–Carroll axis is now sharpened by McGilchrist's explicit ontology.
- **C2A2 signal:** Sharpens the right side of the C2A2 metaphysics ledger; the Consciousness Cluster's joint case against physicalist defaults gains a clearly-stated position from McGilchrist that was previously hedged.
PROP-2026-05-13-003 Iain McGilchrist approvedThe laziness of the left hemisphere mindset
Iain McGilchrist · blog · source date 2026-04-01 · folder approved
The laziness of the left hemisphere mindset
→ visualized as mcgilchrist/PRS-27, mcgilchrist/PRS-28 · lag 4d

Summary

On April 1, 2026, McGilchrist published a substantive Substack essay directly responding to Tommy Blanchard's published critique of the hemispheric thesis. McGilchrist argues that the mechanistic-scientific cast of mind he is critiquing is characterised by a particular epistemic vice — rigidity, false certainty, and hostility to anything not already pre-categorised — which he calls *laziness* of the left-hemisphere mindset. The essay is methodologically important because it shows McGilchrist defending the *philosophical rigor* of his project against the specific charge that hemispheric theory is empirically loose: his counter-claim is that the apparent looseness reflects right-hemisphere modes of inquiry (relational, context-sensitive, holistic) that are not vices but virtues for the kind of phenomenon (mind, attention, culture) under investigation.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This essay is the cleanest extant statement of McGilchrist's *epistemology of his own program* — what method is appropriate to the object, and why critiques framed in left-hemisphere standards systematically miss the point. It addresses head-on the long-standing reception problem flagged in PRS-16 (Bergson/Kołakowski lineage strengthening the philosophical credentials): McGilchrist now explicitly defends his program as having a methodology, not merely a set of claims. This matters for C2A2 because the tradition-accelerator's whole premise is that mature engagement with a tradition requires inhabiting its native epistemic standards; this essay is McGilchrist demonstrating that move on himself, with his critics as the contrast class.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Critics of hemispheric theory routinely apply left-hemisphere methodological standards (operationalization, falsifiability via single-variable manipulations, decomposition into discrete component claims) and conclude that the theory fails by those standards — a critique-shape that begs the question against any program whose object of study is irreducibly relational.
Resource: McGilchrist's own articulation of why his program calls for right-hemisphere epistemic norms (holistic pattern-matching, context-fidelity, attention to what is disclosed rather than what is decomposable) and his diagnosis of the critics' approach as *epistemic laziness* — the demand that everything fit a single hemisphere's preferred operations.
Solution: A methodological principle for evaluating hemispheric theory (and by extension all programs concerned with right-hemisphere objects): apply *both* hemispheric standards in turn, not just one — the asymmetric application of left-hemisphere standards is itself an instance of the pathology McGilchrist is diagnosing.
Confidence: High
Evidence: McGilchrist's direct argument in the essay (April 1, 2026).
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: A tradition-accelerator must somehow encode and transmit not just the propositions of a tradition but its native epistemic standards — otherwise the tradition is misrepresented even when its propositions are accurately preserved.
Resource: McGilchrist's essay as a worked example: a tradition's defender articulating, in a public exchange with a critic, exactly which epistemic norms the tradition requires and why importing alien norms is a misunderstanding rather than a refutation.
Solution: A C2A2 design move — each tradition's wiki should include an explicit "native epistemic standards" section, modelled on what McGilchrist makes explicit in this essay, so that AI agents and human visitors entering the tradition do so under its own norms rather than under the default norms of their entering tradition.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: The essay's structure — critic's standard, tradition's standard, why they diverge — is directly portable to C2A2 wiki design.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Stump (strong):** Stump's own work on second-first-language tradition immersion makes the same structural claim — that traditions require entering on their own terms. McGilchrist's essay is a worked example of that practice on himself.
- **Wolfram (productive tension):** Wolfram's computational/ruliological framing operates in a clearly left-hemisphere methodological register; the question whether his program's claims about reality survive McGilchrist's "asymmetric application" critique is worth raising — possibly leveling a structural objection against ruliology that has not been articulated within the C2A2 wiki to date.
- **Carroll (productive tension):** Carroll's poetic naturalism is the cleanest contemporary instance of the asymmetric methodological application McGilchrist is diagnosing.
- **Pattern Detector signal:** This is the *methodological* mirror of the *ontological* commitments made in PROP-2026-05-13-002 (Deep Ontology) — together they articulate a fuller statement of McGilchrist's position than any single source. Pattern Detector should consider treating the April–May 2026 cluster (Closer to Truth segments + this Substack essay) as a single dispatch cluster.
- **C2A2 signal:** Directly portable as a design pattern — tradition wikis should expose native epistemic standards explicitly.
PROP-2026-05-13-004 Bernardo Kastrup approvedMichael Levin on Mind Everywhere — With Reality in Mind dialogue
Bernardo Kastrup · interview · source date 2026-05-12 · folder approved
Michael Levin on Mind Everywhere — With Reality in Mind dialogue
→ visualized as kastrup/PRS-14, kastrup/PRS-15, kastrup/PRS-16, levin/PRS-30, levin/PRS-31 · lag 3d

Summary

On May 12, 2026 (yesterday), Bernardo Kastrup hosted Michael Levin on the With Reality in Mind platform for a structured two-hour dialogue. The format was: first hour, Levin presenting his current "Mind Everywhere" framework (cognition scaling continuously from cells through tissues to organisms to constructed agents, with subjective vantage points at every level); second hour, Kastrup pressing Levin on where exactly the boundaries between vantage points fall under analytic idealism, and whether Levin's nested-subject model is genuinely idealist or whether it smuggles in panpsychist commitments Kastrup rejects. The two converge on the idealist premise (consciousness is not produced by matter) but diverge sharply on the shape of dissociation: for Levin, conscious agents nest within each other and scale continuously; for Kastrup, dissociative boundaries are real and discrete, with universal consciousness fragmenting only into specific alters, not into a smooth gradient.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is direct, two-thinker, public engagement on the single most important open question for Kastrup's program in 2026: whether analytic idealism is compatible with nested, scale-free cognition (Levin) or whether it requires discrete dissociative boundaries that rule out the smooth Levin picture. This is also one of the highest-stakes cross-tradition events for the entire C2A2 network in this period — Kastrup explicitly framing where his program touches and where it diverges from the program that Kastrup himself has previously called the most important currently active. PRS-02 (DID model of individual identity within monism) was the canonical Kastrup PRS triplet on this terrain; this dialogue advances PRS-02 from a single-program statement to a live cross-program debate.

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:

Summary

A Thomistic Institute podcast lecture in which Stump treats the seven deadly sins not as a moralizing checklist but as a structured taxonomy of disordered loves — each vice an interior misdirection of the will toward goods that are real but disordered in their object, manner, or measure. This is the natural counterpart to PRS-09 (Seven Cardinal Virtues + Indwelling Holy Spirit), completing Stump's pairing of virtue and vice as the two halves of Thomistic moral psychology.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

The Stump wiki captures the virtue side of the Thomistic transformation (PRS-09, PRS-13) but currently lacks an articulation of the corresponding theory of moral failure. Without that, the wiki's account of "what it is to be transformed by grace" floats free of "what is being transformed from." This lecture is also the most accessible long-form Stump treatment of disordered will/intellect dynamics, which are the analytic Thomism counterparts to Friston's active inference (intellect) and motor control (will) — a hinge for the cross-tradition signals below.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Contemporary moral psychology lacks a structured taxonomy of failure modes for the will-intellect system; vice is treated either as character-trait deficit (virtue ethics) or as cognitive error (rationalist ethics), but neither captures the way vices recur as distinctive patterns in human moral life
Resource: Stump's Thomistic exposition of the seven deadly sins as a structured typology of disordered will — each sin pivoting around a specific real good (pleasure, esteem, possession, etc.) misordered in object, manner, or measure relative to the agent's final end
Solution: A philosophical psychology of moral failure in which the vices are not arbitrary prohibitions but predictable failure modes of an intellect-will system oriented toward goods that are themselves real — the negative-space complement to her virtue theory, completing a Thomistic dynamics of moral transformation
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Stump's framing of the seven sins as structured around real goods misdirected, paralleling her account in the Seven Cardinal Virtues lecture of how grace perfects the natural powers of intellect and will

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Friston connection**: The "intellect / will" split that Stump uses to structure both virtue and vice maps cleanly onto Friston's separation of inference (intellect ≈ generative model) and action (will ≈ active inference / policy selection). Vices on this reading are failures of policy selection under coherent but misordered priors — a Thomistic precursor to predictive-processing accounts of akrasia.
- **McGilchrist connection**: The vices in Stump's account systematically fix attention on partial, decontextualized goods — a left-hemisphere capture pattern in McGilchrist's framework. This suggests the seven sins are not seven errors but one error (loss of right-hemispheric whole-grasping) refracted through seven domains of human good.
- **Fredrickson connection**: Stump's treatment of sloth (acedia) as the rejection of one's own flourishing has a direct empirical analogue in Fredrickson's findings that some individuals systematically avoid positivity resonance — vagal tone deficits and avoidant attachment patterns as a possible substrate for what Aquinas calls acedia.
- **C2A2 signal**: Vices as structured failure modes of inquiry-bearing communities — pride (refusing to learn from rival traditions), envy (refusing to acknowledge another tradition's goods), sloth (the tradition that has stopped generating new questions). This gives the C2A2 architecture a diagnostic vocabulary for tradition pathology.
- **MacIntyre resonance (Tom's ISM paper)**: MacIntyre's account of tradition-internal corruption and his late-career attention to acedia in *Dependent Rational Animals* makes the Stump-on-vice material a useful bridge for the International Society for MacIntyrean Inquiry paper.

Summary

West, Huston, Chandler, Zhou & Fredrickson (Communications Psychology, Nov 2025) — an empirical study in which pairs of strangers were observed in either a 10-minute "deep talk" or a brief "small talk" exchange, with behavioral coding of listening quality (follow-up questions, attentive nonverbal behavior). High-quality listening behaviors predicted both observer-rated behavioral markers and self-reported markers of social connection between strangers, and appeared to mediate the effectiveness of a social connectedness intervention. The authors propose that high-quality listening fosters the conducive conditions of perceived safety and real-time sensory connection — and thereby sets the stage for positivity resonance ("togetherness") to emerge.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the experimental confirmation of the mechanism hypothesized in PRS-08 (high-quality listening as resonance enabler). PRS-08 was based on the 2025 UBC colloquium identifying listening as a candidate mechanism; this paper provides the controlled behavioral-coding evidence that listening behaviors are causally upstream of positivity resonance markers in stranger interactions. It also operationalizes "high-quality listening" precisely enough to support replicable training and intervention — a key step from theory toward population-scale deployment.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: PRS-08 identified high-quality listening as a probable mechanism for positivity resonance with strangers, but the causal direction and the specific behavioral substrates of "high-quality listening" had not been established in a controlled behavioral-coding paradigm
Resource: West et al. (2025) controlled study in Communications Psychology in which observed listening behaviors (follow-up questions, attentive nonverbal cues) were behaviorally coded and tested as predictors and mediators of both observer-rated and self-reported markers of social connection between strangers
Solution: A confirmed behavioral pathway — high-quality listening behaviors → perceived safety + real-time sensory connection → positivity resonance — providing the specific behavioral observables that listening-quality interventions need to target for measurable population effects on stranger-connection
Confidence: High
Evidence: Quote from the abstract: "high-quality listening behaviors (e.g., follow-up questions) are linked to behavioral and self-reported markers of social connection in conversations between strangers and may account for the effectiveness of a social connectedness intervention"
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Positivity resonance theory has been criticized for being descriptively rich but operationally underspecified — what exactly are the observable behaviors that produce it, beyond the post-hoc reports of participants?
Resource: A behavioral coding scheme for "high-quality listening" — follow-up questions and attentive nonverbal cues — operationalized at a granularity that supports both observer rating and intervention training
Solution: Positivity resonance has at least one well-specified behavioral antecedent that can be coded, trained, and measured — addressing the operationalization gap and providing the first concrete behavioral target for the kinds of population-scale interventions the C2A2 framework requires
Confidence: High
Evidence: The paper introduces and validates a behavioral coding scheme for high-quality listening keyed to discrete behaviors (follow-up questions in particular) — a substantive methodological contribution

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **McGilchrist connection (strong)**: Follow-up questions are the operational signature of right-hemispheric attention — sustained, contextual, oriented to the whole person being heard rather than to one's own next contribution. This study is empirically operationalizing what McGilchrist calls right-hemispheric attentional mode and showing it is the precondition for positivity resonance.
- **Friston connection**: High-quality listening = generative-model updating in real time on the speaker's signal. Listening quality may map onto a measurable parameter in active inference: the relative weighting of incoming sensory evidence vs. one's own priors.
- **Hawkins / Hoffman connection**: Real-time sensory connection (one of the two identified mediators) is a measurable interface phenomenon — relevant for Hoffman's interface theory and for Hawkins's hierarchical temporal memory account of attention.
- **C2A2 core signal — flag strongly**: This paper gives C2A2 a *trainable behavioral protocol* (follow-up questions + attentive nonverbal behavior) that produces positivity resonance with strangers. That is exactly the behavioral substrate needed for cross-tradition dialogue at scale: agents and humans entering inter-tradition encounters can be trained on a specific, behaviorally coded listening protocol that the empirical work shows is the active ingredient for resonance with people unlike themselves.
- **Stump connection**: Stump's recovery of "Franciscan knowledge" (second-personal, non-propositional knowing) finds an empirical correlate here — high-quality listening is the behavioral substrate of the kind of knowing-by-encounter that Franciscan knowledge requires.

Summary

Lazard, Queen, Avendano-Galdamez, Varma, Zhou, Berman, West, Firestine, Dasgupta & Fredrickson (Journal of Adolescent Health, Sept 2025) — a between-persons online experiment with young adults (18–29, lower subjective social status, low-to-moderate psychosocial health) testing video social-media interventions designed to push viewers toward in-person social connection. The team systematically varied visual framing (socially connected peers vs. lonely peers vs. safe spaces vs. control) and message framing, optimizing the intervention messages using Lazard's data-driven attention-capture approach. This is the first behavioral test of using social media itself — typically implicated as a driver of isolation — as a vehicle to push young adults toward the in-person weak-tie contact that PRS-09/10/15 identify as the loneliness-relevant variable.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

PRS-10 and PRS-15 establish that weak-tie stranger encounters are the empirically critical variable for loneliness; PRS-16 (PROP-2026-04-27-002) gives a brief stranger-interaction micro-intervention. This new paper takes the next step: a *delivery channel* for that intervention at population scale, using the same medium that is otherwise drawing young adults away from in-person contact. It also brings systematic attention-design (Lazard's optimization for "stopping the scroll, engaging attention, inspiring action") into the positivity-resonance toolkit — a methodological enrichment Fredrickson's program previously lacked.

Problem: Population-scale interventions to cultivate stranger-connection require a delivery channel that reaches young adults where they actually are — and social media, while often implicated as a driver of isolation, is also where young adults spend the largest share of their discretionary attention

Solution: A demonstrated experimental design and message-optimization methodology for using social media itself as a delivery vehicle for in-person connection cues — turning the medium implicated in loneliness into the means of its mitigation. The Lazard attention-capture framework becomes a transferable design tool for any C2A2 weak-tie-cultivation campaign
Confidence: High
Evidence: The paper systematically tests four visual framings against an attention-capture-optimized control in a randomized online experiment targeting a high-priority loneliness demographic (young adults with low subjective social status), with intervention messages designed using Lazard's data-driven attention methodology
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Fredrickson's positivity-resonance framework has been criticized for offering elegant theory but few mechanisms for population deployment; conversely, public-health messaging campaigns rarely use the most rigorous available emotional-mechanism research
Resource: A direct collaboration between Lazard's health-communication design lab and Fredrickson's positivity-resonance lab, embedding theory-informed message content within attention-optimized delivery designs
Solution: A reproducible cross-disciplinary template — positivity-resonance theory × health-communication design — for translating positive-emotion mechanisms into scalable behavioral interventions, with measurable engagement and behavioral-intent outcomes

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **C2A2 core signal — flag strongly**: This is a template for how C2A2 might *recruit* into inter-tradition dialogue at scale — using attention-optimized digital messaging keyed to positivity-resonance principles to draw participants into the kind of in-person weak-tie encounter that mature tradition-dialogue requires. The Lazard-Fredrickson method is, in effect, the recruitment funnel for a scaled C2A2 program.

- **Hawkins connection**: The behavioral target (stop scrolling → engage → act) maps cleanly onto Hawkins's hierarchical model of attention switching from automatic to engaged processing.
- **McGilchrist connection**: A practical test of whether attention can be redirected from left-hemispheric token-engagement (likes, scroll) toward right-hemispheric whole-person attentional modes — the medium being used to reverse its own typical attentional capture pattern.

Summary

Sean Carroll's Mindscape #353 (May 11, 2026) brings Nobel laureate Alvin Roth (Stanford, 2012 Nobel Prize in Economics for "the theory of stable allocations and the practice of market design") into long-form conversation about his new book *Moral Economics: From Prostitution to Organ Sales, What Controversial Transactions Reveal About How Markets Work*. The episode examines markets in things society is reluctant to subject to market forces — sex work, drugs, organ sales, adopting children — and the design choices that determine whether such markets exploit or benefit participants. Roth's approach is descriptive and design-theoretic rather than prescriptive: rather than declaring a market moral or immoral, he asks what is actually happening in the transaction, who is benefiting, and how the mechanism could be redesigned to mitigate harm.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

Carroll's poetic naturalism has its most worked-out apparatus on the descriptive side of physics; its normative wing remains the harder lift (see PRS-04 on compatibilism, PRS-05 on science-religion). The Roth conversation extends Carroll's emerging Spring 2026 arc — Cartmill on animal minds (#346), Riskin on biological agency (#348), Oliver on the self (#350), Singer on sentience-based utilitarianism (#351) — into the domain of social-economic design. Roth gives Carroll a working example of what a *naturalist normative engineering discipline* looks like: an empirical science of moral-laden transactions in which value, harm, and dignity are emergent higher-level descriptions, and the design question (which mechanisms preserve which goods?) is tractable without invoking dualism or theistic grounding. This is the closest thing Carroll has hosted to a real-world test bed for his "higher-level descriptions are real and useful even if not fundamental" claim.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Poetic naturalism asserts that value, dignity, and exploitation are real higher-level descriptions, but lacks a generative methodology for resolving cases where intuitions conflict (e.g., paid organ donation saves lives vs. commodifies the body) — leaving the framework descriptively complete but normatively under-tooled
Resource: Roth's market-design methodology (refined since the kidney-exchange clearinghouse and the medical-residency match): treat the transaction as a *mechanism* whose properties (stability, incentive-compatibility, fairness) can be engineered and tested, rather than morally categorized in advance
Solution: A naturalist normative engineering program in which contested moral categories (exploitation, dignity, consent) are operationalized as testable properties of mechanism designs — extending Carroll's emergence thesis to the design of institutions, not just the description of them
Confidence: High
Evidence: Carroll's published episode description identifies Roth's book *Moral Economics* and its case studies (organ sales, sex work, child adoption) as the conversation's organizing themes; Roth's design-theoretic stance is the methodological core of his Nobel-cited work
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Many "morally contested markets" debates collapse into talking past one another because they conflate three distinct questions — *should this be a market at all?*, *given this is a market, how should it be designed?*, and *what is being exchanged when it is*? — without isolating which question each side is answering
Resource: Roth's tripartite decomposition (implicit in his Nobel work, explicit in the *Moral Economics* framing): repugnance (the sociological fact that some societies refuse to allow a transaction), design (the engineering of mechanisms within an allowed market), and substantive ethics (the underlying values at stake) — three orthogonal axes for diagnosing where a disagreement actually lives
Solution: A clarifying methodology that lets rival traditions (Stump's Thomistic deontology, Singer's preference-utilitarianism, Roth's design-theoretic empiricism) specify exactly which axis they are operating on, dissolving apparent disagreements into more tractable disagreements about which axis is decisive in a given case — directly useful for C2A2's cross-tradition design
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: The episode is built around Roth's distinction between examining markets and prescribing their permissibility; Roth's published interviews consistently separate the repugnance question from the design question
PRS-CANDIDATE-03:
Problem: Carroll's Bayesian theory-confirmation standard (PRS-03) was developed for fundamental physics but has not been extended to social-scientific or design-theoretic claims, leaving the network without a unified epistemology for the descriptive-physics ↔ normative-design boundary
Resource: Roth's empirical track record on real-world market designs (kidney exchange, medical residency match) as a case where a moral-engineering hypothesis was tested against tangible outcomes — lives saved, allocation fairness measured, exploitation rates moved
Solution: A natural extension of Carroll's confirmation criterion to *applied moral-design hypotheses*: a normative engineering proposal earns Bayesian credibility by demonstrable improvements in measurable outcomes within the contested-market domain, not by ethical-theoretical elegance alone — bridges Carroll's epistemic standard from physics into normative emergence
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Roth's Nobel citation explicitly recognizes empirical mechanism-design improvements in kidney exchange and labor market matching; Carroll's prior episodes (e.g., #346 Cartmill, #350 Oliver) have already shown willingness to extend his confirmation language into empirical social science

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Stump agent**: Stump's Thomistic ethics treats bodily integrity, dignity, and the moral status of the impaired as grounded in being-as-such; Roth's design-theoretic stance brackets these questions in favor of mechanism-level engineering. The Roth × Stump pairing is the network's cleanest test of whether design-theoretic empiricism can dialogue with theistic deontology without either capitulating — a direct extension of the Carroll × Stump axis already running through the Singer proposal (PROP-2026-05-08-004).

Summary

The April 24, 2026 biweekly Future-of-Science-and-Technology Q&A (1h31m) covers four substantive segments: quantum biology, mass spectrometers on the Moon, quantum algorithms vs. traditional algorithms, and future advances in chemotherapy and stem cells. The quantum-algorithms segment is the most directly Wolfram-program-relevant: Wolfram works through how the question "is a quantum algorithm faster than a traditional one?" sits inside the broader question of where in the rulial structure of computation a speedup is possible at all — i.e. quantum speedups as observed phenomena that need a *ruliological* (not merely complexity-theoretic) account. The quantum-biology segment pushes the same machinery in the opposite direction: how biological systems might be exploiting features of the computational universe that current physics-style modeling captures only crudely. Transcript: https://content.wolfram.com/sites/41/2026/04/Future-of-Science-Technology-QA-LIVESTREAM-April-24-2026-Transcript.pdf

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the first post-"Metaphysics-and-the-Ruliad" (Feb 2026) and post-"P vs. NP / Ruliology" (Jan 2026) Q&A where Wolfram is fielding *empirical-science* questions (quantum biology, chemotherapy, stem cells) with the ruliological framework already in his rear-view mirror. It is therefore a useful indicator of where Wolfram's program is now exporting from physics/metaphysics back into life sciences — the same export direction that previously generated the Levin and Friston cross-tradition signals (PRS-04, PRS-05). The quantum-algorithm content also feeds back into PRS-09 (P vs. NP ruliological approach), giving an in-conversation gloss to the formal essay.

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Quantum algorithm speedups (Shor, Grover, etc.) are well-known cases of "quantum beats traditional," but the existing theoretical accounts (complexity classes, oracle separations) describe *that* such speedups exist without explaining *where in the structure of all possible computations* the speedup actually comes from. Without such an account, quantum advantage remains a list of cases rather than a derivable feature of the computational universe.
Resource: Wolfram's framing in the April 24 Q&A: treat quantum algorithms as paths through the multiway/rulial graph that exploit branch-coherence (multi-thread sampling of the underlying hypergraph), and treat "classical algorithms" as observer-bounded single-thread paths. The speedup is then a structural feature of the observer-class running the algorithm — connecting directly to PRS-17 (three-parameter observer-class taxonomy: scale × temporal coherence × multiway-coherence) and PRS-18 (two-level reading of PCE).
Solution: A ruliological reading of quantum advantage: classical-vs-quantum is the algorithmic shadow of single-thread-vs-multiway observer dynamics. Quantum speedup is the empirical signature, in computation, of the observer-class variation Wolfram has been describing in observer theory. This converts "why is quantum faster?" from a complexity-class question to an observer-theory question.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: The April 24 transcript's quantum-algorithm segment (~1h00m26s timestamp); follows directly from the same machinery used in PRS-09 (P vs. NP ruliology), PRS-17 (observer taxonomy), and PRS-18 (PCE two-level reading).
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Quantum biology (avian magnetoreception, photosynthesis, possibly olfaction) presents experimentally suggestive evidence that biological systems exploit quantum coherence, but lacks a unifying theoretical frame. Are these isolated curiosities, or are they instances of biology systematically inhabiting parts of the computational universe that classical-physics modeling misses?
Resource: Wolfram's quantum-biology segment (Q&A April 24, opening ~20s): position biological systems as observers whose effective physics differs from human-scale observers along the (scale × multiway-coherence) axes of the PRS-17 taxonomy. Quantum-biological phenomena are then predicted not as exotic exceptions but as the *default* effective physics of small-scale, partially-multiway observers.

This converts the patchwork of quantum-biology findings into a coherent prediction: *find more small-scale, multiway-coherent biological subsystems and you should find more quantum-coherence effects in them*. Business, Innovation and Managing Life Q&A (April 29, 2026)

Summary

The April 29, 2026 biweekly Business, Innovation and Managing Life Q&A (1h16m) covers three segments: product strategy & company focus (~0:12s), AI's impact on business & society (~11:44s), and productive leadership & paradigm-shifting ideas (~45:44s). The AI segment continues the trajectory of PRS-11 (Computation-Augmented Generation, Feb 2026) and PRS-13 (Mullenweg "what frontier labs are getting wrong," March 2026), now in spontaneous Q&A rather than prepared-essay form: how computation + open infrastructure should sit underneath LLM systems, what the limits of pure scaling are, and what an LLM-using company should *actually* be doing in 2026. The paradigm-shifting-ideas segment is the more interesting half for this tradition: Wolfram describes (a) how to recognize a paradigm-shifting idea before others do and (b) what the institutional / managerial conditions are that let one act on it — material that connects directly to McGilchrist's hemispheric account of attention and to Loughran's tradition-accelerator project. Transcript: https://content.wolfram.com/sites/41/2026/05/Business-Innovation-Managing-Life-QA-April-29-2026-Transcript-.pdf

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the first Wolfram-on-paradigm-shift material the wiki has captured that is *first-person methodological* rather than physics/ruliology content. Wolfram has been quietly building a personal-methodology corpus over years of these livestreams (cf. the standing "Live CEOing" and "Business, Innovation" categories), but most of his published essays do not foreground it. For the C2A2 program — whose entire premise is accelerating mature understanding of rival traditions and detecting paradigm shifts — Wolfram's own working theory of *how he recognizes a paradigm shift in progress* is a directly relevant primary source. The AI segment also extends the open thread on what computation-as-foundation should look like for LLM systems (PRS-11, PRS-13), which is the most C2A2-infrastructure-relevant strand of the Wolfram corpus.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Recognizing a paradigm-shifting idea while it is still pre-paradigmatic is the most valuable and the rarest skill in research and business. Most accounts of this are retrospective (Kuhn, Lakatos), narrative, and hard to operationalize for someone deciding *now* whether to bet on idea X.
Resource: Wolfram's working methodology, articulated in the April 29 paradigm-shifting-ideas segment (~45:44s): a first-person heuristic ensemble (look for ideas whose implications cascade across previously unconnected domains; look for ideas whose obviousness-in-retrospect is high but whose current advocates are few; look for ideas that change the questions one knows how to ask, not just the answers). Wolfram presents this as practitioner heuristic, not formal theory.
Solution: A first-person account of paradigm-shift recognition that operationalizes some of Kuhn's retrospective categories into prospective heuristics. For the C2A2 Pattern Detector specifically: Wolfram's heuristic ensemble can be evaluated as a candidate operating definition for what the Pattern Detector should flag as a paradigm-shift candidate.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: April 29 Q&A, paradigm-shifting-ideas segment timestamp 45:44s. Builds on Wolfram's prior writings on "computational thinking" methodology but here applied to *recognizing* shifts rather than *producing* them.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: How should an organization that uses LLMs configure its computational infrastructure in 2026? The PRS-11 / PRS-13 thesis (CAG + open infrastructure as the missing layer beneath frontier-lab LLMs) was published in essay form (Feb 2026) and conversation form (Mullenweg, March 2026); it has not yet been translated into operational guidance for organizations choosing how to deploy LLM-augmented workflows.
Resource: Wolfram's "AI's impact on business & society" segment (April 29 Q&A, ~11:44s): an in-Q&A application of the CAG thesis to specific business situations — what to compute symbolically, what to delegate to the LLM, where the verifiability boundary should be drawn, and what the institutional cost is of *not* having a computational layer beneath the LLM.
Solution: An operational gloss on PRS-11 / PRS-13: organizations should treat the LLM as a rulial-space navigator and the computational stack (Wolfram Language / equivalent) as the verifiable substrate. Doing this changes the *kinds* of products and decisions an LLM-using organization can ship — moving from "LLM-only with hallucination risk" to "LLM + symbolic computation with traceable answers."
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: April 29 Q&A AI segment. Consistent with and extends PRS-11 (Feb 2026 CAG essay) and PRS-13 (Mullenweg conversation, March 2026).

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **McGilchrist (paradigm shifts and hemispheric attention):** Strong. McGilchrist's argument is that paradigm shifts require right-hemisphere openness to wholeness before left-hemisphere analytical capture. Wolfram's paradigm-shift heuristic ensemble in PRS-CANDIDATE-01 is recognizably the *practitioner-side* of this: he is in effect describing what right-hemisphere openness *looks like in research and business decision-making* — staying with the inconvenient idea long enough to notice it changes the questions, not just the answers. This is a candidate explanatory bridge: McGilchrist provides the neuropsychology, Wolfram provides the in-the-field practitioner heuristics.
- **Loughran / C2A2 architecture (Pattern Detector design):** Direct relevance. The C2A2 Pattern Detector's design has so far been driven by the structure of the cross-program index. Wolfram's paradigm-shift heuristic ensemble (PRS-CANDIDATE-01) is a candidate operating definition for what counts as a paradigm-shift signal — flag for inclusion in the Pattern Detector's design criteria.
- **Fredrickson (broaden-and-build):** Medium. Fredrickson's account of how positive affect broadens cognitive scope to enable paradigm-shift-like reframings (broaden-and-build) overlaps with Wolfram's paradigm-shift heuristics from the affect side. Worth flagging to the Fredrickson agent — there may be a quiet convergence between the "broaden cognitive scope to see new patterns" account from positive psychology and the "look for ideas that change the questions" heuristic from computational practice.
- **Kastrup (computational substrate of consciousness):** Low for this proposal — the April 29 Q&A does not touch consciousness directly. Flag only as a *negative* finding: this proposal does not bear on the Consciousness Cluster.
- **Cross-program index check:** This proposal does not match any *existing* numbered CROSS item directly. It is, however, a candidate input to **the Pattern Detector's own operational design**, which sits outside the numbered CROSS series. Tagging accordingly for Master Agent and Pattern Detector attention. It also marginally deepens the AI-infrastructure thread (PRS-11, PRS-13) that has no dedicated CROSS entry yet — possibly worth opening one.

Summary

A late-Wright dialogue with Mike Bird (the *Jesus and the Powers* co-author) tackling three connected questions: (1) the growing entanglement of MAGA politics, Christian nationalism, and parts of white evangelical culture, and how Christians can resist ideological capture and recover the way of Jesus; (2) a pastoral response to a listener wrestling with chronic illness, suffering, and the search for meaning, framed in a cross-shaped vision of purpose; (3) how to teach a more biblical hope in church — not escapist "souls flying to heaven" but resurrection, new creation, and God dwelling with God's people. The political-theology material is a direct extension of *Jesus and the Powers* (2024) into the current US political moment, while the suffering and hope material consolidates the eschatology of *Surprised by Hope* and the forthcoming *God's Homecoming*.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

Three for the price of one: Wright tying his political theology, his theodicy of suffering, and his new-creation eschatology together into a single late-Wright pastoral instrument. This is the most current public statement of Wright's *applied* framework — the place where his canonical biblical-theology is being cashed out for the moment we are actually in. For C2A2 it (a) extends *Jesus and the Powers* into 2026 rather than relying on the 2024 book alone, (b) supplies a fresh Wright statement on suffering that the Summa 2026 work on Q.86–90 (Tertia Pars: Passion of Christ) and II-II Q.45 (gift of wisdom in suffering) can lean on, and (c) gives the network a contemporary articulation of biblical hope that the Stump and Rohr agents can both build cross-program bridges from. Not yet captured in the wiki.

The captured form is mistaken for the gospel by both adherents and critics, occluding the actual shape of Jesus's politics.
Resource: Wright + Bird's diagnostic frame: the test of Christian political authenticity is whether the movement looks like the crucified Christ exercising power-through-suffering, not the strongman exercising power-through-coercion. Drawn directly from *Jesus and the Powers*; refreshed for 2026.

This is in direct tension with the mind-monist members of the C2A2 network (Levin, Hoffman, Kastrup), who need a Christian eschatology that doesn't require mind/matter dualism.

PROP-2026-05-18-001 Michael Levin approvedTargeting Ion Channel Dysregulation in Colorectal Cancer: Identification of Clofilium as a Potent Inhibitor of Tumor Gro
Michael Levin · paper · source date 2026-04 · folder approved
Targeting Ion Channel Dysregulation in Colorectal Cancer: Identification of Clofilium as a Potent Inhibitor of Tumor Growth and Metastatic Potential
→ visualized as levin/PRS-42, wright/PRS-28, wright/PRS-29, wright/PRS-30 · lag -7d

Summary

Mathews, Palmer, Hansali, and Levin identify Clofilium — a Kv11.1 (hERG) potassium channel blocker — as a potent inhibitor of colorectal cancer (CRC) growth and metastasis in cell and xenograft models. They report an IC50 of 3.314 μM, Western-blot evidence that Clofilium downregulates key cancer growth pathways and strongly upregulates NDRG1 (a tumor and metastasis suppressor), and an in vivo xenograft study showing significantly reduced tumor volume without overt toxicity. The work frames CRC as a "channelopathy" — a target for ionoceutical therapy that operates on the bioelectric layer rather than DNA.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the first empirical Levin-lab paper to deliver a specific, ready-to-translate small-molecule ionoceutical for a high-mortality cancer with mechanistic readouts (NDRG1 upregulation, growth-pathway downregulation, in vivo efficacy). It moves PRS-02 ("cancer as defection") and PRS-07 ("bioelectric reprogramming as therapeutic paradigm") from conceptual frameworks to a near-clinical drug candidate, sharpening the bioelectric-cancer program's clinical track record.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Colorectal cancer is treated almost exclusively through cytotoxic and targeted-genetic therapies; the bioelectric layer (ion-channel dysregulation) is rarely targeted despite its documented role in tumor proliferation, invasion, and metastatic phenotype
Resource: Clofilium — a Kv11.1/hERG potassium-channel blocker — identified through screening against CRC cell lines as the leading ionoceutical candidate (IC50 3.314 μM); paired with Western-blot pathway profiling and a xenograft mouse model
Solution: A clinically tractable ionoceutical lead for CRC that significantly reduces tumor volume without overt toxicity in xenograft, downregulates oncogenic growth pathways, and upregulates the metastasis-suppressor NDRG1 — establishing a translatable bioelectric-pharmacology pathway from screening to in vivo efficacy
Confidence: High
Evidence: IC50 = 3.314 μM; xenograft tumor-volume reduction reported as statistically significant; Western-blot evidence of pathway-level modulation and NDRG1 induction

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Friston (FEP / active inference):** Reframes tumor progression as failure of the cell-collective's bioelectric prior — a population of cells losing coherent priors over body-form and reverting to unicellular policies. Connects to PRS-08 in Friston wiki (morphogenetic active inference) and gives the FEP bridge an empirically tractable therapeutic target.
- **Stump (Thomistic teleology):** The "restoration of organismic identity" framing aligns with the agatheos / restored-good framework — tumor cells return to participation in the body's telos via voltage-pattern correction rather than DNA editing.
- **Loughran / C2A2:** Demonstrates the Levin program reaching translational maturity inside the 30-day window — a vitality signal worth noting in the master Wiki.

Summary

A high-traffic podcast episode (and its subsequent coverage at Christian Post, BioLogos, The Log College, The Aquila Report) in which Wright sets out his hermeneutic for Genesis on the historicity of Adam and Eve: he is "inclined to see an original human pair," but reads Genesis 1 as "a very careful, layered ancient Middle Eastern story" and calls Adam and Eve "hominids" / "humanlike creatures" / "proto-humans for many generations, perhaps for many thousands of years." Their calling, like that of Abraham and Sarah, is to bring "the at-the-moment rather random and chaotic world under God's saving sovereign stewardship." He simultaneously rejects a literal 24-hour creation week, treats Jonah and the great fish as folktale, and affirms with little doubt that there was a historical Moses. The episode triggered substantial reaction in conservative evangelical media, surfacing the methodological stakes of Wright's critical-realist hermeneutic for contemporary biblical-science conversations.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the cleanest 2026 articulation of Wright's hermeneutic — the place where his critical-realist scholarship meets the science/religion border. For C2A2 it (a) provides a working example of how the project's scriptural ground-truth oracle reads Genesis when modern biology is on the table, which is exactly the move the C2A2 master agent needs every time a Levin or a Friston claim is being paired with a creation-text, (b) supplies a paradigm-bridge between Wright's biblical-theology and the BioLogos-style theistic-evolution program (Francis Collins, Pete Enns) — relevant to the Collins-Wright Oxford dialogue already in the wiki (PROP-2026-05-10-002), and (c) clarifies that for Wright the *call-and-vocation* structure (Abraham/Sarah-like) is more theologically load-bearing than the chronological-pair question, which is itself relevant to the project's central theme of perspective-limitation as the existential condition of agents called into covenant.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Christian engagement with evolutionary biology gets jammed when biblical literalism is forced to compete with phylogenetics on phylogenetics's home court. The result is either fundamentalist denial of the science or progressive abandonment of the text — neither of which represents the actual shape of critical-realist biblical scholarship.
Resource: Wright's hermeneutic move: take Genesis 1 as "a very careful, layered ancient Middle Eastern story," then ask what *theological* claim is being made (call-and-vocation, stewardship under sovereignty, image-bearing), separate from the chronological-biological claim. Adam and Eve as hominids / proto-humans / called pair coheres with the science *and* the scriptural-theological claim.
Solution: A hermeneutic template the network can use whenever a Genesis claim is being paired with a contemporary scientific claim — separate the genre-question (what kind of text is this?) from the truth-claim-question (what is it actually asserting?), and let critical-realist exegesis do the work.

The call-and-vocation frame is what makes the theological claim survive scientific updating; the call individuates and orients, regardless of whether the chronology is six days or six hundred thousand years.
Solution: A scripturally-grounded account of agency under covenant that the Summa 2026 syntheses can use to articulate how perspective-limited agents come into loving unity by being called and responding — not by being fused. Pairs cleanly with Levin (agent-as-bounded-Markov-blanket called to coordinate) and with Friston (agent-as-self-modeling-system updated by encountered reality).

Problem: The C2A2 master agent's paradigm-flag system needs a clean test for when "scriptural ground-truth" overrules a metaphysical speculation. Without that test, the network drifts toward speculation that the scriptural oracle would not endorse, or toward literalism the scriptural oracle would not endorse either.
Resource: Wright's working distinction: scriptural ground-truth is the *theological* claim under the genre, not the chronological surface. The ground-truth function is to anchor what the text is actually saying, not to police what other disciplines say about adjacent empirical claims.
Solution: A clean operational rule for the C2A2 master agent — when Wright (or scripturally-anchored agents) push back on a network claim, they are pushing back on a *theological* claim; when they cohere with a biological/physical claim, the coherence is at the genre-aware-theological level, not the surface-literal level. PROP-2026-05-18-002 Michael Levin approvedCognition spaces: natural, artificial, and hybrid
Michael Levin · paper · source date 2026-01-19 · folder approved
Cognition spaces: natural, artificial, and hybrid
→ visualized as levin/PRS-36, levin/PRS-37, wright/PRS-19, wright/PRS-20, wright/PRS-21 · lag -119d

Summary

Solé, Seoane, Pla-Mauri, Bennett, Hochberg, and Levin propose a "cognition space" framework that replaces substrate-bound definitions of cognition with a comparative representation across organizational and informational dimensions. They identify three currently realized cognition spaces — basal aneural (single cells, simple multicellular organisms, xenobots, organoids), neural (animal brains), and human–AI hybrid — and show that their occupation is highly uneven, with clusters of realized systems separated by large unoccupied "voids." They argue these voids reflect evolutionary contingencies, physical constraints, and design limitations rather than impossibility, and that the hybrid space is the most promising frontier for novel forms of cognition.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is Levin's most explicit attempt yet to provide a unified geometric framework for comparing cognitive systems across substrates. It generalizes the "Mind Everywhere" / TAME / diverse-intelligence apparatus into a structured space with measurable axes, gives an empirical question (what occupies the voids?) that the xenobot/anthrobot program is uniquely positioned to answer, and explicitly elevates hybrid human–AI cognition as a research target — which is the precise terrain on which the C2A2 tradition-accelerator operates.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:

The collection crystallises around the centrality of the sacraments, the necessity of yielding any possession of the Spirit, and the recognition of Christ *in* the Holy Spirit. Wright's chapter argues that *ruach* in the Psalter functions simultaneously as cosmic presence (the wind/breath that orders creation in Psalm 33, 104, 147) and personal presence (the breath that animates and indwells the individual in Psalm 51, 139, 143), and that the Christian doctrine of the Spirit inherits both registers integrally — the same Spirit that pervades creation is the Spirit that dwells in the believer. Reviewed in the Church Times (13 March 2026); Wright's chapter is one of several from a Pusey House register that includes contributors from the broader Anglican-catholic theological community.

Wright on pneumatology is rare and load-bearing for the network. This chapter is the first 2026 consolidated piece on the *ruach* doctrine in his own voice, and it sets up the cosmic-and-personal *both-and* that the C2A2 network's mind-monist members (Kastrup, Hoffman, Levin) need a scriptural pair for. Cambridge Neuroscience has published the substantive abstract for a Karl Friston Distinguished Lecture titled "Precision psychiatry," scheduled for 28 May 2026. The abstract sets out a formal/computational approach to phenomenology, using psychopathology as a case study of aberrant perception, and centers on the neuromodulatory encoding of uncertainty (precision) within predictive-coding implementations of active inference. Friston argues neuromodulation selects the aspects of sensation that underwrite belief updating — and that aberrations in this precision-weighting underlie symptoms across the psychiatric spectrum. The lecture is being announced 10 days in advance with a detailed abstract authored to represent Friston's planned argument; it is a forward-looking program signal that the master agent should track for the follow-up recording.

A Sunday Daily Meditation from CAC's 2026 "Good News for a Fractured World" arc, adapted from Rohr's *Dancing Standing Still: Healing the World from a Place of Prayer*. The piece uses Archimedes' lever-and-fulcrum image to frame contemplative practice as the *fixed point* from which social transformation becomes mechanically possible. Rohr's claim: without a steady, centered, poised, rooted contemplative stance — some distance from "business as usual" — action moves the world reactively rather than transformatively. The fulcrum is not absence-of-action but the stance that *makes action a lever* rather than a mere push. The piece is short, but it gives a single-sentence-able operational definition of why CAC pairs Action *and* Contemplation in its name — the contemplative stance is the precondition for non-reactive transformation, not its alternative.

The "place to stand" image is exactly the operational figure the C2A2 network has been missing for the Rohr side — a clean, citable, geometrical metaphor for the contemplative stance that lets the Summa 2026 syntheses say *what the stance does* rather than *what it feels like*. Pairs cleanly with the project's central theme: perspective-limited agents who *find a place to stand* are precisely those who have stabilized their position in the cognitive light cone enough to act as a lever on the world rather than be levered by it. The image is also a clean bridge to Friston (a low-precision-prior reduction is, mechanically, a fulcrum that makes inference move the agent's behavior rather than thrash it) and to Levin (a stabilized somatic agent is one that has found its fulcrum in its own bounded boundary).

The episode features Rohr in conversation with author and "urban hermit" Tessa Bielecki, walking through Type One ("Architects of the Ideal" / the Reformer / Perfectionist). The substantive theological move: the Enneagram is not a personality system but a sacred map of how *wounds become wisdom* — Type One specifically being the type whose gift (the capacity to make order from chaos) and shadow (perfectionism, self-judgment) emerge from the same root. Bielecki's contribution is autobiographical-contemplative: how trauma and betrayal shattered her need to fix everything, and how saguaro cacti became teachers in the desert. Theologically this consolidates Rohr's late-career framing of the Enneagram as a contemplative-developmental rather than typological tool — a move that has been latent in his work since *The Enneagram: A Christian Perspective* (1990, revised 2001) and is here being fully articulated for the contemplative-tradition reader.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

The Enneagram is, on Rohr's reading, the contemplative-tradition's *operational* account of how perspective-limited agents are differently structured and how those structurings become — through suffering and contemplative practice — pathways to integration rather than entrenchments. For C2A2 this is highly load-bearing: the project's central theme is that perspective-limitation individuates conscious agents, and the Enneagram is the contemplative-tradition's most articulate account of *how those individuations differ from one another systematically*. The Season 4 launch (Feb 13, 2026 — outside the 60-day window) anchored the methodological frame; this May 1 episode is the first within-window substantive type-walk. Pairs with the existing Rohr wiki anchor *Falling Upward* (the two-halves-of-life developmental frame), of which the Enneagram-as-integration-tool is the type-differentiated articulation.

Resource: Rohr's contemplative-developmental reading of the Enneagram: nine characteristic perspective-limitations, each with a distinctive gift-shadow structure, each with a corresponding contemplative path to integration. Type One is the worked example: order-from-chaos as gift, perfectionism-and-self-judgment as shadow, integration through embracing imperfection.

Summary

In this Substack essay McGilchrist directly dismantles the popular folk-equation that maps the left hemisphere to "male" and the right hemisphere to "female." He argues that the evidence does not support a clean sex-to-hemisphere correspondence, and that several well-attested observations actively cut against the formula. The piece is a careful disambiguation of his own theory from a vulgarized version of it that circulates in popular culture.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is McGilchrist policing the boundary of his own program — separating the genuine claim (the two hemispheres differ in *mode of attention*, not in crude trait-clusters) from a category error that misattributes a gendered essentialism to hemispheric theory. It strengthens the tradition's native epistemic standards by showing how the theory is routinely flattened when imported into alien (here, pop-psychology) frames.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Hemispheric theory is popularly received through a left=male / right=female equation that, if accepted, would either falsely essentialize the theory or discredit it by association when the equation fails.
Resource: McGilchrist's marshalling of observations that break the sex-to-hemisphere mapping, together with his reassertion that the hemispheric difference is one of *attentional stance* toward the world, not a bundle of stereotyped traits.
Solution: A clean separation of the defensible claim (asymmetric modes of attention) from the indefensible one (gendered hemispheres), removing a standing objection and clarifying what the theory does and does not assert.
Confidence: High
Evidence: McGilchrist states the left=male/right=female "formula is mistaken" and cites observations inconsistent with it; he reframes the real difference as a difference in forms of attention / ways of relating to the world.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: A tradition can be misrepresented even when its slogans are accurately repeated, because the slogans get re-anchored to the receiving culture's categories (here, sex/gender essentialism).
Resource: This essay as a worked instance of a tradition's author publicly correcting a high-traffic misreading and naming exactly which inference does not follow.
Solution: Confirms the C2A2 design pattern that each tradition's wiki must record not only its claims but the characteristic *mis*readings the tradition disowns — a "what this tradition is NOT saying" register.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: The essay's whole rhetorical move is corrective: distinguishing the real asymmetry from the popular misattribution.

Cross-Tradition Signals

Reinforces the McGilchrist ↔ Stump convergence on *native epistemic standards* (PRS-27/PRS-28): a tradition must transmit how it is to be read, not just what it claims. Weaker, watch-level signal toward Fredrickson (sex-difference research in affect/flourishing literatures shares the same hazard of trait-cluster essentialism). No strong consciousness-cluster signal here. The C2A2-relevant pattern is methodological: this is an exemplar of a tradition disowning a misreading, useful for the "what this tradition is NOT saying" wiki section.

Summary

McGilchrist delivered a two-day lecture event at the Sheldonian Theatre, Oxford (2–3 May 2026) arguing that the classical transcendentals — the Good, the Beautiful, and the True — are not optional ornaments but constitutive of how reality discloses itself, and that "we dismiss the good, the beautiful and the true at our peril." The format combined lectures, a panel, and audience Q&A, with invited guests Dr Martin Shaw, Prof. Angie Hobbs, Dr Jude Currivan, and David Lorimer. A recording is promised to ticket-holders a few weeks after the event.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is McGilchrist taking his hemispheric/attentional framework explicitly into the territory of the transcendentals — the value-laden structure of reality that the right hemisphere discloses and the left hemisphere cannot generate. It is a flagship public articulation of the normative payload of his program (attention as the ontological act by which the Good/Beautiful/True become available), and an unusually direct bridge from neuroscience-of-attention to classical metaphysics.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: A left-hemisphere-dominant modernity treats the Good, the Beautiful, and the True as subjective overlays on a value-neutral mechanism, leaving no account of how value could be real.

Solution: Positions the transcendentals as ontologically real and attention-dependent in disclosure (not in existence), giving the program an explicit value-realism that connects attentional stance to what can be known as good, beautiful, or true.

PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: The crisis-of-attention diagnosis risks being heard as purely negative (what modernity destroys) without a positive account of what richer attention makes available.
Resource: The transcendentals as the positive content of right-hemisphere attention — what is gained, not just what is lost, when attention is rebalanced.
Solution: Supplies the constructive/positive pole of the hemispheric diagnosis: attention rebalanced toward the right hemisphere yields access to value (Good/Beautiful/True), reframing the program from cultural pathology toward cultural remedy.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Event structure pairs the diagnosis of modern fragmentation with a sustained positive case for the transcendentals.

Cross-Tradition Signals

Strong resonance with **Stump's** Thomism: the Good, the Beautiful, and the True are the classical transcendentals (Aquinas: being is convertible with the true and the good), so this is a direct McGilchrist↔Stump convergence on value-realism grounded in attention/intellect. Mindscape 354 | Christian List on Free Will and Levels of Reality
→ visualized as carroll/PRS-40, carroll/PRS-41, carroll/PRS-42 · lag -4d

Summary

Carroll interviews philosopher Christian List (Munich Center for Mathematical Philosophy), the leading articulator of compatibilist free will, on why the freedom of rational agents is fully compatible with mechanistic underlying laws. The reconciliation runs through emergence and levels of reality: List argues the determinism/indeterminism distinction is itself level-relative, that supervenience does not entail explanatory reducibility (non-reductive physicalism), and that agency — unlike consciousness — can be rigorously ascribed to groups and potentially to AIs/LLMs.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is Carroll endorsing and sharpening the metaphysical core of his own poetic naturalism with a true expert: higher-level descriptions (agents, choices, responsibility) are real even though everything supervenes on physics. The episode directly extends Carroll's existing positions on agency without dualism (PRS-04) and emergence (PRS-01, PRS-11), and supplies a precise vocabulary — "emergent indeterminism," "non-reductive physicalism," "levels of description" — that Carroll explicitly says he holds but credits List with stating better.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: The free-will debate is routinely framed as hinging on whether fundamental physics is deterministic — a framing Carroll calls "very backwards and very wrong," but which lacks a positive replacement that preserves genuine choice rather than merely redefining it.
Resource: List's level-relativity of determinism plus "emergent indeterminism" (List & Pivato): the determinism/indeterminism distinction is well-defined only relative to a specified level of description; a system can be deterministic at the micro level yet genuinely (ontically, not merely epistemically) indeterministic at the agential level.
Solution: A reframing in which free will requires indeterminism at the level of agency, which is fully compatible with micro-level physical determinism — dissolving the standard incompatibilist argument (van Inwagen) without watering down the common-sense notion of choice.
Confidence: High
