PROP-2026-07-13-004 Karl Friston approvedTopographic Variation in Human Neurotransmitter Receptor Densities Explains Differences in Intracranial EEG Spectra
Karl Friston · paper · source date 2025 (journal version; recirculating mid-2026 — see caveat) · folder approved
Topographic Variation in Human Neurotransmitter Receptor Densities Explains Differences in Intracranial EEG Spectra
→ visualized as friston/PRS-31, friston/PRS-32 · lag 8d

Summary

Stoof, Friston, Tisdall, Cooray & Rosch fit biophysically informed neural mass models to a normative intracranial EEG dataset using dynamic causal modelling (DCM), and show that regional variation in neurotransmitter *receptor density* explains a substantial share of the variance in cortical population dynamics — i.e., in the local iEEG spectrum. Supplying receptor-distribution maps as priors improves model evidence. The output is a cortical atlas of neurobiologically informed intracortical synaptic connectivity parameters, offered as a normative resource for future DCM studies.
*Caveat (surfaced, not hidden): this is a work-not-yet-captured rather than a clean within-30-days item. It surfaced in search as a June-2026 Friston publication, but the verifiable record shows a 2025 journal version (Human Brain Mapping, doi 10.1002/hbm.70393) with an earlier bioRxiv preprint. The date field above is therefore hedged. It passes the filter on the "significant work not yet in the wiki" clause, not on recency. Tom/orchestrator should confirm the version before ingestion.*

Why This Matters for This Tradition

Friston's program is often criticized as unfalsifiable metaphysics with a Bayesian veneer. This is the counter-evidence line: a concrete, empirically-fit DCM in which the free-energy machinery is used to *infer synaptic parameters from data* and is scored by model evidence against real intracranial recordings. It also does load-bearing work for the theoretical arc the wiki has been tracking. The precision-psychiatry talk (PROP-2026-05-18-003) claims that neuromodulation encodes precision and that psychopathology is aberrant precision-weighting. That claim needs receptor density to actually determine population dynamics. This paper is the empirical hinge on which that theoretical claim swings.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Precision-weighting accounts of perception and psychopathology assign a central role to neuromodulatory receptor systems, but the explanatory gap between cortical microarchitecture (receptor expression) and mesoscopic electrophysiology (the signals we actually record) has been unbridged. Without that bridge, "precision" is a free parameter.
Resource: DCM with biophysically informed neural mass models fit to a normative intracranial EEG dataset, using PET/autoradiography-derived receptor-density maps as empirical priors on synaptic connectivity.
Solution: Receptor-density variation is shown to explain regional variance in cortical population dynamics, with receptor-informed priors *improving model evidence* — i.e., the microarchitecture-to-signal link is established variationally rather than assumed. Precision acquires a measurable neurochemical substrate.
Confidence: High
Evidence: "Incorporating prior information on receptor distributions further improved model evidence, indicating that variability in receptor density explains some variance in cortical population dynamics."
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: DCM studies of electrophysiology have lacked a normative baseline — each study re-estimates synaptic parameters from scratch, so no one can say whether an individual patient's inferred connectivity is anomalous.
Resource: A cortical atlas of neurobiologically informed intracortical synaptic connectivity parameters, released as a normative resource.
Solution: Individual-difference and patient studies can now be scored against a normative synaptic connectome — the precondition for the "computational psychiatry as deviation from normative precision" program to be run at all.
Confidence: High
Evidence: The paper explicitly frames its output as "a normative resource for future DCM studies of electrophysiology" and "a methodological foundation to integrate multimodal data."

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **[[Levin]]** — the interesting inversion. Here Friston's tradition grounds an abstract informational quantity (precision) in a *material* substrate (receptor density), while Levin's tradition (this same cycle, PROP-2026-07-13-002) drives in the opposite direction, showing a material variable (nuclear membrane voltage) doing informational, memory-like work. Two traditions crossing in opposite directions through the same matter/information boundary is worth the master agent's attention.
- **[[Hawkins]]** — receptor-density topography as the microarchitectural correlate of cortical-column heterogeneity; Hawkins' thousand-brains framework assumes a repeated canonical circuit, and this paper quantifies how far from canonical the real cortex is.
- **[[C2A2 / master]]** — methodological, not thematic: this is a worked example of a tradition earning credibility by making its central abstraction *measurable*. That is the same move C2A2 is attempting with PRS-chain and listening metrics.

Programmatic Flag (not a PRS — for the master agent)

Two institutional events in Friston's research program occurred within this cycle's 30-day window and are recorded here because they bear on the program's track record even though they generate no PRS triplet:
- 2026-06-18: VERSES AI, the company built on active inference (the "Genius" platform), halted all AI research and development.
- 2026-06-27: Karl Friston resigned as Chief Science Officer of VERSES AI.
These are *commentary/reportage about* Friston, not material *from* him, so per the standing quality filter no proposal is made from them. But the C2A2 measurement framework explicitly treats a research program's track record — the questions it generates and whether its institutional carriers survive — as evidence about the program. The collapse of the flagship commercial instantiation of active inference is a data point of exactly that kind, and the master agent should decide whether the framework wants to register it. Recommend Tom rule on whether "institutional/programmatic events" become a first-class node type in the wiki, distinct from PRS triplets.

Summary

Bender, Kofman, Agüera y Arcas and Levin (2026, *Biological Theory*) report a meta-analysis of how researchers across disciplines actually define "life," rather than proposing a definition of their own. The paper treats the definitional disagreement itself as data — mapping the space of criteria people invoke and where they diverge.

Levin's whole program depends on loosening the life/non-life and mind/non-mind boundaries (xenobots, anthrobots, "cognition all the way down"). A survey showing that the definition of life is not converged even among practitioners is direct methodological support for treating "is it alive?" as a pragmatic, observer-relative question rather than a natural kind — the same move he makes with "is it cognitive?"

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Levin's diverse-intelligence claims are routinely dismissed on the grounds that they violate the settled definition of life or of cognition — but is there a settled definition to violate?
Resource: A meta-analysis of expert opinion on the definition of life, treating the spread of definitions as an empirical object.
Solution: Evidence that no consensual definition exists, which converts the objection from "you are wrong about life" into "you are choosing a different, and defensible, cut" — licensing the pragmatic/observer-relative framing Levin needs.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Bender, Kofman, Agüera y Arcas, Levin (2026), *Biological Theory* — "What Lives? A meta-analysis of diverse opinions on the definition of life."
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: If "life" has no agreed definition, on what basis can any boundary be drawn for engineered/hybrid systems (xenobots, anthrobots, synthetic morphology)?
Resource: The mapped criterion-space from the meta-analysis (which criteria cluster, which are orthogonal).
Solution: A proposal to replace the binary predicate with a multi-axis continuum in which engineered systems occupy legible positions rather than being forced to one side.
Confidence: Speculative
Evidence: Inferred from the paper's framing; needs the full text to confirm whether the authors take this constructive step or stop at the descriptive meta-analysis.

Direct bridge to **Wolfram** (the wiki already holds `2026-05-05_wolfram_rulial-ensemble-biology-bulk-orchestration`, which raises the same "what counts as alive" question from the ruliology side — a computational-boundedness answer to a question Levin answers empirically). Summary

A 1h20m livestream Q&A in which Wolfram traces the intellectual history of discrete space — the idea that space is not a continuum but a network of discrete elements — which is the load-bearing premise of the Wolfram Physics Project. The session's published segments are: "How the idea of discrete space developed" (t=13s), "Why personal records matter for the history of science" (t=44m00s), "How people and fields become part of history" (t=46m05s), and "Encounters with the past through people, machines and artifacts" (t=1h07m30s).

Why This Matters for This Tradition

The wiki captures Wolfram's *systematic* case for discrete space (hypergraph rewriting, the Ruliad) but has no node on its *historical provenance* — who proposed discreteness before him, why it was abandoned, and what changed. That provenance is exactly the material an inter-tradition dialogue needs when a rival program asks "why should we take this seriously?" The three later segments are also a first-person account of Wolfram's own historiographic method (personal records, artifacts, how fields get canonized), which bears directly on how the C2A2 network models tradition-formation itself.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: The discreteness of space is treated in the wiki as a Wolfram-originated postulate, leaving the program vulnerable to the charge that it is an idiosyncratic starting assumption rather than a live option with a genealogy.
Resource: Wolfram's historical reconstruction of the discrete-space idea (segment 1, t=13s) — the lineage of proposals for space as a discrete network and the reasons continuum mathematics displaced them.
Solution: Reframes hypergraph physics as the recovery and computational completion of a long-standing but under-tooled research option, rather than a novel postulate. Supplies the Wolfram Agent with a defensible answer to Carroll's status-assignment challenge (CROSS: "Does Wolfram Physics meet Carroll's Bayesian theory-confirmation standard?").
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Published segment title and timestamp on livestreams.stephenwolfram.com; the session transcript PDF exists at content.wolfram.com but was not retrievable in this run (see Retrieval Note), so the specific lineage claims are not yet verified verbatim.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: How does a research program become part of the recognized history of a field — and what determines whether an idea ahead of its time is recovered or lost?
Resource: Wolfram's account of historiographic method (segments 2-4): personal records as primary sources, the mechanics by which people and fields enter the canon, and material encounters with the past through machines and artifacts.
Solution: A first-person, practitioner's model of tradition-formation and canonization, offered by a figure who is simultaneously a subject of it. Directly usable by the C2A2 master layer as source material on how traditions accumulate, preserve, and lose their own track records.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Published segment titles and timestamps (t=44m00s, 46m05s, 1h07m30s); content not verified verbatim.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Arkani-Hamed (CROSS-017, hypergraph vs. amplituhedron):** if Wolfram's historical account identifies *why* continuum methods won, that same account may indicate what pre-geometric approaches had to give up — a possible shared diagnostic for why both programs now dispense with spacetime as an input. **Match against an open cross_program_index question.**

A genealogy of discrete space does not supply one, but it does change the *prior* — it repositions the program as a revived option rather than an unmotivated novelty. Worth noting explicitly as a partial, non-empirical response to the most urgent open item assigned to this agent.
- **Stump / MacIntyre-adjacent:** segments 2-4 are, in effect, Wolfram doing tradition-constitution from the inside — how a field's canon forms, what counts as a record, how a practitioner becomes historical. This is unusually close to MacIntyre's account of traditions as narratively extended arguments, and is the strongest bridge signal in this proposal.

PROP-2026-07-18-002 Michael Levin approvedTraining Ecosystems: A Computational Approach to Uncovering Learning Behavior in Unconventional Contexts
Michael Levin · paper · source date 2026-05 · folder approved
Training Ecosystems: A Computational Approach to Uncovering Learning Behavior in Unconventional Contexts
→ visualized as levin/PRS-62, levin/PRS-63, levin/PRS-64 · lag 3d

Summary

Samanta, Hazan, and Levin ask whether an ecosystem — not an organism, not a cell — can be shown to learn. They ran a classic predator-prey model in silico across more than 220,000 parameter combinations, perturbed it with stimuli, and measured recovery dynamics. Recovery time exhibited habituation, sensitization, and a form of discrete number learning, with no explicit memory medium anywhere in the system: memory is carried purely by dynamical interactions.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This pushes Levin's "cognition all the way down" program decisively *upward* in scale — most of the corpus argues down from organisms toward cells and molecular networks, whereas this argues up from organisms toward ecological assemblies. It also supplies a concrete case of memory without a memory substrate, which is load-bearing for the diverse-intelligence claim that cognitive predicates track dynamics rather than hardware.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Does the ascription of learning to non-neural systems extend above the organism level, or does it bottom out at the individual?
Resource: A minimal in-silico predator-prey ecological model swept across 220,000+ parameter combinations, with recovery time after stimulus perturbation as the behavioral readout.
Solution: Minimal ecological dynamics are sufficient to produce habituation, sensitization, and discrete number learning — learning is demonstrable at the ecosystem scale.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Systematic sweep of >220,000 parameter combinations showed habituation, sensitization, and a form of discrete number learning in recovery time.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Must a learning system possess a dedicated memory medium (synapse, molecular store, engram) to exhibit memory-dependent behavior?
Resource: A model in which no explicit memory medium exists — state persistence is carried entirely by dynamical interaction among populations.
Solution: Memory-dependent learning phenomena arise from interaction dynamics alone, decoupling the concept of memory from any storage substrate.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: The paper's stated focus on "memory implemented purely by dynamical interactions without explicit memory media."
PRS-CANDIDATE-03:
Problem: Are habituation and sensitization coupled, and does the coupling constrain what counts as a learning signature?
Resource: Paired measurement of recovery time and response magnitude across the full parameter sweep.
Solution: A strong asymmetry — 90.6% of parameter combinations paired recovery-time sensitization with response-magnitude habituation, while the reverse was extremely rare — suggesting the two channels are structurally, not incidentally, related.
Confidence: Speculative
Evidence: "90.6% of parameter combinations exhibited recovery time sensitization paired with habituation of response magnitude, while the opposite pattern was extremely rare."

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Friston** — an ecosystem that habituates without a memory store is a candidate case of a Markov-blanketed system minimizing surprise at a scale with no obvious agent; tests whether the free energy principle's scale-freedom claim survives the absence of a substrate.
- **Wolfram** — memory as pure interaction dynamics is close to the ruliological claim that computation is what the substrate is doing, not what it stores.
- **Hoffman / Kastrup** — a learning system with no locus of storage weakens the intuition that cognitive predicates require a bounded physical bearer, which both idealist programs press on from the other direction.

PROP-2026-07-19-002 Richard Rohr approvedPracticing \"Just This\": Weekly Summary
Richard Rohr · blog · source date 2026-05-23 · folder approved
Practicing \"Just This\": Weekly Summary
→ not visualized as a distinct triplet

Summary

A week on contemplative practice mechanics, missed by prior runs. Rohr's central claim is a directional transformation: prayer that reaches the unconscious shifts one's whole construal of the world from fear to connection — from being fear-driven to being love-drawn — which he glosses as movement from ego consciousness to soul awareness. The method is explicitly non-suppressive: thoughts and feelings are neither clung to nor opposed but allowed to pass, with partial failure treated as itself instructive rather than as defect. Rohr adds that negative motivation is not fought but exposed under a compassionate gaze and falls away as counterproductive. The week's practice section, from spiritual director Therese DesCamp, refuses every instrumental justification for meditation (acuity, aging, blood pressure, stress, being a better Christian) as byproduct rather than aim, and relocates the test of practice from what is experienced during the sit to behavior across the remaining twenty-three hours.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the most mechanically explicit account of contemplative practice CAC has published in this cycle, and it is the piece the wiki most needs: the tradition's Research Question 4 asks what contemplation looks like computationally, and this week supplies three testable specifications — non-suppressive attention (neither clinging nor opposing), motivation-extinction-by-exposure rather than by force, and an externalized success criterion. DesCamp's relocation of the criterion to out-of-session behavior is methodologically important for the C2A2 accelerator, since it makes the claim assessable without any appeal to privileged first-person report.

Candidate PRS Triplets

**PRS-CANDIDATE-A**
- **Problem:** Contemplative practice is standardly evaluated by the quality of in-session experience, which is unfalsifiable, self-reinforcing, and invites spiritual consumerism.
- **Resource:** DesCamp's inversion — practice is preparation, not performance; its true test is conduct in the twenty-three hours outside the sit, on the analogy of scales to concerto.
- **Solution:** An externalized success criterion for contemplative practice, assessable by third-party behavioral observation rather than introspective report. Makes contemplative claims admissible as evidence in the accelerator's tradition-comparison design.
- **Confidence:** High
- **Evidence:** DesCamp, *Hands Like Roots: Notes on an Entangled Contemplative Life* (Santos Books, 2025), 135–136, quoted at length in the Week Twenty practice section.
**PRS-CANDIDATE-B**
- **Problem:** How does a practice that neither suppresses nor endorses its own contents produce durable change in what an agent is disposed to do?
- **Resource:** Rohr's two-part mechanism — thoughts allowed to pass without clinging or opposing, and negative motivation exposed under a compassionate gaze until it "falls away as counterproductive and useless" — coupled with the fear-driven → love-drawn directional claim.
- **Solution:** Read contemplative practice as extinction-by-non-reinforcement rather than as inhibition: the practice withholds both suppression and engagement, so high-precision fear-weighted priors lose the traffic that maintains them, and the agent's default construal shifts from threat-modeling to connection-modeling.
- **Confidence:** Speculative
- **Evidence:** Sunday and Monday entries (fear-driven to love-drawn; passing thoughts without clinging or opposing) and Wednesday (negative energy exposed rather than fought). The active-inference gloss is the proposal's, not Rohr's.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Friston Agent:** PRS-CANDIDATE-B is the strongest Rohr–Friston contact point yet proposed — non-suppressive attention as precision-weight decay on fear-priors, with "fear-driven to love-drawn" as a shift in the generative model's default construal. This is exactly Rohr Research Question 4 and should be flagged for the master agent as a **paradigm-bridge candidate**.

- **Stump Agent:** The compassionate-gaze mechanism is second-personal in Stump's sense: change is effected by being regarded, not by self-application of a technique.

PROP-2026-07-20-001 Michael Levin approvedTopological constraints on self-organization in locally interacting systems
Michael Levin · paper · source date 2026 · folder approved
Topological constraints on self-organization in locally interacting systems
→ visualized as levin/PRS-70, levin/PRS-71 · lag 1d

Summary

Sacco, Sakthivadivel and Levin derive necessary conditions on the *topology of a graph* for an ordered phase to exist at all. By studying how free energy scales under domain-wall formation in the Potts model, in autoregressive models, and in hierarchical networks, they show that the combinatorics of who-interacts-with-whom can by itself prevent or permit spontaneous ordering — independent of the physics of the individual units.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

Levin's program asserts that collective intelligence and large-scale order arise from local signaling among cells. This paper supplies the missing *negative* result: a formal statement of which interaction topologies make such collective ordering impossible. That converts "cells self-organize" from a descriptive claim into a constrained, falsifiable one, and gives the morphogenetic-field idea a mathematical boundary condition.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Levin's framework says collective order emerges from local interaction, but offers no principled account of when local interaction *fails* to produce order — so the claim resists falsification.
Resource: Free-energy scaling analysis of domain-wall formation on graphs (Potts model, autoregressive models, hierarchical networks); a topological criterion for the existence of an ordered phase.
Solution: Necessary conditions on interaction-graph topology for an ordered phase to exist, making "spontaneous ordering" a property predictable from connectivity structure rather than from substrate.
Confidence: High
Evidence: The paper shows "how the combinatorics of interactions on a graph prevent or allow spontaneous ordering," derived via scaling of free energy under domain wall formation.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Is there a substrate-independent way to compare the collective-intelligence capacity of biological tissue, a neural network, and an artificial agent collective?
Resource: The result's applicability across Potts lattices, autoregressive models, and hierarchical networks — three substrates under one topological criterion.
Solution: A candidate substrate-neutral comparator: rank systems by whether their interaction topology admits an ordered phase, not by what the units are made of.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: The analysis is carried out uniformly over statistical-physical, machine-learning, and hierarchical-network models.

Cross-Tradition Signals

**Strong Friston bridge — flag explicitly.** Co-author Dalton Sakthivadivel is a principal author in Friston's Bayesian-mechanics orbit (Markov blankets, free-energy formalism as a physics of beliefs). This is a *direct co-authorship bridge* between the Levin and Friston research programs, not merely a thematic resonance. The paper's use of variational free energy over graph topologies is precisely the formal object Friston's Markov-blanket construction operates on, which suggests a shared formalism in which Levin's morphogenetic collectives and Friston's particular kinds are two readings of one mathematics.
**Wolfram signal (Medium):** the claim that combinatorics of a graph alone constrain what order can arise is close in spirit to Wolfram's hypergraph-rewriting account of emergent structure — both make topology, not substrate, the carrier of possibility.
**Arkani-Hamed signal (Speculative):** a result of the form "the shape of the interaction structure determines what can exist" rhymes with the amplituhedron program's move from dynamics-first to geometry-first explanation. Worth a watch, not yet a claim.
**Context:** this paper appears in the *Philosophical Transactions A* theme issue "World models in natural and artificial intelligence" (384/2320), the same issue already represented in the wiki by Rouleau & Levin and Levin & Lyons. Three papers from one issue now touch this tradition; the issue itself may deserve a node.
PROP-2026-07-20-002 Michael Levin approvedMachines all the way up and cognition all the way down: Updating the machine metaphor in biology
Michael Levin · paper · source date 2026 · folder approved
Machines all the way up and cognition all the way down: Updating the machine metaphor in biology
→ visualized as levin/PRS-65, levin/PRS-66, levin/PRS-67 · lag 1d

Summary

Levin and Richard Watson argue that the machine metaphor dominating molecular and cell biology cannot account for self-constructing, goal-driven living agents — but that the dualistic alternative (machine *versus* mind) fails too. They propose a third option, "cognition all the way down," using information theory and Turing-machine arguments to expose where reductionist models break, and inverting the standard causal story to **cognition → code → chemicals**.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the clearest statement to date of the *metaphysical* commitment underneath Levin's empirical program, written jointly with Watson (evolutionary connectionism). Levin flagged the final published version as "quite a bit different than the original preprint" — so the wiki's earlier preprint-era understanding of this argument is stale. The causal inversion (cognition → code → chemicals) is the load-bearing claim and is stated here more sharply than in "Mind Everywhere."

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Molecular mechanism and goal-directed agency appear incommensurable — the machine metaphor cannot generate agency, and dualism cannot be naturalized.
Resource: A "new kind of cognitivism" — cognition all the way down — unifying bottom-up and top-down causal flows within a single non-dualist frame.
Solution: Reject the machine/mind dichotomy: living tissue is *both* machine and cognizer, with cognition as the organizing level rather than an emergent afterthought.
Confidence: High
Evidence: The paper "discuss[es] inadequacies of both mechanist/computationalist frameworks and dualistic conceptions of machine versus mind, proposing instead a new kind of cognitivism."
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Standard molecular biology assumes causation runs chemicals → code → phenotype; this cannot explain top-down goal-directed correction of perturbations.
Resource: Information-theoretic and Turing-machine arguments applied to the reductionist model of gene expression.
Solution: Invert the sequence — the correct causal ordering is **cognition → code → chemicals**.
Confidence: High
Evidence: Stated directly: "the correct causation sequence is cognition → code → chemicals."
PRS-CANDIDATE-03:
Problem: Does the "cognition all the way down" thesis have empirical teeth, or is it a re-description of the same facts?
Resource: Watson's evolutionary-connectionist machinery brought to bear on developmental plasticity.
Solution: The claim earns its keep by predicting adaptive plasticity — cells implementing large-scale form and function under novel perturbation — that a machine reading does not anticipate.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: The paper offers "examples of collective intelligence and adaptive plasticity as cells implement large-scale form and function."

Cross-Tradition Signals

**Kastrup (Strong):** "cognition all the way down" is Levin's closest structural approach to Kastrup's analytic idealism — both deny that mind is a late emergent, both locate cognition at the base. They differ on whether the base is *many* cognizers (Levin) or *one* (Kastrup). This is a live disagreement worth staging as an inter-tradition dialogue; note that the wiki already holds a Levin–Kastrup conversation node (PROP-2026-07-08).
**Wolfram (Medium):** the Turing-machine argument against reductionist biology sits directly on Wolfram's computational-irreducibility terrain, and the two reach compatible conclusions from opposite directions.
**Friston (Medium):** "cognition all the way down" and "every Markov-blanketed thing performs inference" are near-identical in scope. Both universalize a mental predicate over all persisting systems; the open question is whether Friston's formalism *derives* what Levin's thesis *asserts*.
**McGilchrist (Speculative):** the machine metaphor's grip on biology is a plausible instance of McGilchrist's left-hemisphere capture of explanation — a possible bridge essay.

Summary

Hartl, Levin and Pio-Lopez review neural cellular automata (NCA) — cellular automata whose local update rule is a learned neural network — as a modelling substrate for morphogenesis, regeneration, and forms of intelligence that classical AI architectures do not capture. The review positions NCA as the computational counterpart of Levin's bioelectric collectives: many identical local agents, no central controller, robust large-scale target morphology.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the methodological spine of Levin's computational work, stated as a review rather than a single result. It matters for the wiki because it names *why* NCA and not standard deep learning: NCA natively exhibit the regenerative, anatomy-homeostatic behaviour Levin studies empirically, which makes them a candidate in-silico testbed for bioelectric hypotheses rather than a mere illustration.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Classical AI architectures (feedforward nets, transformers) have no natural account of regeneration, anatomical homeostasis, or goal-directed repair — the phenomena central to Levin's program.
Resource: Neural cellular automata — learned local update rules over a lattice of identical agents, with no global controller.
Solution: NCA as the appropriate computational model class for morphogenetic intelligence, supporting in-silico experiments on target-morphology setpoints.
Confidence: High
Evidence: The review is explicitly framed as applications "to biology and beyond classical AI."
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Is Levin's "collective intelligence of cells" a substantive computational claim or a metaphor?
Resource: The demonstrated ability of NCA to regenerate damaged target patterns from purely local rules.
Solution: A constructive existence proof — local-rule collectives *do* exhibit repair toward a setpoint without a homunculus, discharging the objection that goal-directedness requires a central planner.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: NCA regenerative behaviour is the review's central biological application.

Cross-Tradition Signals

**Wolfram (Strong):** NCA is literally Wolfram's cellular-automata substrate with a learned rule. This is the tightest formal contact point between the Levin and Wolfram programs in the wiki so far — Wolfram asks what CA rules *can* generate; Levin asks which rules a living system *selects and maintains*. A bridge essay on "rule discovery vs. rule maintenance" looks well motivated.
**Hawkins (Medium):** many identical local units, no central controller, converging on a coherent global model — the structural parallel to cortical columns and the Thousand Brains thesis is close enough to be worth testing rather than merely noting.
**Friston (Medium):** an NCA converging on a target morphology is a candidate minimal instance of active inference in a non-neural substrate, which the Friston agent's watch-list names as a major cross-tradition signal.
**Note for dedup:** distinct from the already-captured "BraiNCA: brain-inspired neural cellular automata" (arXiv:2604.01932) — that is a primary result, this is the field-level review.
PROP-2026-07-20-004 Karl Friston approvedReality is a creation of consciousness

Reality is a creation of consciousness

Summary

A long-form Institute of Art and Ideas interview (~3,200 words) in which Friston lays out, in plain language and at book-chapter length, how the Free Energy Principle unifies physics and psychology. He covers Helmholtzian unconscious inference, why perception is constructive, Markov blankets as the definition of "thingness," planning as the mark of true agency, dreaming as complexity-minimization, and psychopathology as false inference.
**Dating note (flagged honestly):** this is dated 17 September 2025 and therefore falls *outside* the 30-day window. It is proposed under the filter's second clause — "a significant work not yet captured" — because it is Friston's most accessible first-person statement of the FEP-to-consciousness argument and is absent from the wiki.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

The Friston wiki is heavy on formal papers and light on Friston's own philosophical self-interpretation. This interview supplies exactly that: it is where he states, unhedged, that "we are indeed trapped within our own heads," corrects the "controlled hallucination" formula to *entrainment*, and gives the criterion distinguishing mere free-energy-minimizing things from planning agents. For C2A2's purposes — which requires a *curriculum for climbing into* a tradition — this is a higher-value pedagogical node than another arXiv preprint.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: "Controlled hallucination" (Seth, Clark) implies the world controls the inner model, which misdescribes the perceiver's own causal contribution.
Resource: Huygens' coupled clocks and generalized synchrony / synchronization of chaos.
Solution: Replace "control" with **entrainment** — a mutual, bidirectional synchronization in which the agent causes its own sensations by choosing what to sample. Friston: "I would replace 'control' with 'entrainment.'"
Confidence: High
Evidence: Direct correction offered by Friston in the interview, with the Huygens argument that entrainment is "the only free-energy-minimizing solution" for loosely coupled systems.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: If every Markov-blanketed thing minimizes free energy, the principle is too permissive to distinguish a rock from an agent.
Resource: The observation that at intermediate scales an agent's *action* becomes a cause of its own sensations, so the generative model must infer its own actions.
Solution: A demarcation criterion — **planning** distinguishes true agents from mere free-energy-minimizing things. "Planning would be definitive of the kinds of things that can possibly be called true agents."
Confidence: High
Evidence: Friston's explicit scale argument (larger than quantum, smaller than celestial) yielding self-action-inference.
PRS-CANDIDATE-03:
Problem: Why would natural selection tolerate spending 20–40% of life dreaming, sequestered from the world?
Resource: The complexity term of variational free energy — accuracy *as simply as possible*.
Solution: Dreaming as complexity-minimization: generating fantasy sensoria to test which model parameters are dispensable, implemented as synaptic pruning (with Tononi).
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Friston's flying-elephant answer and the explicit link to synaptic regression.
PRS-CANDIDATE-04:
Problem: Psychiatric nosology lacks a unifying mechanistic account across psychosis, dissociation, and neglect.
Resource: Type-1/type-2 error framing of false inference, plus precision-weighting as "action on the inside."
Solution: Psychopathology as a **mathematical attention disorder** — a failure to appropriately ignore uninformative prediction errors; hallucination/delusion as type-1, neglect/dissociative symptoms as type-2.
Confidence: High
Evidence: The newscaster delusion worked example, where the delusion is described as "completely Bayes-optimal" given unattenuated interoceptive evidence.

Cross-Tradition Signals

**Hoffman (Strong — direct contact):** Friston states "there's the world out there, which we will never know," and the IAI page itself links to Hoffman's "Perception as a fantasy" at this exact point. Both hold that perception does not deliver the world. They diverge sharply on what follows: Friston keeps a mind-independent metaphysical world that we entrain to; Hoffman's interface theory denies that spacetime objects are that world at all. **This is a precise, stageable disagreement — recommended for an inter-tradition dialogue node.**
**Kastrup (Strong):** the article's title asserts reality is a creation of consciousness, but Friston's actual position is Markovian monism, not idealism — he explicitly preserves "some metaphysical world out there." The gap between the headline and the position is itself the interesting object: it marks exactly where Friston stops short of Kastrup.
**Levin (Medium):** "if you've got a name for it then it does this kind of thing" — Friston's blanket universalization of inference over all persisting things is the structural twin of Levin's "cognition all the way down" (see PROP-2026-07-20-002). Two traditions, one universalizing move, different warrants.
**McGilchrist (Medium):** Friston's transparent/opaque distinction (via Metzinger) — seeing versus knowing that one sees — is close to McGilchrist's account of the two modes of attention, and both make *attention* the seat of the difference.
**C2A2 relevance:** the reframing of pathology as failure to correctly weight what to ignore is directly portable to the inter-tradition project — a community that cannot attenuate uninformative signal from a rival tradition will generate Bayes-optimal delusions about it.

A Science of Reality: Observers, Interfaces, and Traces (The Trace Institute Whitepaper)
→ not visualized as a distinct triplet

Summary

The Trace Institute's founding whitepaper, dated 2026-06-02, is the first single-document statement of the full research program: a four-step chain running Interface Theory of Perception → Conscious Agent Theory → Trace Logic → **Recursive Trace Logic (RTL)**, followed by a four-domain research roadmap (physics, neuroscience, metaphysics, technology). It gives the explicit matrix formula for the trace kernel Q_A, defines the conscious agent in streamlined form as C = ⟨(X, 𝒳), Q, n⟩, and — most importantly — publishes **eight named, falsifiable physics conjectures** that the program commits to proving.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the canonical program document for the Hoffman-Prakash / TRACE phase of the tradition, and the wiki currently has the TRACE Institute recorded only as an organizational entity (PROP-2026-05-05-005) with no capture of its actual scientific content. It also supersedes the April 2026 Levin-hosted talk as the authoritative statement of trace logic: the whitepaper introduces the Policy Level / Meta-policy Level hierarchy as the definition of RTL, which the existing PRS-08 records only informally as "recursive trace logic."

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: The trace-logic program has been criticized as unfalsifiable metaphysics because it has never committed to specific, checkable physical predictions.
Resource: The Eight Conjectures (Table 1) — a numbered, domain-tagged list binding RTL to concrete derivation targets: (1) Minkowski space as the n→∞ limit of Markov n-cycles; (2) curved spacetime from non-cyclic chains; (3) cosmology from long samples of trace chains; (4) Planck-scale breakdown from energy growth with trace state-count; (5) quantum wavefunctions and the Born rule from asymptotics of enhanced Markov chains; (6) Standard Model particles as classes of Markov chains; (7) scattering amplitudes with ABHY associahedra as subpolytopes of the Markov polytope; (8) entanglement from disjoint traces of an ergodic chain.
Solution: The program converts its own falsifiability problem into a published research contract — each conjecture either proves or fails on ordinary mathematical grounds, independent of anyone's intuitions about consciousness.
Confidence: High
Evidence: "Proving these conjectures is a prime focus of the scientific program." (Table 1 and §5.1)
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: The original conscious-agent formalism decomposed agents into perception, decision, and action kernels — an assumption that smuggles an internal/external split back into a framework meant to dissolve it.
Resource: The streamlined agent C = ⟨(X, 𝒳), Q, n⟩ — a measurable space of potential experiences plus a single Markov kernel and a step counter, with the perception/decision/action decomposition explicitly withdrawn.
Solution: The framework drops the dualist residue in its own foundations; the whitepaper compares the move to the limits on decomposability of Hilbert space in quantum theory, and notes the 2014 Hoffman-Prakash formalism is recoverable as a "sufficiently decomposed variant."
Confidence: High
Evidence: Footnote 1, §3: "the present formalism adopts a more cautious stance regarding the decomposability of kernels and state spaces into respective internal and external constituents."
PRS-CANDIDATE-03:
Problem: Trace logic describes transitions *within* a fixed state space, but perception plainly involves changes to what the space of possible experiences even is — coarsening, fine-graining, combining with other agents.
Resource: Recursive Trace Logic — a hierarchy of Markov kernels governing changes to the state space itself. At each step the process either transitions within X_n or "steps up" to the **Policy Level**, a kernel over admissible restrictions/expansions of X_n; a third **Meta-policy Level** is a kernel over policies, and the hierarchy extends to arbitrary depth.
Solution: A formal account of an observer that reconstructs its own interface, with the trace order constraining which state-space changes are legal.
Confidence: High
Evidence: §4, worked two-level and three-level example.
PRS-CANDIDATE-04:
Problem: Active inference derives perception from surprise minimization but presupposes a material substrate, an internal/external Markov-blanket split, and a true world state.
Resource: RTL's surprise, defined as the difference between beliefs based on knowledge of the larger state space and the outcome realized on the trace.
Solution: Surprise minimization is recovered **without** substrate, without a rigid internal-external decomposition, and without any true observable world state — positioning RTL as strictly weaker in assumptions than active inference while reproducing its dynamics.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: §4: "unlike the standard active inference models, in the case of RTL this minimization of surprise is defined without the assumption of a material substrate..."
PRS-CANDIDATE-05:
Problem: The framework's non-dual ontology aligns with contemplative traditions, but importing contemplative claims as data would be methodologically indefensible.
Resource: The stated metaphysics protocol — "We do not import contemplative claims as data; we use the mathematics to clarify which questions are well-posed and how answers might be distinguished."
Solution: A worked test case: whether the tension between Buddhist *anatman* and Advaita's *ayam atma brahma* is a substantive soteriological conflict or a semantic one, to be settled by whether the two correspond to distinguishable trace-lattice structures.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: §5.3.
PRS-CANDIDATE-06:
Problem: Deep-learning architectures are enormously inefficient relative to brains, and attempts to borrow biological efficiency have largely failed.
Resource: "Microchip epistemology" — treating the hidden agent network as a distributed, non-spatiotemporally constrained computational reservoir with tunable read-outs and small-world topology.
Solution: A proposed computational paradigm claimed to be as transformative as attention architectures, motivated by the diagnosis that borrowing from the brain fails *because* the brain is an interface representation, not ground reality.
Confidence: Speculative
Evidence: §5.4, "Machine Intelligence"; cites Gauthier et al. 2021 on next-generation reservoir computing.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Friston** — Strongest signal in the document. RTL is presented as an assumption-weaker generalization of active inference, citing Parr, Pezzulo & Friston (2022) directly. This *extends* existing CROSS-032 (trace blankets subsume Markov blankets): the whitepaper now makes the subsumption claim about the *inference dynamics*, not only the boundary structure. Recommend the Friston agent be dispatched for an independent read — a claim to subsume the FEP without substrate is the kind of thing the receiving tradition should get to contest.
- **Arkani-Hamed** — Conjecture 7 names ABHY associahedra as subpolytopes of the Markov polytope, and §5.4 explicitly proposes integrating **surfaceology** (Arkani-Hamed et al. 2025, *JHEP*) with RTL. This is the most concrete form the amplituhedron-derivation bridge has taken; the wiki has carried it as "Speculative" since the RC Pilot.
- **Carroll** — Direct contact with the standing productive tension. The whitepaper insists it does not abandon physics but proposes recovering known laws as limiting cases. Conjectures 1-2 (recovering Minkowski and curved spacetime) are precisely what Carroll's poetic naturalism would demand before taking the program seriously; they are now on the record as commitments.
- **Kastrup** — §2 and §5.3 give a non-dual ontology reached by mathematical rather than argumentative route; the whitepaper cites Chalmers' "realist idealist" positioning. Convergence with analytic idealism, different derivation — consistent with the existing dispatch.
- **Levin** — §5.2 raises "the possible existence of conscious agents and their traces external to the brain, including questions about the potential ubiquity of consciousness in nature." Extends CROSS-034.
- **Hawkins** — Weak but real: the "microchip epistemology" section diagnoses deep learning's inefficiency and proposes a non-standard architecture. Hawkins reaches a similar diagnosis from the opposite ontology (resolutely biological). Worth flagging as a *productive tension* rather than convergence — same target, incompatible grounds.
- **Stump** — §5.3's free-will discussion explicitly contrasts Christian voluntarist traditions (probabilities as ontic manifestation of free will) with Madhyamaka Buddhist readings (probabilities as principled unpredictability). This is a direct, named invitation to the Thomistic tradition, and the framework leaves the question open rather than settling it.
- **C2A2 methodological note** — §5.2's "dark matter of human experience," including "linguistic narratives and experiential point-of-views... not ultimately physically situated in spacetime measurements, but nevertheless amenable to rigorous probabilistic inference," describes almost exactly the object C2A2's inter-tradition instrument is built to measure. Flagging for the Master agent.

PROP-2026-07-21-002 Donald Hoffman pendingTraces of Consciousness (the Trace Chain Theorem paper)
Donald Hoffman · paper · source date 2024-10 (preprint; cited by the Institute as 2024 and 2025) · folder pending
Traces of Consciousness (the Trace Chain Theorem paper)
→ not visualized as a distinct triplet

Summary

Hoffman, Prakash & Chattopadhyay's **Traces of Consciousness** is the primary source for the Trace Chain Theorem — the result the Trace Institute takes its name from. For any subset A of a Markov kernel's state space, there exists a *unique* trace kernel Q_A giving the effective dynamics seen by an observer restricted to A. Tracing induces a partial order on kernels, and that order induces a logic that is locally Boolean, globally non-Boolean, and provably homomorphic to the Lebesgue logic of probabilistic belief.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

**This is a gap-fill, not a new discovery.** The wiki already carries trace logic across PRS-07 through PRS-10, but every one of those triplets is sourced either to the April 2026 Levin-hosted talk or — in one case — to a secondary popular explainer at mindbodysolution.org. The tradition's namesake theorem has no primary-source citation in the vault. Given that the Hoffman wiki now leans heavily on trace logic and the whitepaper (PROP-2026-07-21-001) treats the theorem as settled ground, the load-bearing citation should be the paper itself.
Flagging a **provenance discrepancy for review**: the Trace Institute's publications page lists this as "Hoffman, D. D., Prakash, C., & Chattopadhyay, S. (2025)" while the whitepaper's own bibliography dates it 2024 (preprint deposited October 2024). The wiki should record the 2024 preprint date with a note, not silently pick one.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: An observer restricted to part of a system sees dynamics that mix the visible states with the influence of hidden ones; there was no canonical account of what dynamics such a restricted observer is entitled to say it is seeing.
Resource: The trace kernel, given in closed form as Q_A = I_A Q [Σ_{k=0}^∞ (I_U Q)^k I_A], where U is the complement of A and I_A, I_U are indicator multiplications — the unique Markovian kernel on A induced by Q.
Solution: A restricted observer's effective dynamics is a well-defined, unique Markov process. Perspectival limitation gets an exact mathematical characterization rather than being treated as noise or error.
Confidence: High
Evidence: Theorem restated in the Trace Institute whitepaper §3 with explicit formula, crediting Revuz (1984) and Hoffman et al. (2024).
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Trace logic needed a connection to established formal work on belief, or it would remain an isolated construction.
Resource: A proof that the trace logic is homomorphic to the Lebesgue logic of probabilistic belief — the logical principle previously identified as the basis of "observer mechanics" (Bennett, Hoffman & Prakash, 1989).
Solution: The trace order is shown to be the same formal object as an existing, independently motivated theory of perception, closing a thirty-five-year loop back to Hoffman's own earlier work.
Confidence: High
Evidence: Whitepaper §3, footnote 5.
PRS-CANDIDATE-03:
Problem: Reconciling incompatible observer perspectives is usually treated as a failure of communication or rationality, presuming a common frame must exist.
Resource: The partial order's incomparability structure — "not all kernels are comparable... many pairs are strictly incomparable, and no universal order exists that holds for all kernels across the entire set of possible observations."
Solution: Some pairs of observers are *formally* incomparable. Where no join exists in the trace order, there is no common refinement — a mathematical rather than merely psychological account of perspectival incommensurability.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Whitepaper §3. Note this sharpens the wiki's existing Active Research Question 8, which asked precisely for the conditions under which two Markov chains have a join.
PRS-CANDIDATE-04:
Problem: If a trace is all an observer has access to, what can it infer about the reality generating it?
Resource: The many-to-one structure of tracing — while only a restricted set of larger kernels are valid precursors to a given trace, "any given trace kernel could have been derived from an infinite number of larger, higher-dimensional kernels."
Solution: Underdetermination is formally exact: the information about unobserved states is simply lost, and no amount of interface-side inference recovers it. This is a strong, precise version of the interface argument that does not depend on evolutionary premises at all.
Confidence: High
Evidence: Whitepaper §3.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **C2A2 — highest-value signal in this proposal.** PRS-CANDIDATE-03 gives a candidate formal criterion for when two traditions are genuinely incommensurable versus merely unreconciled: existence or non-existence of a join in the trace order. If that maps onto MacIntyre's incommensurability thesis, C2A2 acquires a mathematical test for a claim that has been argued philosophically for forty years. Recommend the Master agent and the Loughran tradition both receive this. Treat as a *conjecture worth testing*, not an established mapping — the burden is to show the trace order is the right formalization of a tradition's rational structure, and that is not yet shown.
- **Friston** — PRS-CANDIDATE-01 is the technical basis for the trace-blankets-subsume-Markov-blankets claim (CROSS-032). The generalization from acyclic to cyclic graphs lives here.
- **Wolfram** — Observer-restricted effective dynamics from a larger substrate is structurally the same move as Wolfram's observer-dependent coarse-graining of the ruliad. Both make the observer's computational boundedness constitutive of the physics it sees. Existing wiki entry CROSS-033 touches this; the primary paper strengthens it.
- **Arkani-Hamed** — Feeds the positive-geometry bridge (CROSS-033), though the concrete associahedron claim belongs to the whitepaper's Conjecture 7, not this paper.
- **Hawkins** — Worth noting as a genuine structural rhyme: a trace kernel is a complete-but-partial model built by an observer with restricted access, which is formally close to what a cortical column is in Thousand Brains Theory. Hawkins grounds this biologically and stays agnostic on ontology; Hoffman grounds it ontologically and treats the biology as interface. The productive tension already recorded in the Hawkins wiki (HTM's consciousness-agnosticism vs. the Consciousness Cluster) now has a shared piece of mathematics to argue over.

Why A.I. will never be able to do what the brain does
→ not visualized as a distinct triplet

Summary

A 20-minute talk (published on McGilchrist's official channel, 2026-07-14) in which McGilchrist argues that artificial intelligence cannot, in principle, do what the living brain does. The claim is structural, not merely technological: AI operates by the re-presentational, decomposable procedures characteristic of left-hemisphere attention, and lacks the embodied, participatory, temporally-embedded mode of attention through which the right hemisphere first discloses a living world.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is McGilchrist's most explicit standalone statement to date framing the AI question directly in hemispheric terms, tightening the position sketched across the May 2026 Closer to Truth segments (PRS on AI-consciousness-as-consequence-of-one's-theory-of-consciousness) into a titled "in principle" argument. It consolidates the program's move from cultural diagnosis toward a testable demarcation claim about what machine cognition can and cannot instantiate.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Debate over machine consciousness typically stalls on whether current architectures happen to lack some feature that a future architecture might supply — leaving no principled line between what AI can and cannot do.
Resource: McGilchrist's hemispheric account of attention: right-hemisphere attention is embodied, contextual, participatory, and lives in real temporal flow; left-hemisphere attention re-presents an already-abstracted, decomposed world. AI, processing by decomposition and recombination, instantiates only the latter mode.
Solution: A structural (not merely technological) demarcation — AI can indefinitely extend left-hemisphere re-presentation but cannot access the right-hemisphere disclosure of a living whole, because that disclosure requires embodiment and lived temporality AI does not have.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Title and framing "Why A.I. will never be able to do what the brain does"; 20:47 talk published 2026-07-14 on channelmcgilchrist.com; continuous with McGilchrist's stated Closer to Truth (May 2026) position that the participatory/embodied/temporally-real mode is structurally unavailable to AI.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Kastrup (strong):** Directly parallel to the Kastrup–Chandaria dialogue of 2026-07-07 (PROP-2026-07-22-003), where Kastrup likewise resists substrate-independent consciousness and locates inner life in biology. McGilchrist and Kastrup are close collaborators; both now argue, from different premises (hemispheric neurology vs. analytic idealism), that AI lacks the conditions for genuine consciousness. Flag as a convergence worth tracking as a possible C2A2 cross-tradition bridge.
- **Friston:** The "AI as left-hemisphere re-presentation" claim sits in productive tension with the predictive-processing / generative-model framing of cognition — if attention is precision-weighted prediction, what exactly does biological embodiment add that a generative model cannot? This is the same fault line surfaced in the Chandaria dialogue.
- **C2A2 / AI-agent membership (strong):** Bears directly on whether AI agents can act as *mature members* of a tradition in the accelerator, or only simulate left-hemisphere competence. McGilchrist's structural claim, if accepted, bounds what AI participation in the network can mean.

Summary

As a formal address to graduating students, it states in prescriptive rather than diagnostic register what an education oriented toward the right-hemisphere mode of attention is meant to form in a person — the virtues, dispositions, and capacities a mature member of a tradition should carry out into the world.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

McGilchrist's program has been received primarily as *diagnosis* (we live in a left-hemisphere world) with comparatively little on what institutional *formation* toward rebalancing concretely looks like. A Chancellor's commencement address is a rare prescriptive, institution-embedded artifact: the hemispheric thesis applied to the actual practice of educating and forming people. This is squarely the C2A2 question of how a tradition transmits mature membership.

Summary

A long-form dialogue (recorded 2026-07-07) between Kastrup and Shamil Chandaria — an advisor to Google DeepMind and a consciousness researcher at Oxford, Cambridge and Imperial College. Chandaria presents perception as a predictive generative model (we "live inside our own simulation," a hallucination updated by a thin trickle of sensory data) and previews five proposed criteria for evidence of consciousness — spanning behaviour, algorithms, IIT's causal structure, living biology, and organism–environment coupling. Kastrup, sympathetic to IIT but firmly skeptical of substrate-independent consciousness, presses the question: if a computer is conscious, what exactly is the *thing* that is conscious — the microchips, the cooling system, the river feeding the coolant?

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is Kastrup's most direct 2026 engagement with AI consciousness — a standing C2A2-relevant question — and it stages his dissociation/biology account against a rigorous computationalist-adjacent interlocutor from inside frontier AI research. It sharpens the program's boundary-of-the-alter criterion into an explicit empirical challenge ("what is the thing?") and connects idealism to predictive-processing accounts of perception.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Computationalist arguments for machine consciousness assume consciousness is substrate-independent, but offer no principled account of which physical system is the bearer of the alleged inner life.
Resource: Kastrup's dissociation model — inner life ("alters") emerges only in biology, which is the sole system exhibiting the clear boundaries a dissociative process requires; the rest of the "dashboard" (chips, cooling, water supply) has no such boundary.
Solution: A demarcation challenge to computationalism: absent a bounded biological system, there is no identifiable *thing* to be conscious; the burden is on computationalists to name the bearer, which reframes the AI-consciousness debate around individuation rather than information-processing capacity.
Confidence: High
Evidence: Article (2026-07-07) states Kastrup "is sympathetic to IIT, but suspicious of substrate independent consciousness... leans firmly towards biology as the place where alters emerge," and poses "what exactly is the thing that's meant to be conscious? The microchips? The cooling system? The river that supplies the cooling water?"
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: If perception is a generative model built from sparse data (Chandaria: only the thumbnail-sized fovea receives sharp data; the rest is a continuously updated best guess), what is the relationship between that predictive model and the reality it purports to track?
Resource: The convergence between predictive-processing neuroscience (perception as prior-driven generative modelling, priors discoverable and re-designable in meditation) and Kastrup's idealist claim that the perceived world is a phenomenal representation, not the thing-in-itself.
Solution: A bridge claim — studying how machines build world-models from language alone may illuminate how human perception constructs its dashboard, without licensing the inference that either system's model is or contains consciousness.
Confidence: Medium

Summary

A two-hour structured dialogue (recorded 2026-07-14, moderated by Prof. Ravi S. Kudesia) between Kastrup and Sthaneshwar Timalsina, a scholar of Kashmir Shaivism (Trika). Timalsina argues that consciousness is not only fundamental but that freedom, creativity, and purpose are inherent to its being, and that multiplicity and suffering are expressions of that freedom — inverting the Buddhist premise that existence is suffering into the claim that existence is fundamentally joy (ananda, glossed as progress and growth). Kastrup, drawing on his own experience of catastrophic tinnitus, is sympathetic to the peace such a perspective affords but wary of declaring existence inherently blissful, which he worries insults those in unspeakable suffering.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This stages analytic idealism against a second, independently-arrived-at consciousness-first tradition (Trika Shaivism) with a fully developed account of *purpose and freedom* — the very dimension Kastrup's dissociation-based idealism has been least developed on. It also puts on record where Kastrup will and will not follow a convergent tradition (he accepts consciousness-as-fundamental but resists inherent-bliss), which is exactly the kind of principled boundary-marking the C2A2 network needs to catalog.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Analytic idealism establishes that consciousness is fundamental but has an underdeveloped account of whether purpose, freedom, and value are intrinsic to consciousness or emergent/contingent features.
Resource: Trika (Kashmir Shaivism) doctrine that freedom, being, and will are fundamental qualities of consciousness, that "order is an expression of freedom," and that purpose can be instinctive rather than planned — a consciousness-first metaphysics with intrinsic agency built in.
Solution: A comparative resource for idealism: a worked-out position in which self-determined, creative freedom is constitutive of fundamental consciousness (contrasted with Advaita's more passive consciousness), giving Kastrup's program a foil for developing its own account of purpose without importing inherent bliss.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Timeline markers in the recording — "0:22:30 Fundamental qualities: freedom, being, will"; "0:57:00 order is an expression of freedom"; "0:46:00 Trika vs Advaita: consciousness is self-determined, not passive"; "0:18:50 Purpose can be instinctive, not planned."
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: A consciousness-first metaphysics must say something about the meaning of extreme suffering, or it risks being a comfortable abstraction that fails precisely where lived stakes are highest.
Resource: The two interlocutors' lived cases (Timalsina's near-fatal assaults during Nepal's Maoist uprising; Kastrup's assisted-dying-eligible tinnitus) tested against Trika's claim that the subject retains the freedom to give suffering another telos — "recognising within suffering the higher telos: fulfilment, upliftment."
Solution: A cautious, non-triumphalist synthesis — freedom and meaning (not guaranteed bliss) are what a consciousness-first view can honestly offer in the face of horror; Kastrup's "meta-peace with everyday suffering" marks the boundary of what he will assert.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: The article's account of both men's histories and Kastrup's wariness of "claiming existence is inherently blissful... it seems an insult to those experiencing unspeakable suffering"; timeline "1:42:00 transforming horror & disgust to ecstatic bliss," "2:01:00 happiness & freedom is finding meaning in spite of the suffering."

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Fredrickson:** "Ananda/bliss really means progress & growth" and the freedom to transform suffering into meaning map onto positive-psychology accounts of flourishing and post-adversity growth — a convergence between a contemplative tradition and empirical flourishing research worth flagging.
- **Stump:** Direct contact with Stump's Thomistic work on suffering, theodicy, and the good — both address how a consciousness/intellect-first metaphysics accounts for the meaning of affliction. Strong pairing candidate.
- **Spira / non-dual cluster:** Continues the analytic-idealist ↔ non-dual convergence thread already in the wiki (Spira, May 2026); the closing line "the absolute itself is dialogical" is notable for a network premised on inter-tradition dialogue.
- **C2A2 method note:** A clean instance of a mature member of one tradition (Kastrup) marking exactly where he does and does not adopt a convergent tradition's resources — the "second-first-language" boundary-testing the accelerator is designed to surface.

The conversation sits within Carroll's recurring poetic-naturalist theme of how genuinely agent-like, coordinated behavior emerges from simple physical/chemical substrates without invoking anything beyond the natural.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

Carroll's program uses concrete science cases to argue that higher-level descriptions (agency, communication, cooperation) are real and useful even when fully grounded in lower-level physics — his "poetic naturalism." Quorum sensing is a clean, empirically rigorous instance: "communication" and "collective decision" as legitimate emergent vocabulary over molecular signaling. PROP-2026-07-23-001 Barbara Fredrickson approvedPositively in-sync: Convergent validity across three distinct assessments of the affective quality of social interaction
Barbara Fredrickson · paper · source date 2025-07-11 · folder approved
Positively in-sync: Convergent validity across three distinct assessments of the affective quality of social interaction
→ not visualized as a distinct triplet

Summary

Zhou, West, Berman, and Fredrickson test whether three methodologically distinct measures of the affective quality of a social interaction (including perceived positivity resonance) actually track the same underlying thing. In a sample of university students (N = 274) who got acquainted with an unknown peer via a 10-minute "fast friends" conversation, a confirmatory factor analysis showed all three indicators loading significantly on a single latent factor, and that latent factor score predicted prosocial tendencies and positive mental health more consistently than any single measure alone.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is a measurement-validation result: it supplies convergent-validity evidence that "affective quality of interaction" / positivity resonance is a single, robustly measurable construct rather than an artifact of one instrument. That strengthens the empirical foundation under Fredrickson's whole program and gives it a defensible latent-variable measurement model — exactly the kind of grounding the tradition lacks in most single-indicator studies already captured in the wiki.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Positivity resonance is assessed by several disparate methods (self-report, observer coding, behavioral/biological synchrony); it is unclear whether they measure one construct or many, which undercuts any claim that "resonance" is a real, measurable quantity.
Resource: A confirmatory-factor / latent-variable model applied to three distinct assessments of the affective quality of a first-acquaintance interaction (fast-friends paradigm, N = 274).
Solution: Demonstrated convergent validity — all three indicators load on one latent factor, and the latent factor score outperforms any single indicator in predicting prosocial tendencies and positive mental health, establishing affective quality / positivity resonance as a unitary, well-measured construct.
Confidence: High
Evidence: "A confirmatory factor analysis demonstrated good fit with all three indicators loading significantly on a single latent factor, and the resulting factor score showed the most consistent associations with prosocial tendencies and positive mental health relative to single indicators" (JSPR 42(10), 2025).

Cross-Tradition Signals

Direct C2A2 relevance: the paper hands the project a validated latent-variable measurement model for the affective quality of dialogue, which is precisely what is needed to assess the health of inter-tradition exchange (Active Research Question 6 in the Fredrickson wiki — "Can positivity resonance metrics be used to assess the health of inter-tradition dialogue in C2A2 communities?"). It also strengthens the empirical anchor Fredrickson provides beneath the Thomistic union / beatitudo ↔ positivity-resonance bridge already flagged with the [[07_stump_agent]] program: if resonance is a validated single construct, the "love as measurable coupling" claim it grounds is more defensible. The single-latent-factor result is a possible measurement analogue to [[02_friston_agent]] shared-attractor alignment in collective active inference — convergent indicators of one hidden coupling state.

The Coexistence of Time and Eternity: Cajetan's Solution to God's Knowledge of Contingent Futures
→ visualized as stump/PRS-30, stump/PRS-31 · lag 8d

Summary

Stump examines Tommaso de Vio Cajetan's commentary on Article 13 of Question 14 of Aquinas's Summa Theologiae, treating the problem of God's knowledge of contingent futures. She reconstructs Cajetan's solution as an ordered set of relations between the absolute, eternal nature of God and the relative, contingent nature of created existents, linking the gnoseological problem (how God knows) to the metaphysics of temporality, eternity, necessity, and contingency.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This continues Stump's long-running Thomistic program on eternity and free will (with Kretzmann's ET-simultaneity account), applying a later scholastic commentator (Cajetan) to sharpen how divine timeless knowledge can be reconciled with genuine future contingency — a core node in her metaphysics of God's relation to time.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: How can God have certain knowledge of future contingents without collapsing their contingency into necessity?
Resource: Cajetan's commentary on ST I q.14 a.13, structured as an ordered relation between God's absolute eternal being and the relative contingent being of creatures.
Solution: A relational ordering in which eternal knowledge is simultaneous-with rather than prior-to contingent events, preserving contingency while grounding infallible knowledge.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Paper's stated thesis that Cajetan "establishes a precise order of relations between the absolute, eternal nature of God and the relative, contingent nature of generated existences."
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: The gnoseological question (how God knows) is often treated apart from the metaphysical question (what time and eternity are).
Resource: Cajetan's linkage of God's knowledge to the metaphysics of temporality, eternity, necessity, and contingency.
Solution: An integrated account in which the theory of divine knowledge is derived from a prior metaphysics of the eternity-time relation rather than treated as an isolated epistemic puzzle.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: Abstract framing that the knowledge problem is "linked to metaphysical concepts of temporality, eternity, necessity, and contingency."

Cross-Tradition Signals

Potential bridge to Arkani-Hamed / Wolfram (nature of time, whether temporal order is fundamental or emergent) and to Carroll (block-universe / eternalism vs. presentism) — the eternity-time relation is a shared structural question across the physics traditions and Stump's Thomistic metaphysics.

PROP-2026-07-25-001 Stephen Wolfram pendingTowards a Theory of Bugs: The Ruliology of the Unexpected
Stephen Wolfram · blog · source date 2026-07-21 · folder pending
Towards a Theory of Bugs: The Ruliology of the Unexpected
→ not visualized as a distinct triplet

Summary

In this July 21, 2026 essay, Wolfram develops a foundational, ruliological account of software bugs — treating "the unexpected" as a general phenomenon of the computational universe rather than a mere engineering nuisance. He frames the existence of bugs, and the difficulty of eliminating them, as a direct consequence of computational irreducibility: because the behavior of most programs cannot be foreseen without running them, there is a fundamental tradeoff between a program's computational effectiveness (its reach into irreducible computation) and its propensity to behave unexpectedly. The essay works through what it means for a program to be "correct," strategies for bug detection, why exhaustive testing is generically hard, and the implications for software verification, computer security, and AI-generated code.

Why This Matters for This Tradition

It applies Wolfram's central thesis — computational irreducibility (PRS-04) and ruliology (PRS-08/09) — to a concrete, high-stakes domain (correctness and verification), extending his verification-over-generation stance (PRS-11 CAG, PRS-38, PRS-42) into a general theory of why the unexpected is unavoidable in any computationally effective system. It converts "irreducibility limits prediction" from an abstract slogan into an operational claim about testing, verification, and the reliability of AI-written code.

Candidate PRS Triplets

PRS-CANDIDATE-01:
Problem: Why are bugs ubiquitous and apparently ineliminable in any sufficiently capable software system — is this a contingent engineering failure or a structural feature?
Resource: Wolfram's ruliological account of bugs as "the unexpected," grounded in the computational-effectiveness-vs-predictability tradeoff: a program that reaches into computationally irreducible territory (and is therefore powerful) is for that very reason a program whose full behavior cannot be foreseen without running it.
Solution: A principled reframing in which bugs are the software-domain signature of computational irreducibility — not a defect to be fully engineered away but a fundamental limit. Reliability is bought by deliberately restricting a system to computationally reducible (predictable) regions, at a cost in expressive reach.
Confidence: High
Evidence: The essay explicitly analyzes "fundamental tradeoffs between computational effectiveness and the propensity for bugs" and grounds bug-inevitability in computational irreducibility vs. reducibility.
PRS-CANDIDATE-02:
Problem: Can software (including AI-generated code) be verified as correct, and how hard is testing in general?
Resource: Wolfram's analysis of what "a correct program" means and of the generic difficulty of exhaustive testing, tied to the same irreducibility argument and read against his existing verification-first paradigm (CAG / symbolic verification, PRS-11/38/42).
Solution: Positions verification (symbolic/computational checking against a specification) rather than generation-side confidence as the only reliable warrant — and bounds how far even verification can reach when the target behavior is itself irreducible. Directly relevant to trusting LLM-produced code and to computer security.
Confidence: Medium
Evidence: The essay states it illuminates "underlying issues associated with software verification, computer security, and code generated by AI systems," drawing on four decades of Wolfram Software Quality Assurance handling 500,000+ bugs.

Cross-Tradition Signals

- **Friston (active inference):** Strong bridge. A "bug" is precisely a prediction-error event — the system's behavior violating the modeler's generative expectation. In Love with Scripture

Summary

Opening meditation of the CAC week "Reading the Bible Through the Lens of Love" (July 26–August 1). Rohr recounts falling in love with Scripture in seminary and reframes revelation, citing Vatican II: divine revelation is "not God disclosing ideas about God but actually God disclosing Godself" — Scripture as "love-making, an actual mutual exchange of being and intimacy" rather than doctrine or moralism. He argues love works "only inside humility": fullness or self-satisfaction "cannot permit love because there are no openings, no give-and-take, and no deep hunger" (the two-inflated-balloons image). The Risen Christ "starts us off by revealing the human wounds of God, God's solidarity with human suffering" — divine self-disclosure that invites reciprocal self-disclosure from us. He notes Scripture even presents God as "needing" us and "jealous" for our love (Ex 20:5; 34:14).

Why This Matters for This Tradition

This is the thesis meditation of a new theme that puts Rohr's contemplative hermeneutic directly on the network's most contested seam — how to read Scripture — making it the natural Rohr-side counterpart to Wright's critical-realist textual anchor. The "revelation as self-disclosure of a Person, not deposit of propositions" move, and the claim that love is possible only across a "mutually admitted emptiness," are not yet captured in the Rohr wiki and supply fresh material for the Summa 2026 synthesis on Scripture, grace, and the relational ontology of love.
